speed:   4.1 ms/step, measured over steps 1,000–2,000 of this run
licence: ASL (non-commercial), from the label table
warn:    none
Line What it tells you header version, model and head, structure, atom count, supercell, ensemble and timestep physics dispersion, charge and spin plan the tier (graph is the CUDA-graph engine, the fastest), the backend, the force precision and the rewrites gate the gate result, or that it was not run setup the time to load, rewrite, compile, capture and gate speed the measured time per step; at the end of the run, the whole-run mean output the files written licence the model's licence warn anything you should know: a slower plan than a full install would give and why, experimental features, small cells

If the plan line does not say graph and hybrid, a warning says why and what would change it. print(run.plan) gives about 30 lines on the decisions, and run.plan.describe(full=True) all of them. See The planner.

docs.title: 7. Find the files
docs.text:
run/ holds:

File Content thermo.0.csv thermo rows: step, time, temperature, energies (and pressure for NPT) trajectory.0.traj ASE trajectory frames restart.npz the complete state at the last restart point simulation.json the inputs and planner options, for resume metadata.json the report, plan, gate and provenance (versions, model hash, GPU)

By default FastMACE writes a frame and a thermo row every 20 steps and a restart point every 10,000 steps. At each restart point a new chunk starts (thermo.1.csv, trajectory.1.traj, ...). To read a whole run in order:

from fastmace.io.output import read_frames, read_thermo

frames = read_frames("run/")
thermo = read_thermo("run/")

To continue a run: fm.Simulation.resume("run/"), then sim.run(steps=...). See Output, restart and resume.

docs.title: 8. Runs the flags cannot express
docs.text:
A temperature schedule, MC moves, an explicit integrator, a full D3 record or other output intervals go in a TOML file. fastmace init writes one with every fm.md argument, each commented with what it does:

fastmace init --model mh1 --head matpes_r2scan --structure NaCl.cif --temperature 300 --steps 20000 > run.toml
fastmace run run.toml

With the same flags, fastmace run run.toml is the same run as fastmace md. The keys are fm.md's argument names, and the records are tables at the end of the file. For example, a CSVR thermostat with sparser output:

[integrator]
type = "CSVR"
timestep_fs = 1.0
temperature_K = 300.0
tau_fs = 100.0

[output]
directory = "run/"
trajectory_every = 100
thermo_every = 20

A schedule is schedule = "anneal" (a profile: slow, fast, ultrafast or anneal) or a list of [[schedule]] segments, not both. fastmace run refuses a key that is not an fm.md argument and names it. Paths are relative to the directory you start it in.

docs.title: Rewrite screens: adopted and rejected
docs.text: SPEC §6.2 asks for this record of every screen, adopted or not, so that work is not repeated. The adopted rewrites are the registry records (fastmace/rewrites/, SPEC §6.2 catalogue). This file lists FastMACE's own screens and summarises the research engine's rejected ones.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The public API is the fastmace namespace, imported as import fastmace as fm. Importing it loads neither torch nor MACE; each name is resolved at first use.

Name Page fm.md Quick runs fm.load, fm.ForceField, fm.Workload Models and force fields fm.Simulation Simulation fm.integrators Integrators fm.optimize Optimisers fm.mc Monte Carlo fm.protocols Protocols and schedules fm.Output Output fm.D3 Dispersion fm.calc, fastmace.ase ASE front end exceptions Errors

Units follow ASE: Å, eV, eV/Å, K and amu, times in fs at the API, pressure in GPa only where a name ends in _GPa.

runtime_info()

The file-lock mode and CUDA driver-cache status of this process (a frozen record).

docs.title: calculator
docs.text:
FastMACECalculator and fm.calc: the ASE calculator, compiled tier (SPEC §7.4, §7.7 level 0).

ASE calls a calculator once per step, so this front end gets the compiled tier at most (§8.2): a compiled model, exact edge counts, no CUDA graphs. Full speed needs FastMACE to own the MD loop (fm.md, the fastmace.ase integrators). The calculator builds nothing itself: at the first calculation, and again whenever the species or the atom count change, it makes a one-off evaluation plan through the minimal planner (MinimalPlanner.plan_evaluation: compiled, with stress, no workload) and gets that plan's MACEForceField from build_evaluation. Each plan's superset is its structure's species (owner decision D3), so new species get a fresh plan; the plans share one compiled-model cache. Evaluation plans compile with a dynamic edge dimension (EngineConfig.dynamic_edges, 2-T13), so relaxations, phonopy and NEB, whose edge counts change between calls, pay one compile.

docs.title: FastMACECalculator
docs.text:
Bases: Calculator

FastMACECalculator(model, *, head=None, rewrites="auto", precision="float32", dispersion=None): energy, free_energy, forces and Voigt stress in ASE units; full 3D PBC only (§7.6).

  • model: an fm.load result or a label of the model table (a checkpoint path or URL needs fm.load or fm.calc with sha256=/trusted=, since the trust decision needs one); head selects a head of a label's checkpoint, and must match a loaded model's head;
  • rewrites: "auto" or a RewriteConfig; precision: the force precision, "float32" or "float64". Energies are accumulated in float64 (§7.3);
  • dispersion: None, "d3bj" or an fm.D3, as fm.ForceField takes it (MACE plus D3, SPEC §11.2; 3b-T04). dispersion is then the complete record. With D3 there are no per-atom energies (D3's energy is not split by atom here).

energies (per atom) is listed only for models whose energy terms are all atom-resolved; PolarMACE's k-space electrostatics are not (§7.3). Non-periodic or mixed-PBC atoms raise PlanRefused (rule 1); gas-phase molecules need MACE's MACECalculator (§4.3).

plan is the current evaluation plan (None before the first calculation) and notes what the calculator recorded, the compatibility-tier note first; the note is printed once.

docs.text:
calc(
    model: Any, *, head: str | None = None, **options: Any
) -> FastMACECalculator

atoms.calc = fm.calc("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan"): a FastMACECalculator for model (label, path or URL, loaded as fm.load does); prints the compatibility-tier note once.

docs.title: md
docs.text:
ASE MD scripts on the graph engine: fastmace.ase.Langevin, LangevinBAOAB and the phase 4 classes (SPEC §7.7 level 1).

An ASE script is ported by changing the import and adding model=. Each class takes the argument names and units of its ASE 3.27 class (SUPPORTED) and refuses the rest with the reason (REFUSED); any other argument is a TypeError naming it. The FastMACE additions are keyword-only (ADDITIONS). The shim never reinterprets an ASE argument: friction, the pressures and the time constants are in ASE units, and the conversion to the public integrator record is the only arithmetic (the record's to_config converts back, so a value may differ by one ulp).

The centre of mass (owner decision D2, conductor's answer to 4-T10): a class whose ASE original takes fixcm (Langevin, NVTBerendsen, NPTBerendsen) passes it through and follows decision 37, as fastmace.ase.Langevin does (LangevinBAOAB keeps its phase 1b mapping). A class whose ASE original has no fixcm (VelocityVerlet, Bussi, NoseHooverChainNVT, IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT) removes no centre of mass, as ASE, and counts ASE's degrees of freedom: its keyword-only dof defaults to "ase"; dof="auto" (or "fastmace") is FastMACE's convention instead, the total momentum removed and 3N - 3 counted (fixcm="auto": with FixAtoms no momentum is removed and 3(N - n_fixed) counted, 4-T04). FixAtoms runs where owner decision 44 allows it (NVE, CSVR, NVT Berendsen, Langevin; with fixcm=False for the classes that take ASE's fixcm, whose default True is refused with it); rule 1 refuses it elsewhere at the first run, with the reason.

Nothing here builds an engine: the classes build a fm.Simulation at the first run or step, which plans, runs the optional gate (owner decision D1: check="gate") and builds through the minimal planner (SPEC §5). The setup report is printed then.

run(n) advances the Simulation in chunks that end where an observer is due (ASE's attach rule: every interval steps from step 0, or once at step |interval| for interval <= 0). Before the observers of a step the committed state is written into atoms with a single-point results cache as atoms.calc; after them, changed positions or momenta changed species, masses, initial charges, positions or momenta become one event through Simulation.update (SPEC §8.5; species in the superset), and any other change raises PlanRefused with its reason. The shortest observer interval is the workload's host_callbacks_every (rule 9). trajectory= and logfile= keep their ASE meaning (one ASE Trajectory, ASE's MDLogger format) and are written from the Simulation's asynchronous snapshots; every other file goes to output.

docs.title: Langevin
docs.text:
Bases: _Dynamics

ASE 3.27's ase.md.langevin.Langevin on FastMACE's graph engine (Langevin, SPEC §10.2).

Langevin(atoms, timestep, temperature=None, friction=None, fixcm=True, *, temperature_K=None, trajectory=None, logfile=None, loginterval=1, append_trajectory=False, model=None, force_field=None, head=None, seed=None, output=None, check="skip", dispersion=None, fixcm_projection="auto"): ASE's arguments and units (timestep and 1/friction in ASE time units, temperature in eV, deprecated as in ASE); rng, a non-default comm/communicator and master are refused. The additions are those of fm.md, and fixcm_projection (fm.integrators.Langevin's; decision 37). With fixcm, "auto" resolves to the mass-weighted projection: the log then reads its frames with ASE's FixCom, so its temperature counts 3N - 3 (the trajectory frames stay unconstrained). fixcm_projection="ase" is ASE's Langevin exactly (its noise stream, 3N). FixAtoms runs with fixcm=False (ASE's default fixcm=True is refused with it, owner decision 44); the log and the trajectory frames carry the constraint, so temperatures count 3(N - n_fixed).

docs.title: LangevinBAOAB
docs.text:
Bases: _Dynamics

ASE 3.27's ase.md.langevinbaoab.LangevinBAOAB on FastMACE's graph engine (BAOAB NPT, §10.2).

LangevinBAOAB(atoms, timestep, *, temperature_K, externalstress, hydrostatic=False, T_tau=None, P_tau=None, P_mass=None, P_mass_factor=1.0, disable_cell_langevin=False, trajectory=None, logfile=None, loginterval=1, append_trajectory=False, model=None, ...), ASE units throughout: externalstress in eV/Å³ (a scalar, 3 diagonal, 6 Voigt components or a symmetric 3×3), T_tau and P_tau in ASE time. Mapped to fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB with friction_per_fs = fs / T_tau and cell_mode = "hydrostatic" if hydrostatic else "full".

Refused: no externalstress (fixed-cell BAOAB: use Langevin), no temperature_K (NVE/NPH, phase 4), an explicit P_mass (P_mass_factor scales ASE's heuristic), rng, a non-default comm/communicator and master.

ASE 3.27's ase.md.verlet.VelocityVerlet on FastMACE's graph engine (NVE, SPEC §10.2).

VelocityVerlet(atoms, timestep, trajectory=None, logfile=None, loginterval=1, *, append_trajectory=False, model=None, ..., dof="ase"): timestep in ASE time units, the momenta the structure's. Mapped to fm.integrators.NVE; dof as the module docstring says. The workload's max_temperature_K is fm.md's for NVE (quick.nve_max_temperature_K).

docs.text:
Bases: _Dynamics

ASE 3.27's ase.md.bussi.Bussi on FastMACE's graph engine (CSVR, SPEC §10.2).

Bussi(atoms, timestep, temperature_K, taut, *, trajectory=None, ..., seed=None, dof="ase"): timestep and taut in ASE time units. docs.title: NoseHooverChainNVT

docs.title: optimize
docs.text:
ASE relaxation scripts on the graph engine: fastmace.ase.LBFGS and FIRE (SPEC §7.7; decision 48).

An ASE script is ported by changing the import and adding model=. Each class takes the argument names, units and defaults of its ASE 3.27 class (SUPPORTED) and refuses the rest with the reason (REFUSED): restart other than None (a relaxation writes no restart files, conductor's choice 5), LBFGS's use_line_search=True, FIRE's deprecated maxmove and position_reset_callback, and a non-default comm/master. The FastMACE additions are keyword-only (ADDITIONS).

atoms is an Atoms (fixed cell) or ase.filters.FrechetCellFilter(atoms, ...) (variable cell, read into fm.optimize.FrechetCell); every other filter (UnitCellFilter, ExpCellFilter, StrainFilter, ...) is refused with the reason (decision 48).

Nothing here builds an engine: the classes build a fm.Simulation(optimizer=...) at the first run, irun or step, and run(fmax, steps) is Simulation.relax in chunks that end where an observer or a trajectory frame is due (ASE's attach rule). logfile is ASE's optimiser log (ASE's Log, "-" by default as ASE's), one line per step from the relaxation's per-step energies and max forces; trajectory= is one ASE Trajectory with a frame every loginterval steps. Before the observers of a step the relaxed state is written into atoms (positions and cell) with a single-point results cache as atoms.calc. An observer that changes atoms raises: the optimiser's history would no longer describe the structure (conductor's answer to 4-T10).

Refused: the deprecated maxmove (use maxstep) and position_reset_callback (decision 48).

docs.title: D3 dataclass
docs.text:
A complete D3 dispersion correction.

  • functional: the parameter set, e.g. "r2scan" (MH-1 matpes_r2scan) or "pbe";
  • damping: Becke–Johnson;
  • pair_cutoff_bohr, cn_cutoff_bohr: 40 bohr each (mace_mp and torch-dftd);
  • three_body: the ATM term, off (ForceField refuses it on: no D3 term implements it);
  • smoothing: cutoff smoothing, none;
  • precision: the precision of the CN, energy and virial reductions, float64 only. The pair terms run in the plan's force precision (conductor's choice 3, docs/design/d3.md);
  • autoang, autoev: torch-dftd's unit constants (they differ from ASE's Bohr and Hartree by about 1e-7 relative), recorded with the parameters;
  • s6, s8, a1, a2: the Becke–Johnson numbers. Left out (all four), they are the functional's set in BJ_PARAMETERS; given (all four), they are used as given and functional only names them. Either way the record holds the numbers, so equal records are equal corrections.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Every FastMACE error derives from FastMACEError.

docs.title: errors
docs.text:
FastMACE exceptions (SPEC §7.6 "Exceptions") and their message shape (§7.7 "Errors").

Every exception FastMACE raises derives from FastMACEError. Its message has one shape, so that no traceback needs reading: what happened; why, in one or two sentences; what to do next; where the record is (run.plan, run.gate, metadata.json); and fastmace doctor for environment problems. The CLI prints this message alone (§7.5).

This module imports nothing heavy: import fastmace imports neither torch nor MACE, and the 1a modules that defined these classes re-export them.

docs.title: FastMACEError
docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Base class of every error FastMACE raises.

FastMACEError(what, why=None, next_step=None, record=None, environment=None); a plain one-argument construction gives just what. Each class may set a default next step, record location and environment flag; None takes the class default.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text:
Bases: str

One refusal reason: the text, the §9.3 hard rule (None for a run request) and a stable code.

Reports and tests match code, never the text. Decisions use the same record. Plan task 5-T01's contract (fastmace.planner.rules): rule is None or one of 1-15; with a rule, code is one of that rule's codes (or rules.OVERRIDE_CODE for an overridden preference), and a rule's code never comes without its number. rules.check_reason says what is wrong; the conformance suite calls it (tests/cpu/test_rules_meta.py), the planner does not, so a reason costs nothing at run time.

docs.title: PlanRefused
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, ValueError

The planner cannot plan this workload, or a run request the plan does not cover.

reasons lists every hard-constraint reason of the refusal at once (SPEC §9.3): plain strings (1a) or Reason records. Raise through PlanRefused.from_reasons, which picks SpeciesNotInSuperset when rule 2 is among them.

docs.title: codes property
docs.text:
codes

The stable code of each reason (None for a plain-string reason).

docs.title: rules property
docs.text:
rules

The §9.3 rule of each reason (None where none applies).

docs.title: from_reasons classmethod
docs.text:
from_reasons(reasons, **parts)

One exception carrying every reason: SpeciesNotInSuperset if a reason has rule == 2.

docs.title: SpeciesNotInSuperset
docs.text:
Bases: PlanRefused

Rule 2: a species outside the ForceField's declared superset (SPEC §8.5), with every reason.

docs.title: ChargeParityRefused
docs.text:
Bases: PlanRefused

A transmutable set violates the charge and spin rule of SPEC §10.4: a move needs ΔZ − Δq even.

Raised by the planner through ChargeParityRefused.from_reasons with a reason coded CHARGE_PARITY_CODE (3-T09); every other reason of the refusal comes with it.

docs.title: ProcessConstraintError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, RuntimeError

An engine would break a process-wide constraint (SPEC §8.7).

docs.title: InputError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, ValueError

The run's input cannot start: no plan or fallback candidate changes that, so it is raised at once.

docs.title: FallbackExhausted
docs.text:
Bases: PlanRefused

No fallback candidate passed validation (SPEC §9.4 step 5); revisions holds every tried plan.

revisions is the revision chain of the fallback, oldest first: the failed plan, then each candidate tried, each with its reason. reasons are the refusal's, as for PlanRefused.

docs.title: SubprocessRunnerError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, RuntimeError

The subprocess runner's child failed, was killed or stalled (SPEC §8.7); never a hang.

exit_code is the child's (negative: killed by that signal; None: still running when it was stopped), child_message its error message, and directory the hand-off directory, kept after an error.

docs.title: TemplateChangedError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, RuntimeError

A cached converted model (opt-1 OPT-T06) changed after it was stored; it is never copied for a plan.

docs.title: IsolationError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError, RuntimeError

An instance whose lease on a shared component was taken by another instance (SPEC §8.7).

component names the shared component, holder the instance that holds its lease now.

docs.title: ReproducibilityError
docs.text:
Bases: FastMACEError

A (backend, model family) failed qualification for reproducible=True (SPEC §9.3 rule 5).

blocking names the kernels or operators without a deterministic implementation. A plan that asks for reproducible=True without a qualified family is refused by PlanRefused (rule 5), not by this error.

docs.title: GateFailed

The gate on the user's structure failed (SPEC §12.3); gate_record holds the comparison.

docs.title: CheckpointTrustError

docs.title: NonFiniteError

docs.title: CellDivergedError

docs.title: integrators
docs.text:
Graph-capturable MD integrators over SimulationState and a ForceField (SPEC §10).

This package's namespace is fm.integrators: the public integrator records (plan task 1b-T01), which a Simulation takes as integrator= and which map onto IntegratorConfig. The implementations (langevin.py, baoab.py) are built from that config by the planner only (SPEC §5); importing this package imports neither them nor torch.

Units at the API (SPEC §7.3): fs, K, GPa and friction per fs. IntegratorConfig.friction is in inverse ASE time units, as in main.py; to_config converts (friction_per_fs / units.fs).

Phase 4 (plan task 4-T01, conductor's choice 1) adds the records of the new schemes: NVE, CSVR, NoseHooverChain, MTK and Berendsen. Their scheme settings travel in IntegratorConfig.parameters in the record's units (fs, K, GPa); the implementations (4-T02, 4-T03) convert. Time constants have no defaults, as in ASE: physics is never chosen silently. A record whose scheme is not registered yet plans to a scheme-unknown refusal (rule 1).

fixcm of the schemes that take FixAtoms (Langevin, NVE, CSVR, Berendsen; plan task 4-T04) defaults to "auto": off when the structure has fixed atoms, which pin the frame already, on otherwise. to_config resolves it from fixed_atoms (the Simulation passes whether its Atoms carry FixAtoms); an explicit fixcm=True with fixed atoms is refused by rule 1 (owner decision 44).

docs.title: Langevin dataclass
docs.text:
Langevin NVT, ASE's Langevin on the graph engine (SPEC §10.2).

fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=0.5, temperature_K=300, friction_per_fs=0.002) (about fm.md's friction, quick.default_friction_per_fs). temperature_K is the starting target; a schedule (Simulation.run(schedule=…)) moves it. fixcm_projection is how fixcm projects the noise (IntegratorConfig.fixcm_projection; docs/design/fixcm-projection.md): "ase", ASE's, "mass_weighted", canonical at a fixed centre of mass for unequal masses too, or "auto", the planner's choice ("mass_weighted" under fixcm, for MD as for MC (decision 37), else "ase"). fixcm: "auto" (off with FixAtoms, on otherwise), True or False.

docs.title: to_config
docs.text:
to_config(
    *, seed: int, fixed_atoms: bool = False
) -> IntegratorConfig

The IntegratorConfig of this record with seed (the Simulation's); fixed_atoms: whether the structure has FixAtoms (fixcm="auto").

docs.title: LangevinBAOAB dataclass
docs.text:
Langevin-Hoover NPT, ASE 3.27's LangevinBAOAB on the graph engine (SPEC §10.2).

  • friction_per_fs: the thermostat friction; ASE's T_tau is 1 / friction, as in main.py (workflow.baoab_settings);
  • pressure_GPa or external_stress_GPa (ASE's externalstress sign: a scalar or six Voigt components), not both;
  • cell_mode: "hydrostatic" (ASE hydrostatic=True) or "full";
  • barostat_tau_fs: ASE's P_tau, None = ASE's default 20 T_tau;
  • barostat_mass_factor: ASE's P_mass_factor;
  • disable_cell_langevin: as ASE;
  • max_volume_ratio and max_cell_length_A: the cell-divergence stop (3b-T07). A Simulation stops with CellDivergedError (restart and metadata written first) once the volume leaves [V0 / ratio, V0 ratio], V0 the run's starting volume, or a cell vector is longer than max_cell_length_A (1000 Å: float32 coordinates still resolve 6e-5 Å there). A vapour at a low pressure expands without bound otherwise, until the coordinates lose their precision. None turns a limit off;
  • fixcm: False only. BAOAB, as ASE's, never removes the total momentum, so the record does not claim a fixed centre of mass (MC velocity treatments and refusals follow it).

The production drag term is the corrected one (SPEC §12.1, 1b-T09); ASE's own variant stays an IntegratorConfig option for comparisons with ASE.

docs.title: to_config
docs.text:
to_config(
    *, seed: int, fixed_atoms: bool = False
) -> IntegratorConfig

The IntegratorConfig of this record with seed (the Simulation's). fixed_atoms is accepted as by every record; rule 1 refuses FixAtoms with a variable cell.

docs.title: NVE dataclass
docs.text:
Velocity Verlet, ASE's VelocityVerlet on the graph engine (SPEC §10.2; 4-T02).

fixcm: remove the total momentum at the start and project it out each step (owner decision D2); "auto" turns it off with FixAtoms. dof: "auto" (3N - 3 under fixcm, 3(N - n_fixed) with FixAtoms; the same as "fastmace") or "ase" (ASE's count), for the reported temperature. The conserved quantity is E_kin + E_pot.

docs.title: to_config
docs.text:
to_config(
    *, seed: int, fixed_atoms: bool = False

The IntegratorConfig of this record with seed (the Simulation's).

docs.title: CSVR dataclass
docs.text:

tau_fs is ASE's taut. The noise is ASE's stream from the Simulation's seed (conductor's choice 3). The conserved quantity adds the energy the thermostat transferred, as ASE's Bussi.

docs.title: Berendsen dataclass
docs.text:
Berendsen thermostat and barostat: ASE 3.27's NVTBerendsen (no pressure), NPTBerendsen (pressure_GPa) and Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen (pressure_GPa and mask) on the graph engine (4-T02). Non-canonical: equilibration only; the plan warns.

taut_fs, taup_fs and compressibility_per_GPa as ASE's taut, taup and compressibility_au in fs and 1/GPa; mask: three 0/1 flags of the scaled cell directions, ASE's mask. A pressure needs taup_fs and compressibility_per_GPa.

docs.text:

    *, seed: int, fixed_atoms: bool = False

The IntegratorConfig of this record with seed (the Simulation's); FixAtoms runs with NVT only (rule 1).

docs.title: moves
docs.text:
MC move records and their attempts (SPEC §10.4; contracts: plan task 3-T01).

Swap, Transmute and Displace are frozen records a user builds before any model is loaded, so this module imports neither torch nor MACE nor ASE. They are checked against the workload and the superset by Simulation.run(mc=...) (§7.6). Species stay as given (symbols or atomic numbers); the driver maps them to atomic numbers. build_attempt builds the captured attempt of a move: 3-T09 (swaps, transmutations), 3-T10 (displacements, fastmace.mc.displace).

docs.title: Swap dataclass
docs.text: Swap the species of two atoms (§10.4): a pair type uniformly from pairs, then one atom of each species uniformly. every MD steps, then attempts attempts. velocities: exchange (default; the atoms swap velocities), rescale, redraw or redraw_all.

docs.title: Transmute dataclass
docs.text:
Change one atom's species within the transmutable set species (§10.4, semi-grand canonical).

velocities: rescale, redraw or redraw_all; None takes the default (rescale, or redraw_all when the integrator fixes the centre of mass). mu: configurational chemical potential differences in eV against a reference species (configurational_mu converts full ones); absent species have 0. formal_charges: q_s per species (0 if absent), for the parity rule ΔZ − Δq even (§10.4 "Charge and spin"). Both are stored as sorted pairs.

docs.title: Displace dataclass
docs.text: Displace one atom uniformly within a sphere of radius delta_A (§10.4). adaptive=True retunes δ after every block while it is set (toward 30 % acceptance, at most delta_A), and each value is recorded; a fixed δ keeps the chain's detailed balance, so sample with adaptive=False.

docs.title: configurational_mu
docs.text:
configurational_mu(
    mu_full: Mapping[Any, float],
    temperature_K: float,
    reference: Any,
    masses: Mapping[Any, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[Any, float]

Configurational chemical-potential differences from full ones (§10.4): Δμ_s^conf = Δμ_s^full + (3/2) k_B T ln(m_s / m_ref).

mu_full maps species to Δμ_s^full in eV relative to reference (whose own entry, if given, must be 0). masses in amu, by species; None takes ASE's standard atomic masses. The result has the keys of mu_full, for fm.mc.Transmute(mu=...).

docs.title: Models and force fields
docs.text: fm.load is fastmace.model.loading.load_pristine.

docs.title: load_pristine
docs.text:
load_pristine(
    source,
    head=None,
    *,
    sha256=None,
    trusted=False,
    download=False,
    charge=None,
    spin_multiplicity=None,
    checkpoint=None,
    environ=None,
)

fm.load (SPEC §7.1): the checkpoint as a pristine model, e3nn in float64 on the CPU.

source is a label ("mh1-r2scan"), an alias with head= ("mh1"), a path or a URL. A multi-head checkpoint needs head= or a label that names one; otherwise ValueError lists its heads. A path or URL is unpickled only with a matching sha256= or trusted=True; a label's file must match the table (SPEC §7.6). download=True fetches a missing file into the models cache and checks it before it is kept. The trust decision and the hash are in provenance(). The plan converts the model to its backend and precision; the pristine model itself is never changed (fm.ForceField). Before MACE is imported, the OEq runtime is prepared where the hybrid is possible (prepare_hybrid_if_possible; the outcome is oeq_runtime). The expandable-segments allocator is configured first (configure_allocator, a no-op if PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF is set): preparing the hybrid can touch CUDA, and the allocator reads the variable only once (5-T07).

docs.title: ForceField
docs.text:
ForceField(model, atoms=None, *, precision="float32", rewrites="auto", species=None).

  • model: an fm.load result (a LoadedModel, normally the pristine e3nn float64 CPU model) or a label, which is loaded with fm.load. A path needs fm.load first, because the trust decision needs one (§7.6);
  • atoms: optional; its species are the default superset (§7.1 passes it). Without it the superset is the species of the first structure the force field is used with;
  • precision: the force precision, "float32" or "float64" (§7.3);
  • rewrites: "auto" or a RewriteConfig; resolved per plan;
  • species: the declared superset (§8.5), symbols or atomic numbers, compared as a set; a species without an embedding raises ModelElementError. It may be larger than the structure's species (phase 3, rule 8): every species-indexed table is built for it, so an atom can become any superset species in place (3-T02);
  • dispersion: None, "d3bj" or an fm.D3 (SPEC §7.7, §11.2). "d3bj" expands from the model's training functional (fastmace.longrange.d3.expand: ValueError when it is unknown or already contains dispersion); an explicit record whose functional differs from the training one is kept with a warning in dispersion_warnings. The complete record is dispersion and part of the identity. Refused (PlanRefused): the ATM term (d3-three-body) and PolarMACE (d3-polar, decision 41). Plans carry the record and put the D3 term into their force field (fastmace.model.dispersed, 3b-T04).

On CUDA with cuEq or hybrid, a later plan of the same conversion gets a private copy of the first plan's converted model instead (fastmace.model.templates; opt-1 OPT-T06), unless EngineConfig.model_template_cache is False.

docs.title: Workload dataclass
docs.text:
What the run will do (SPEC §9.2). Only max_temperature_K is required.

  • max_temperature_K: the highest thermostat target of the run, K; sizes the skin and the bucket headroom of MC and species-change workloads (rule 11; plain MD keeps the 0.3 Å skin). Simulation.run refuses a schedule above it (§7.6);
  • species_changes: swaps, transmutations or species events (§8.5);
  • atom_count_changes: reserved; the planner refuses it in 1.0 (§9.3 rule 7, §8.6);
  • min_mc_temperature_K: the lowest MC target temperature, K; the ΔE gate threshold 0.01 k_B T_min (§12.3). Required when mc_moves is non-empty, and positive;
  • host_callbacks_every: user Python every n steps (rule 9); None = no callbacks;
  • needs_per_atom: per-atom outputs the run needs ("energies", "charges", ...);
  • mc_moves: declared move types ("swap", "transmute", "displace");
  • reproducible: bitwise within the scope of §9.3; the planner refuses what it cannot guarantee. Qualified (2-T16, planner.reproducible): plain cuEq with the unfused convolution, the MH-1 architecture and the pinned cuequivariance_ops version;
  • mc_energy_precision: §10.4; "auto" = the force precision if the ΔE gate passes;
  • max_displacement_A: the largest displacement δ, Å, any Displace move of the run may use (adaptive δ included). Required when "displace" is in mc_moves; rule 11 adds 2δ to the skin (§10.4), and attaching a Displace with a larger delta_A is refused.

docs.title: optimize
docs.text:
GPU structure relaxations, fixed and variable cell (SPEC §10.3).

This package's namespace is fm.optimize: the public optimiser records (plan task 4-T01, conductor's choice 1), which a Simulation takes as optimizer= (4-T05) and which map onto OptimizerConfig. The implementations (lbfgs.py, 4-T05; fire.py, 4-T06; cell.py, 4-T07) are built by the planner only, over a base.DOFView (SPEC §5); importing this package imports neither them nor torch.

The optimisers take ASE 3.27's arguments and defaults; lengths are Angstrom. FIRE's dt and dtmax are in ASE time units, as ASE's (they are step-size parameters, not physical times). FrechetCell is ASE's FrechetCellFilter with the pressure in GPa.

docs.title: LBFGS dataclass
docs.text: ASE 3.27's LBFGS on the graph engine (4-T05): maxstep_A (ASE maxstep), memory, damping and alpha with ASE's defaults. use_line_search is not offered (refused in the fastmace.ase class). cell_filter: None (fixed cell) or FrechetCell(...).

The OptimizerConfig with ASE's run(fmax=, steps=).

docs.text: ASE 3.27's FIRE on the graph engine (4-T06), with ASE's arguments and defaults: dt and dtmax in ASE time units, maxstep_A (ASE maxstep), Nmin, finc, fdec, astart, fa, a and downhill_check. ASE's deprecated maxmove and position_reset_callback are not offered. cell_filter: None or FrechetCell(...).

docs.text:

    *, fmax: float = 0.05, steps: int = 100000000

The OptimizerConfig with ASE's run(fmax=, steps=).

docs.text:
ASE 3.27's FrechetCellFilter on the device (4-T07): positions and the log of the deformation gradient, both optimisers unchanged on it.

scalar_pressure_GPa is ASE's scalar_pressure in GPa; hydrostatic_strain, constant_volume, mask (six Voigt flags or a 3x3 of flags, as ASE) and exp_cell_factor (None: N, ASE's default) as ASE's.

docs.title: output
docs.text:
Output: where a Simulation writes and how often, and the chunked writer (SPEC §7.2, §10.6).

Output is the record (plan task 1b-T01). ChunkedOutput (plan task 1b-T06) writes the thermo rows and trajectory frames of a run as chunks, thermo.<n>.csv and trajectory.<n>.traj for n = 0, 1, ..., with a chunk boundary exactly at every restart point (SPEC §10.6 "Output files at restart points"):

  • restart_point() closes the current chunks, fsyncs them and their directory (plan task 2-T10; rows and frames in between are flushed, not fsynced) and opens the next pair; it returns the indices the restart file stores (io.restart.OUTPUT_KEYS): output_chunk, the last closed chunk, and output_rows and output_frames, the rows and frames in chunks 0 to output_chunk. Call it after draining the output queue (AsyncOutput.restart_point does both), then write the restart file. Every restart write is a chunk boundary, a stop request's included.
  • Resume (resume_from= those indices) checks the chunks up to output_chunk (present, with the stored numbers of rows and frames) and that every later chunk can be deleted, before it touches anything; otherwise it raises RestartMismatch. Then it deletes the later chunks and opens chunk output_chunk + 1. Nothing is ever rewritten: the research engine's resume reread and rewrote md.traj (workflow.truncate_outputs, up to 770 MB on the NAS).

Rows and frames written after the last restart point (by the asynchronous writer, or before a crash) are thus in later chunks only. A crash between restart_point and the restart write leaves the older restart file, and resume from it deletes the newer chunks as well.

Every chunk is complete on its own: each thermo chunk starts with the header, and a chunk without rows or frames still has both files (an empty trajectory reads as no frames). read_thermo and read_frames concatenate the chunks in order; ase.io.read(path, index=":") reads one. This module imports neither torch nor ASE at import time (fm.Output is a light name).

docs.title: Output dataclass
docs.text:
Output directory and cadences, in MD steps (defaults: the production settings of §7.7).

trajectory_every and restart_every may be None (no trajectory, no restart files); thermo rows are always written. directory is kept as given, as a string.

docs.title: schedule
docs.text:
Temperature schedules: ramps and holds, whole steps, the target per step (SPEC §7.2, §7.6 "Schedules").

A Schedule is timestep-free: segments in ps. Schedule.resolve(timestep_fs) rounds each segment to whole steps (half up) and records the boundaries, the total and the rounded durations and rates. The target is piecewise linear in the step. Step n of a segment uses the target at the step's end point, as the research engine does ("update the target every timestep using that step's endpoint", docs/protocol.md), so the target changes every step on a ramp and never on a hold. It reaches the integrator through Integrator.set_temperature before the step (TargetFill), never as an event.

Each ramp interpolates from its colder end, T_low + (T_high - T_low) * w. This reproduces the research engine's float expressions bit for bit: peak * n / H when heating from 0 K and final + (peak - final) * (H + C - n) / C when cooling.

ScheduleState is the schedule position: the restart record of SimulationState.protocol.

docs.title: profiles
docs.text:
Run profiles as data (SPEC §10.5): today's slow, fast, ultrafast and anneal.

The research engine's workflow.PROFILES: the schedule, the output intervals, the initial relaxation and, for anneal, the quench settings (docs/assets/Simulated_Annealing.txt). The relaxation and quench settings are data only here; nothing in this module runs them.

Profiles from files: TOML (tomllib, tomli before Python 3.11) or YAML (PyYAML's safe_load only, imported when needed).

docs.title: Profile dataclass
docs.text:
A named schedule with its output intervals, initial relaxation and quench settings.

relax_fmax 0 means no initial relaxation (fixed cell, eV/Å). quench is None or a mapping with QUENCH_KEYS (frames per bin_K bin of the target from min_K, quenched to fmax with optimizer, at most max_steps). Optimizer names are resolved (resolve_optimizer). Relaxation and quench keep the cell fixed; after NPT each frame is quenched at its own cell.

ensemble is "NVT" or "NPT" (fm.md's; any case). pressure_GPa is NPT's constant hydrostatic target, None for NVT and 0 GPa by default for NPT; pressure schedules are refused until the pressure setter (plan task 3b-T05). dispersion is "none" or "d3bj" (fm.md's, SPEC §7.7).

docs.title: md
docs.text:
md(
    structure: Any,
    *,
    model: Any,
    head: str | None = None,
    charge: int | None = None,
    spin_multiplicity: int | None = None,
    sha256: str | None = None,
    trusted: bool = False,
    ensemble: str = "NVT",
    temperature_K: float | None = None,
    schedule: Any = None,
    pressure_GPa: float = 0.0,
    cell_mode: str = "hydrostatic",
    timestep_fs: float = 0.5,
    steps: int | None = None,
    mc: Any = None,
    min_mc_temperature_K: float | None = None,
    dispersion: Any = None,
    repeat: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1),
    output: Any = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
    initial_velocities: Any = "keep",
    check: str = "skip",
    integrator: Any = None,
    mode: str | None = None,
    allow_reference: bool = False,
    fallback: Any = None,
    gate: Any = None,
    runner: Any = None,
    engine: Any = None,
    neighbours: Any = None,
    calibrate: bool = False,
) -> RunResult

Run MD on structure (path or Atoms) with model and return a RunResult.

Arguments as SPEC §7.7 level 2:

  • model: a label, path or URL, with head, charge, spin_multiplicity and sha256/trusted as fm.load; or an fm.load result (then without those);
  • ensemble: "NVT" (Langevin), "NPT" (BAOAB with pressure_GPa and cell_mode) or "NVE" (velocity Verlet from the structure's momenta, no temperature_K). integrator= chooses any fm.integrators record explicitly;
  • temperature_K or schedule (an fm.protocols schedule); steps (optional with a schedule: the whole schedule);
  • mc and min_mc_temperature_K: one fm.mc record or a sequence of them, checked as §7.7 says, attached where the target is at or above min_mc_temperature_K;
  • dispersion: None, "d3bj" or an fm.D3: the complete record goes into the force field (MACE plus D3, SPEC §11.2) and is shown in the report; a functional other than the training one is a report warning;
  • repeat: the supercell, (1, 1, 1) by default (never expanded silently);
  • output: a directory or an fm.Output; default ./<structure stem>.fastmace/, or ./fastmace-run/ for an Atoms;
  • seed: the noise seed; None draws one, recorded in metadata.json;
  • initial_velocities: what a structure at rest (zero kinetic energy) starts with. "keep" (default): its momenta as they are, so it starts at rest (as ASE; CSVR refuses that). "maxwell_boltzmann": seeded Maxwell-Boltzmann momenta at the run's starting target (temperature_K, the integrator's, or the schedule's first); refused when that is 0 K and for NVE. A temperature in K (a float above 0): Maxwell-Boltzmann momenta at it, also for NVE and for a schedule that starts at 0 K. The draw uses seed (its own stream, not the thermostat's), is not made when the structure already moves (its momenta are kept), and either way the report and metadata.json's warnings say what happened. Opt-in;
  • check: as Simulation (the gate is opt-in, check="gate");
  • mode, allow_reference, fallback, gate, runner, engine, neighbours: the planner inputs, passed to Simulation as they are (simulation.PlannerOptions);
  • calibrate: True measures the backends the rules rank equal (hybrid against plain cuEq) on this structure before the run and takes plain cuEq only if it is faster by more than 5 % in every pair (SPEC §9.1, decision 55; CalibrationConfig, planner.calibrate). Off by default: it costs four child builds. Refused with MC moves.

Every ValueError and refusal comes before the model is loaded.

docs.title: RunResult dataclass
docs.text:
What fm.md returns: the report and the expert objects it built.

  • summary: the one-screen report (§7.7, 1b-T15), simulation.report.text() after the run;
  • plan, gate: the Plan and gate records (§9.5, §12.3);
  • simulation: the Simulation, for restarts and the expert API; its output is flushed and it can run on (simulation.run);
  • metadata: the dict written to metadata.json (§13);
  • output: the output directory.

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
MD on the graph engine with a plan, an optional gate, schedules and complete restarts.

Simulation(atoms, force_field, *, species=None, integrator, workload=None, output=None, seed, check="skip", allow_naive_cueq=False, mode=None, allow_reference=False, fallback=None, gate=None, runner=None, engine=None, neighbours=None, adaptation=None, calibration=None):

  • atoms: ASE Atoms, full 3D PBC (§4.4); copied, the caller's object is never changed;
  • force_field: a fm.ForceField, an fm.load result or a label; a model is wrapped in a float32 ForceField with species= (default: the structure's species). A path raises TypeError (load it with fm.load, the trust decision needs one); species with a ForceField raises ValueError (the ForceField owns the superset);
  • integrator: an fm.integrators record (fm.integrators.RECORDS); a scheme not registered yet is refused by the plan (rule 1);
  • workload: fm.Workload; default Workload(max_temperature_K=integrator.temperature_K);
  • output: fm.Output; thermo rows, trajectory frames and metadata.json go to its directory, in chunks (§10.6). None writes no file;
  • seed: the integrator's noise seed, recorded;
  • check: one of CHECK_MODES;
  • allow_naive_cueq: accept cuEquivariance's naive kernels (§9.2), recorded;
  • the planner inputs (PlannerOptions, recorded in simulation.json): mode (§9.3; None lets the planner choose), allow_reference (rule 1), fallback (FallbackConfig, §9.4), gate (GateConfig, §12.3 "Resources"; the record is sim.gate_config, the result sim.gate), runner (RunnerConfig, §8.7), engine (EngineConfig) and neighbours (NeighbourConfig), adaptation (AdaptationConfig, §9.6) and calibration (CalibrationConfig, §9.1; both phase 5, plan task 5-T01). None takes the defaults, and for engine and neighbours the default planner's.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
run(
    steps: int | None = None,
    schedule: Any = None,
    mc: Any = ...,
) -> None

Advance steps steps, or along schedule to its end (§7.2 "Schedules and step counts").

schedule=None continues the attached schedule, or keeps the target without one. mc=... (the default) keeps the attached move set, mc=None detaches it, a move set attaches it in place of any attached one (§7.6): one fm.mc record (Swap, Transmute, Displace) or a sequence of them. Every check runs before the first step: a schedule above Workload.max_temperature_K raises PlanRefused, steps beyond the schedule ValueError, and the move set that will be attached (given or kept) is checked against the workload over every step of this call (PlanRefused; SpeciesNotInSuperset for a species outside the superset).

docs.title: switch_tier
docs.text:
switch_tier(request)

The tier switch of SPEC §9.6 at the committed step, for request (a planner.adapt.SwitchRequest): the compiled revision, built from the pristine model, validated, then given the committed state. A candidate that fails leaves the run on its revision, with a warning (adapt.SWITCH_FAILED_CODE); returns whether the switch was made. Not inside an MC block, nor from an uncommitted step.

docs.title: add_metadata_block
docs.text:
add_metadata_block(name: str, provider: Any) -> None

Add {name: provider()} to every metadata.json record this Simulation builds, evaluated at each write: the fastmace.ase classes' "ase" block (4-T10), in the run's own durable write instead of a second one per run(). name must not be a key of the record itself.

docs.title: relax
docs.text:
relax(
    *, fmax: float = 0.05, steps: int = 100000000
) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, Any]]

Relax with the optimiser (SPEC §10.3; 4-T05): ASE's Optimizer.run(fmax=, steps=) on the engine.

A converged start takes no step; otherwise one step at a time until the largest constraint-adjusted force is below fmax (eV/Angstrom) or steps steps are done, one force call per step. A second call continues with the optimiser's history, as a second run of one ASE optimiser does. Returns the relaxed Atoms (a copy of the structure at the committed positions and cell, no calculator) and the summary of fastmace.optimize.driver.relax: steps, converged, seconds, initial and final energies per atom, fmax, the per-step energies and max forces, and the engine's neighbour rebuilds and re-captures.

docs.title: save_restart
docs.text:
save_restart(path: Any) -> None

Write the complete §10.6 state at the current committed step, a canonical restart point.

path is <directory>/restart.npz (or the directory): Simulation.resume(directory) reads it there. The output queue is drained and the output chunks end here (§10.6), the engine is canonicalised and written by io.restart.write_engine_restart (T05's format), and simulation.json next to it holds what that format does not: the model source, the integrator record, workload, Output, seed, allow_naive_cueq, the planner options, species, masses and PBC. A plan that runs in a child copies the child's last hand-off, a canonical restart point at the committed step (2-T07).

Only at a committed step: refused (RuntimeError) inside an MC block and while the engine holds an uncommitted (overflowed) step, before anything is written (§10.6, 3-T08).

docs.title: resume classmethod
docs.text:
resume(
    directory: Any,
    *,
    allow_plan_change: bool = False,
    check: Check = "skip",
) -> Simulation

Continue from the restart in directory. A different force-field identity raises RestartMismatch, except that another MACE or FastMACE version alone warns and is recorded as a plan revision and in the report (owner decision 23); a different plan needs allow_plan_change=True and makes a new revision (§9.5, §10.6). check as in the constructor.

The model is loaded again from simulation.json's file, checked against its SHA-256; the engine is built at the restart's positions, cell and composition (species and masses at the restart step, not the initial structure's; 3-T08) through the planner, then takes the restart's state, edge bucket and neighbour capacity (io.restart.resume_engine). Output chunks after the restart point are deleted and new ones opened; nothing is rewritten.

docs.title: set_positions
docs.text:
set_positions(positions: Any) -> None

Host write of positions at a canonical point: quiesce, write, rebuild, re-evaluate (owner decision D4). positions in Å, shape (N, 3); the momenta stay.

docs.title: set_momenta
docs.text:
set_momenta(momenta: Any) -> None

Host write of momenta at a canonical point (owner decision D4). momenta in ASE units, shape (N, 3); the engine integrates velocities, momenta / masses.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
update(
    *,
    species: Any = None,
    masses: Any = None,
    charges: Any = None,
    total_charge: Any = None,
    friction_per_fs: Any = None,
    positions: Any = None,
    momenta: Any = None,
    cell: Any = None,
) -> None

Any combination of host changes as one transaction with one force evaluation (SPEC §8.5, §7.7).

  • species: atomic numbers or symbols, (N,); in the ForceField's superset (SpeciesNotInSuperset). Masses follow the new species' standard masses unless masses is given too;
  • masses: amu, (N,); the momenta stay (ASE), so the velocities change;
  • charges: per-atom charges, (N,), and total_charge, for models that take them;
  • friction_per_fs: the Langevin friction in 1/fs (the record's unit); it drops the captured graphs, which bake it in (a recorded re-capture), and with the default barostat τ moves P_tau and the barostat mass with it;
  • positions (Å) and momenta (ASE units), (N, 3); momenta use the new masses;
  • cell (Å, (3, 3), rows the lattice vectors), fixed-cell runs only (4-T05; 4-T09 relaxes quench frames with their own NPT cells on one engine): the positions are not scaled, so give them too. The lists and cell inputs change in place, so the captured graphs stay unless the rebuild grows a capacity or the edge count needs a new padded size.

Everything is validated before anything is written. The changes apply in this order: species, masses, charges, friction, cell, positions, momenta; then a canonical point (neighbour list rebuilt at the committed positions, forces and stress evaluated once, integrator.start), as a host write of positions (owner decision D4). Nothing given: nothing happens.

docs.title: set_species
docs.text:
set_species(species: Any) -> None

Set every atom's species (atomic numbers or symbols, shape (N,)), one event. Each must be in the ForceField's superset (SpeciesNotInSuperset); masses follow the new species' standard masses unless set_masses follows.

docs.title: set_masses
docs.text:
set_masses(masses: Any) -> None

Set every atom's mass in amu, shape (N,), one event; the momenta stay (ASE), so the velocities change: v' = v m_old / m_new.

docs.title: set_charges
docs.text:
set_charges(
    charges: Any, *, total_charge: float | None = None
) -> None

Set the per-atom charges (models that take them), shape (N,), and optionally the total charge, one event. charges=None with total_charge changes the total only.

docs.title: set_friction
docs.text:
set_friction(friction_per_fs: float) -> None

Set the Langevin friction in 1/fs, one event; it drops the graphs that bake c1/c2 in (a recorded re-capture).

docs.title: Committed dataclass
docs.text:
The committed step as read-only host arrays: what an observer sees (Simulation.committed).

stress (3×3, eV/Å³) is None for fixed-cell integrators; energy in eV. The composition (3-T03): species atomic numbers (N,), masses amu (N,), charges (N,) or None for models that take none.

docs.title: Port your ASE script
docs.text:
FastMACE offers three ways in from ASE. They all use the same force field, planner, gate and restart files.

You have Use Speed a tool that needs only a calculator (phonopy, NEB, your own optimiser) fm.calc compiled tier, no CUDA graphs an ASE MD or optimiser script fastmace.ase classes full graph-engine speed a new run fm.md or fm.Simulation full graph-engine speed

docs.title: Level 0: a calculator, fm.calc
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

atoms.calc = fm.calc("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
energy = atoms.get_potential_energy()
forces = atoms.get_forces()
stress = atoms.get_stress()

fm.calc wraps fastmace.ase.FastMACECalculator. ASE calls a calculator once per step from Python, so a calculator cannot use CUDA graphs over the whole step. You get the compiled model and the exact rewrites, not the full speed-up. FastMACE prints this once: use fm.md or the fastmace.ase integrators for full speed.

docs.title: Level 1: change the import
docs.text:
An ASE Langevin script:

from ase import units
from ase.md.langevin import Langevin

atoms.calc = mace_mp(...)
dyn = Langevin(atoms, 0.5 * units.fs, temperature_K=300, friction=0.02 / units.fs,
               trajectory="run.traj", logfile="run.log", loginterval=20)
dyn.attach(print_energy, interval=1000)
dyn.run(1_000_000)

becomes:

from ase import units
from fastmace.ase import Langevin

dyn = Langevin(atoms, 0.5 * units.fs, temperature_K=300, friction=0.02 / units.fs,
               model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", trajectory="run.traj",
               logfile="run.log", loginterval=20)
dyn.attach(print_energy, interval=1000)
dyn.run(1_000_000)
print(dyn.summary)        # the run report

Rules:

  • Arguments keep ASE 3.27's names and units. friction is in ASE's inverse time units, as in ASE. The shim never reinterprets an ASE argument. An argument that is neither supported nor explicitly refused raises TypeError naming it.
  • Refused: rng (pass seed=; the noise comes from FastMACE's device generator), a non-default communicator, and master.
  • FastMACE additions are keyword-only: model= or force_field=, head=, seed=, output=, check=, dispersion=.
  • Files: trajectory= and logfile= keep their ASE meaning and format, so your analysis scripts work unchanged. Everything else (metadata.json, the report, restart files) goes to output=, by default <trajectory stem>.fastmace/.
  • Observers see the committed state in atoms, and get_potential_energy(), get_forces() and get_stress() return the engine's values without a new evaluation. An observer may change positions, momenta, species, masses or charges; FastMACE applies the change as one event. Changing the atom count, PBC, cell, constraints or atoms.calc raises, because each would invalidate the plan.
  • FastMACE members: summary, plan, gate, metadata, simulation (the underlying fm.Simulation) and output.

docs.title: Mapped classes
docs.text:
ASE 3.27 class fastmace.ase class FastMACE integrator Langevin Langevin fm.integrators.Langevin LangevinBAOAB LangevinBAOAB fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB VelocityVerlet VelocityVerlet fm.integrators.NVE Bussi Bussi fm.integrators.CSVR NoseHooverChainNVT NoseHooverChainNVT fm.integrators.NoseHooverChain IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT same names fm.integrators.MTK NVTBerendsen, NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen same names fm.integrators.Berendsen LBFGS, FIRE (optimisers) LBFGS, FIRE fm.optimize.LBFGS, fm.optimize.FIRE

An ASE class without a mapping raises PlanRefused with the list of mapped ones. The shim never falls back to ASE's own loop silently.

docs.title: Resume a shim run
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

sim = fm.Simulation.resume("run.fastmace/")
sim.run()

The resumed run continues in FastMACE's chunked output format in that directory (see Output, restart and resume).

docs.title: Level 2: one call, fm.md
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NVT",
            temperature_K=300, steps=1_000_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3),
            output="run/", seed=1)
print(run.summary)

See FastMACE in five minutes for the arguments and the command-line equivalent, fastmace md.

See also: API: ASE front end, Integrators and optimisers.

docs.title: Monte Carlo and swaps
docs.text:
Experimental

MC moves carry an "experimental: not yet qualified" line in the run report until their qualification study is recorded.

FastMACE runs hybrid MD/MC: MD steps on the graph engine, with blocks of MC attempts in between. Species changes are transactional events inside the captured graph, so a swap does not cost a re-capture. The species superset (every species the run may contain) is declared up front.

docs.title: Move records
docs.text:
Record Move fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50) swap the species of two atoms; velocities="exchange" (default), "rescale", "redraw" or "redraw_all" fm.mc.Transmute(species=("Na", "K"), every=..., attempts=..., mu={...}) semi-grand canonical species change; mu are configurational chemical-potential differences in eV, fm.mc.configurational_mu converts full ones fm.mc.Displace(delta_A=0.1, every=..., attempts=...) displace one atom in a sphere; adaptive=True retunes δ after every block (equilibration only; sample with a fixed δ)

Each attempt is accepted by the Metropolis rule at the thermostat's current target temperature. The thermo output has mc_<move>_attempted and mc_<move>_accepted columns, and the counters survive restarts.

docs.title: With fm.md
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

run = fm.md("NaNbOCl4.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan",
            temperature_K=600, steps=200_000,
            mc=fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50),
            output="swap/", seed=1)

fm.md infers the species superset and the workload from mc=. With a constant temperature the MC temperature is that temperature, which must be positive. With a schedule, min_mc_temperature_K= is required: MC blocks attach only where the schedule's target is at or above it.

docs.title: With Simulation
docs.text:
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, species=["Na", "Nb", "Cl", "O"])
sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, ff,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=600, friction_per_fs=0.002),
    workload=fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=1000, species_changes=True, mc_moves=("swap",),
                         min_mc_temperature_K=250),
    output=fm.Output("run/"), seed=1,
)
sim.run(steps=100_000)                                    # MD only
sim.run(steps=100_000, mc=fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50))
sim.run(steps=50_000)                                     # the swap block stays attached
sim.run(steps=50_000, mc=None)                            # detach

A move set stays attached until a later run passes another mc= or mc=None. A species outside the superset raises SpeciesNotInSuperset.

docs.title: From TOML
docs.text:
[[mc]]
move = "swap"
pairs = [["O", "Cl"]]
every = 100
attempts = 50

docs.title: Charge and spin
docs.text:
For models that read charges (PolarMACE) or a total charge or spin (OMOL-0), a transmutation must keep ΔZ − Δq even (formal_charges=), or it is refused with ChargeParityRefused.

See also: Monte Carlo, Command line and TOML.

docs.title: Running MD
docs.text: This page covers the choices every MD run makes: the ensemble and integrator, the timestep, the friction, the seed, how long the run lasts and how often it writes. It uses fm.md for one-call runs and fm.Simulation when you want to keep the simulation and run it in pieces.

docs.title: Two ways in
docs.text:
fm.md builds and runs a simulation in one call and returns a RunResult:

import fastmace as fm

run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NVT",
            temperature_K=300, timestep_fs=0.5, steps=100_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3),
            output="run/", seed=1)
print(run.summary)

fm.Simulation takes the pieces explicitly: the structure, a force field or model, an integrator record, a workload, an output record and a seed. fm.md builds exactly this:

from ase.io import read

import fastmace as fm

atoms = read("NaCl.cif").repeat((3, 3, 3))
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, model,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=0.5, temperature_K=300, friction_per_fs=0.002),
    output=fm.Output("run/"),
    seed=1,
)
sim.run(steps=100_000)
sim.run(steps=100_000)          # 100,000 more steps, same engine
sim.flush_output()
print(sim.report.text())
sim.close()

Simulation copies atoms; your object is never changed. It needs periodic boundaries in all three directions. It can also be used as a context manager (with fm.Simulation(...) as sim:), which closes it at the end.

docs.title: Choosing an ensemble
docs.text:
fm.md's ensemble= and fastmace md --ensemble pick one of three integrators:

ensemble= Integrator ASE 3.27 class Needs "NVT" (default) fm.integrators.Langevin Langevin temperature_K or schedule "NPT" fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB LangevinBAOAB as NVT, plus pressure_GPa (default 0) and cell_mode ("hydrostatic" or "full") "NVE" fm.integrators.NVE (velocity Verlet) VelocityVerlet no temperature; refuses temperature_K, schedule and mc

pressure_GPa and cell_mode are for NPT only; fm.md refuses them with another ensemble.

docs.title: Choosing an integrator
docs.text:
For any other thermostat or barostat, pass an integrator record. It decides the ensemble, so leave out ensemble=, and set the temperature and timestep in the record only:

run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", steps=100_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3),
            integrator=fm.integrators.CSVR(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=300, tau_fs=100.0),
            output="csvr/", seed=1)
Record Ensemble ASE 3.27 class Required fields besides timestep_fs and temperature_K Langevin NVT Langevin friction_per_fs LangevinBAOAB NPT LangevinBAOAB friction_per_fs; pressure_GPa defaults to 0 NVE NVE VelocityVerlet none (no temperature_K) CSVR NVT Bussi tau_fs NoseHooverChain NVT NoseHooverChainNVT tdamp_fs MTK NPT IsotropicMTKNPT (cell_mode="hydrostatic"), MTKNPT ("full") pressure_GPa, tdamp_fs, pdamp_fs Berendsen NVT, or NPT with pressure_GPa NVTBerendsen, NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen (mask) taut_fs; with a pressure also taup_fs and compressibility_per_GPa

All times are in fs, pressures in GPa and compressibilities in 1/GPa. The other parameters keep ASE 3.27's names and defaults; for example NoseHooverChain has tchain=3 and tloop=1. Records are frozen dataclasses, so a typo in a field name is an error.

Some choices are flagged in the run report:

  • NPT (LangevinBAOAB, MTK, and Berendsen with a pressure) carries an "experimental: not yet qualified" line until its qualification study is recorded.
  • Berendsen is non-canonical. Use it for equilibration only; the report says so.

The same records go into a TOML file as an [integrator] table with type = "CSVR" and the record's fields (see Command line and TOML).

docs.title: Timestep
docs.text: timestep_fs is in fs. fm.md's default is 0.5 fs. The shipped anneal and melt-quench examples use 1.0 fs. With an explicit integrator record, the record's timestep_fs is the timestep, and fm.md refuses a different timestep_fs= argument.

docs.title: Friction
docs.text:
The Langevin records take friction_per_fs, in 1/fs. fm.md, fastmace md and a TOML [integrator] table without the field use 0.02 per ASE time unit, about 0.002 per fs (0.001965/fs).

The fastmace.ase classes take ASE's friction in ASE's inverse time units, as ASE does: friction=0.02 / units.fs is 0.02 per fs, ten times fm.md's default.

For LangevinBAOAB, ASE's thermostat time T_tau is 1 / friction, and the barostat time barostat_tau_fs defaults to 20 T_tau.

sim.set_friction(friction_per_fs) changes the friction during a run. It re-captures the CUDA graphs once, and the change is recorded.

docs.title: Starting velocities
docs.text:
By default FastMACE draws no starting velocities. A run starts from the momenta stored on the structure; most structure files have none, so the atoms start at rest and a Langevin thermostat heats them. CSVR cannot start from rest (it rescales velocities, and there are none): it refuses such a structure at once with an InputError, before anything is compiled.

fm.md(..., initial_velocities=...) (in a fastmace run file, the key initial_velocities; fastmace md has no flag for it) changes this. It is opt-in and acts only on a structure at rest (zero kinetic energy):

Value A structure at rest starts with "keep" (default) no velocities: it starts at rest, as in ASE "maxwell_boltzmann" Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities at the run's starting target: temperature_K, the integrator's, or the schedule's first temperature. Refused when that is 0 K (a schedule from 0 K) and for NVE, which has no target a float, K Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities at that temperature; works for NVE and for a schedule that starts at 0 K 
from fastmace.protocols import ramp

# CSVR heating from 0 K: start the atoms at 10 K, then follow the ramp.
run = fm.md(atoms, model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan",
            integrator=fm.integrators.CSVR(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=0.0, tau_fs=100.0),
            schedule=ramp(0, 1000, ps=20), initial_velocities=10.0, seed=1, output="heat/")

What to know before using it:

  • Seeded. The draw uses seed= (a drawn seed when seed is None, recorded in metadata.json as always), through its own random stream, so the thermostat noise is the same as without the option. The same seed gives the same starting velocities.
  • Only at rest. A structure that already has momenta keeps them; nothing is redrawn.
  • Recorded. The report and metadata.json's warnings say which happened, for example starting velocities: Maxwell-Boltzmann at 10 K, drawn from seed 1.
  • What is drawn. ASE's Maxwell-Boltzmann draw (thermalize_momenta, or MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution before ASE 3.29), without rescaling to the exact temperature; FixAtoms atoms get none. The integrator then treats the momenta as usual: with fixcm it removes the total momentum at the start.
  • fm.Simulation does not draw. The option belongs to fm.md (and so fastmace run); with Simulation, set the momenta on the Atoms yourself, as below.

To set the momenta yourself instead:

import numpy as np
from ase.md.velocitydistribution import MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution

MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution(atoms, temperature_K=300, rng=np.random.default_rng(1))
run = fm.md(atoms, model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NVE",
            timestep_fs=0.5, steps=100_000, output="nve/", seed=1)

This matters most for NVE, which has no thermostat. An NVE run sizes its neighbour-list skin for twice the starting kinetic temperature, at least 1 K. fm.md with an Atoms writes to ./fastmace-run/ unless you pass output=.

docs.title: Seeds
docs.text:
seed= seeds the thermostat noise and the MC streams. In fm.md it is optional: None draws a seed and records it in metadata.json, so any run can be repeated. fm.Simulation requires an int.

Bitwise reproducibility

The default hybrid backend uses atomic sums, so two runs with the same seed are not bitwise identical; compare them statistically. See Reproducibility.

docs.title: Steps and schedules
docs.text:
A run with a constant temperature needs steps=. A run with a schedule needs no steps=: it covers the whole schedule.

fm.protocols.ramp(start_K, end_K, ps=...) (or rate_K_per_ps=, signed) and fm.protocols.hold(temperature_K, ps=...) build a schedule; + joins them, and each segment must start where the previous one ended:

heat_hold_cool = (fm.protocols.ramp(0, 1000, ps=20) + fm.protocols.hold(1000, ps=10)
                  + fm.protocols.ramp(1000, 250, rate_K_per_ps=-3))
run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", schedule=heat_hold_cool,
            timestep_fs=1.0, repeat=(3, 3, 3), output="anneal/", seed=1)

temperature_K= and schedule= exclude each other. Durations are rounded to whole steps at the run's timestep. The named profiles slow, fast, ultrafast and anneal are in fm.protocols.PROFILES; for example fm.protocols.PROFILES["anneal"].schedule is 0 → 1000 K in 20 ps, then 1000 → 250 K over 250 ps.

With a schedule, steps= runs only the first part. Simulation.run continues it:

sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, model,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=0.0, friction_per_fs=0.002),
    workload=fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=1000),
    output=fm.Output("anneal/"), seed=1,
)
sim.run(schedule=heat_hold_cool, steps=50_000)   # the first 50,000 steps
sim.run()                                        # the rest of the schedule

fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=...) tells the planner the highest target, which sizes the neighbour-list skin. fm.md works it out from the schedule; with Simulation you pass it, and a schedule above it is refused before the first step. Without a workload, Simulation takes the integrator's temperature_K.

Simulation.run(steps=..., schedule=None) without an attached schedule keeps the current target. Example script: examples/01_nvt_anneal_nacl.py.

docs.title: Output intervals
docs.text:
fm.Output sets the directory and the intervals, in MD steps. The defaults are those of fm.md:

out = fm.Output("run/", trajectory_every=20, thermo_every=20, restart_every=10_000)
run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", temperature_K=300,
            steps=100_000, output=out, seed=1)
  • trajectory_every: a trajectory frame every n steps; None writes no trajectory.
  • thermo_every: a thermo row every n steps; always written.
  • restart_every: a restart point every n steps; None writes no periodic restart points.

A plain string, output="run/", takes these defaults. Output is written asynchronously, so writing does not slow the GPU. The files are described in Output, restart and resume.

See also: Integrators and optimisers, Output files, API: quick runs, API: Simulation.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
fm.load, fm.md, fm.calc and the CLI take a model as a label, a local path or a URL. List the labels with:

fastmace models
Label Head Licence Kind mp0-medium, mp0-large, mp0b3-medium, mpa0-medium MIT MACE-MP foundation models (PBE) omat0-medium, matpes-pbe, matpes-r2scan ASL OMAT and MatPES models mh1-omat, mh1-mp, mh1-r2scan fixed by the label ASL MACE-MH-1 with one head mh1 head= required ASL MACE-MH-1, any of its six heads polar1-s, polar1-m, polar1-l ASL MACE-POLAR-1 (needs [polar]) omol0-xl (omol0) omol ASL MACE-OMOL-0, molecules; takes charge= and spin_multiplicity= off23-small, off23-medium, off23-large, off23b-medium, off24-medium ASL MACE-OFF, organic molecules and crystals

fastmace models prints the file names and SHA-256 of each checkpoint.

docs.title: Heads
docs.text: A multi-head checkpoint without head= raises ValueError listing its heads. There is no default head. MH-1's heads are matpes_r2scan, mp_pbe_refit_add, spice_wB97M, oc20_usemppbe, omol and omat_pbe.

docs.title: Where checkpoints come from
docs.text:
fm.load(label) looks for the file in $FASTMACE_MODELS, then in <cache root>/models. With download=True it fetches the file from its official URL and checks the SHA-256 before keeping it. FastMACE never ships or redistributes model weights.

A file outside the label table needs sha256= (its expected hash) or trusted=True, because loading a checkpoint runs pickled code.

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
The weights' licence binds you independently of FastMACE's MIT licence. Several foundation models, MACE-MH-1 among them, are under the Academic Software License (ASL, non-commercial use only). FastMACE shows each model's licence once per process as a ModelLicenceWarning, and the run report has a licence: line read from the label table.

FastMACE's own licence and its dependencies' licences are on the Licences page.

docs.title: Which model for what
docs.text:
• Inorganic crystals: MH-1 (mh1-r2scan or mh1 with a head), OMAT-0 or MP-0. MH-1 runs at its fastest in FastMACE through the MH-1 rewrites.
  • Long-range electrostatics: MACE-POLAR-1. POLAR-1-S showed a Fukui charge runaway on NaNbO3, and all POLAR sizes failed on NaTaO3 in our tests.
  • Molecules: OMOL-0 (charge and spin) or MACE-OFF (organic elements only: H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br, I).
  • Dispersion: see NPT and D3. MACE-OFF, OMOL-0 and MH-1's omol head already contain dispersion, so dispersion="d3bj" is refused for them.

See also: Models, D3, PolarMACE and schedules, Environment and cache.

docs.title: NPT and D3 dispersion
docs.text:
Experimental

NPT and D3 carry an "experimental: not yet qualified" line in the run report until their qualification studies are recorded.

docs.title: NPT
docs.text:
ensemble="NPT" in fm.md (and --ensemble NPT on the command line) is ASE 3.27's LangevinBAOAB barostat on the graph engine:

run = fm.md("NbCl5.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", ensemble="NPT",
            temperature_K=300, pressure_GPa=0.0, cell_mode="hydrostatic",
            steps=200_000, repeat=(3, 3, 3), dispersion="d3bj", output="npt/", seed=1)

cell_mode is "hydrostatic" or "full". For other barostats, pass an explicit integrator:

Record ASE class fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB(...) LangevinBAOAB fm.integrators.MTK(..., cell_mode="hydrostatic" or "full") IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT fm.integrators.Berendsen(..., pressure_GPa=...) NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen (equilibration only, non-canonical)

Cell divergence. A vapour at low pressure expands without bound. LangevinBAOAB stops the run with CellDivergedError (restart and metadata written first) once the volume leaves [V0/20, 20 V0] or a cell vector is longer than 1000 Å. Change the limits with max_volume_ratio and max_cell_length_A.

Stress convention. The force field returns the potential (virial) stress as a full 3x3 tensor in ASE's sign convention; the integrator adds the kinetic part, as ASE's get_stress(include_ideal_gas=True) does.

docs.title: D3(BJ) dispersion
docs.text:
FastMACE has its own GPU D3(BJ) term. It runs inside the captured step in MD, in relaxations and in quenches, and needs no extra package.

run = fm.md(..., dispersion="d3bj")

"d3bj" is shorthand. FastMACE expands it to a complete fm.D3 record before planning: Becke-Johnson damping with the parameter set of the head's training functional (pbe for PBE-trained models, r2scan for matpes_r2scan), 40 bohr pair and coordination cutoffs, no three-body term, float64. The expanded record is printed in the report and recorded in metadata.json.

"d3bj" is refused when:

  • the training reference already contains dispersion (MACE-OFF, OMOL-0, MH-1's omol head), since D3 would count it twice;
  • the training functional is unknown (a model loaded from a path or URL). Pass an explicit record then:
run = fm.md(..., model=model, dispersion=fm.D3(functional="pbe"))

PolarMACE (POLAR-1) with D3 is refused with any record.

An explicit fm.D3 is used as given; a functional that differs from the training functional is a report warning. In TOML, a [dispersion] table holds the record's fields.

When to use it. The molecular chlorides need D3 in NPT: without it, NbCl5 swelled by 20 % at 300 K and evaporated at 600 K in our tests.

See also: Integrators and optimisers, Models, D3, PolarMACE and schedules.

docs.title: The planner
docs.text:
Every Simulation (and so every fm.md, fastmace md and fastmace.ase run) starts with a plan. The planner reads the model, the structure, the integrator, the workload, the installed software and the GPU, and decides:

  • the tier: the CUDA-graph engine (fastest), the compiled tier without graphs, the eager hybrid, or the reference path;
  • the backend: the cuEquivariance/OpenEquivariance hybrid, or plain cuEquivariance;
  • the precision of the force evaluation (float32 by default; integration is always float64);
  • which rewrites are on, and the reason for each one that is off;
  • the neighbour-list skin and buffer sizes.

Rules are general: there are no per-GPU or per-crystal tuning tables. Every rewrite is exact to rounding and is checked against the original MACE module when it is applied.

docs.title: Read the plan
docs.text:
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, model, integrator=..., seed=1)
print(sim.plan)                  # str(plan): about 30 lines, by section
print(sim.plan.describe(full=True))   # every decision with its rule and reason

str(plan) gives a short overview: the tier, backend and precision, the hard rules that decided them, the rewrites that are on and the ones that are off with a short reason. describe(full=True) lists every decision. The same text is in the run report and in metadata.json.

plan.decision(key) returns (item, choice, reason) for one decision, and plan.overrides() lists the options you set explicitly.

docs.title: Influence the plan
docs.text:
• Workload: fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=..., species_changes=..., mc_moves=..., host_callbacks_every=...) tells the planner what the run will do. fm.md infers it from its arguments. A schedule above max_temperature_K is refused. For runs with MC moves or species changes the skin and buffer headroom are sized from it; plain MD keeps the 0.3 Å skin.
  • Mode: Simulation(mode=...) asks for a tier; None lets the planner choose.
  • Rewrites and precision live on the force field: fm.ForceField(model, atoms, precision="float32", rewrites="auto").
  • An option the planner cannot honour raises PlanRefused with every reason, before the first step. Nothing is substituted silently.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text: check="gate" evaluates the planned engine on your structure (and rattled copies) against a float64 reference before the first step. If it fails, the fallback searches for the closest plan that passes, turning off rewrites one by one, and records what it did. The gate is opt-in; the default is check="skip". The record is sim.gate.

docs.title: Runtime adaptation
docs.text: During a run the planner watches re-captures and buffer overflows. Past a budget it may switch tier at a committed step, or fall back after a capture error, and the report's runtime line records it. A resume rebuilds the recorded revision exactly.

docs.title: When the run did not get the graph engine
docs.text:
The report says why and what would change it: a structure that is not 3D periodic, a missing OpenEquivariance (fastmace doctor names the piece), a model outside the rewrite registry, padded edges that are not exactly zero, a failed self-check, or a fallback after a failed gate.

The full rule list is on Planner, gate and fallback. The planner design note in the repository explains the design.

See also: Planner, gate and fallback, Engine and neighbour list, Rewrites and precision.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
fastmace relax NaCl.cif --model mh1 --head matpes_r2scan --optimizer gpu-LBFGS --fmax 0.01
fastmace relax NaCl.cif --model mh1 --head matpes_r2scan --optimizer gpu-FIRE --cell-filter frechet --pressure 0
fastmace quench run/ --into gpu --optimizer gpu-LBFGS
Optimizer name Runs on gpu-LBFGS (default) the graph engine gpu-FIRE the graph engine ase-LBFGS, ase-BFGS ASE's optimisers on fm.calc LBFGS, BFGS ASE's (so existing protocol files keep their meaning)

gpu-LBFGS reproduces the annealing-benchmark minima of ASE's LBFGS.

fastmace relax writes the relaxed structure (--output, default <stem>.relaxed.extxyz) with a .json summary and a .log.

fastmace quench RUN_DIR quenches frames of a finished run, chosen as a protocol's quench picks them. Each frame keeps its own cell. --into NAME writes RUN_DIR/quench-NAME/, so one run can be quenched with several optimisers side by side. A GPU quench relaxes all its frames on one engine.

docs.title: Python: Simulation.relax
docs.text:
import fastmace as fm

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
opt = fm.optimize.LBFGS()                                  # ASE 3.27's defaults
opt = fm.optimize.FIRE(cell_filter=fm.optimize.FrechetCell(scalar_pressure_GPa=0.0))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, model, optimizer=opt, seed=0)
relaxed, summary = sim.relax(fmax=0.01)

A relaxation Simulation takes optimizer= instead of integrator= and writes no output files (pass no output=).

docs.title: Python: ASE-style optimisers
docs.text:
from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
