from fastmace.ase import LBFGS

opt = LBFGS(FrechetCellFilter(atoms), model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
opt.run(fmax=0.01)

fastmace.ase.LBFGS and FIRE take ASE 3.27's arguments. use_line_search=True, position_reset_callback and the deprecated maxmove are refused. They take Atoms or FrechetCellFilter; other cell filters are refused with the reason.

docs.title: Anneal and quench protocols
docs.text:
schedule=fm.protocols.PROFILES["anneal"].schedule (or the profiles slow, fast, ultrafast; in TOML just schedule = "anneal") runs a temperature schedule; fm.protocols.ramp and fm.protocols.hold build your own:

anneal = fm.protocols.ramp(0, 1000, ps=20) + fm.protocols.ramp(1000, 250, rate_K_per_ps=-3)
sim.run(schedule=anneal)

A protocol file's [relax] and [quench] tables take the same optimizer names.

See also: Integrators and optimisers, Command line and TOML.

docs.title: What a run writes
docs.text:
fm.Output("run/", trajectory_every=20, thermo_every=20, restart_every=10_000) (the fm.md defaults) writes into run/:

File Content thermo.<n>.csv thermo rows (step, time, temperature, energies, pressure for NPT), each chunk with its header trajectory.<n>.traj ASE trajectory frames restart.npz the complete simulation state at the last restart point simulation.json the inputs and planner options, for resume metadata.json plan, gate, report, provenance (versions, model hash, GPU)

The outputs are written in chunks, n = 0, 1, ..., with a chunk boundary at every restart point. Each chunk is complete on its own: ase.io.read("run/trajectory.0.traj", index=":") reads one. To read a whole run in order:

from fastmace.io.output import read_frames, read_thermo

frames = read_frames("run/")
thermo = read_thermo("run/")

Output is asynchronous: a snapshot is copied to the host and written while the next step runs, so writing does not slow the GPU.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
A restart file holds the complete state: positions, momenta, cell, barostat and thermostat state, the RNG state, species after MC exchanges, the schedule position, the MC counters and the plan revision. Restart points are written every restart_every steps, at the end of each protocol piece and by save_restart. A run whose steps is not a multiple of restart_every has no restart at its last step; see Output files.

sim.save_restart("run/restart.npz")         # an extra one by hand
sim = fm.Simulation.resume("run/")          # continue
sim.run()                                   # the rest of the schedule

Resume checks the chunks up to the restart point, deletes later chunks (rows and frames written after the restart point) and continues with the next chunk. Nothing is rewritten. If the stored chunks do not match, it raises RestartMismatch before touching anything.

A resume rebuilds the recorded plan. If the software or GPU changed so that the plan would differ, it refuses unless you pass allow_plan_change=True. A resume never falls back.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: Hybrid runs (the default backend) use atomic sums and are not bitwise reproducible; compare them statistically. A resumed run agrees bit for bit with an uninterrupted one in plans made with fm.Workload(reproducible=True), which the planner refuses where it cannot guarantee it. Restart points rebuild the neighbour list, so for bitwise agreement set restart_every=None too.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
fastmace run run.toml writes the same files. To quench frames of a finished run, see Relaxations and quenches.

See also: Output files.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: These pages list every option FastMACE takes, with its values, default and effect. The user guide shows how to use them for common jobs. The API reference lists the functions and classes with their signatures.

docs.title: How options reach a run
docs.text:
Every option is a field of a frozen record. Nothing is set through module-level switches or environment variables, except the few process-wide settings on Environment and cache.

Where you set it What it takes Page fm.load(label, head=..., ...) the model, head, charge, spin, trust Models, D3, PolarMACE and schedules fm.ForceField(model, atoms, precision=..., rewrites=..., dispersion=..., polar=...) force precision, a RewriteConfig, D3, a PolarConfig Rewrites and precision, PolarMACE fm.Simulation(..., integrator=...) or optimizer=... an fm.integrators or fm.optimize record Integrators and optimisers fm.Simulation(..., engine=..., neighbours=...) EngineConfig, NeighbourConfig Engine and neighbour list fm.Simulation(..., mode=..., check=..., workload=..., fallback=..., gate=..., runner=..., adaptation=..., calibration=...) the planner's inputs Planner, gate and fallback fm.md(..., mc=...), Simulation.run(..., mc=...) fm.mc move records Monte Carlo fm.Simulation(..., output=fm.Output(...)) output intervals and files Output files fastmace md, fastmace run run.toml, ... flags and TOML keys Command line and TOML

fm.md takes most of these as keyword arguments too and passes them on.

The configuration records are not in the fm namespace. Import them from fastmace.config:

import fastmace as fm
from fastmace.config import EngineConfig, NeighbourConfig, RewriteConfig

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, rewrites=RewriteConfig(radial_tables="on"))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, ff, integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(temperature_K=300, friction_per_fs=0.002), seed=1,
                    engine=EngineConfig(pipelined="off"), neighbours=NeighbourConfig(skin=0.5))
print(sim.plan.overrides())   # the options you set, and what the planner did with them

docs.title: "auto", "on" and "off"
docs.text:
Many fields are toggles with three values.

  • "auto" (the default) lets the planner decide, with a general rule based on the model, backend, precision and execution tier. The plan records the rule and the reason.
  • "on" asks for the option. If the model or plan cannot use it, the planner raises PlanRefused with the reason before the first step. Nothing is substituted silently.
  • "off" turns the option off.

print(sim.plan) shows the decisions that matter, and sim.plan.describe(full=True) shows every decision with its rule. The same text is in the run report and in metadata.json.

docs.title: Units
docs.text: Units follow ASE: Å, eV, eV/Å, K and amu. Times are in fs at the API. Pressures are in GPa wherever a name ends in _GPa.

docs.title: Command line and TOML
docs.text:
fastmace is installed as a console script. python -m fastmace.cli is the same command. This page lists every subcommand, every flag and every key of the fastmace run file. FastMACE in five minutes shows the common runs.

fastmace [--version] [--debug] COMMAND [--debug] [options]
Command What it does doctor checks the installation; changes nothing models lists the model labels, heads, files, SHA-256 and licences md constant-temperature or NVE MD in one command (fm.md) init writes a commented TOML of fm.md's arguments run runs MD or a protocol from a TOML (or YAML) file relax relaxes one structure, at fixed cell or with a cell filter quench quenches the trajectory frames of a finished run

docs.title: Global options and exit codes
docs.text:
Flag Values Default What it does --version prints fastmace <version> and exits 0 --debug off prints the traceback of a FastMACE error instead of its message alone; a ValueError raised inside fm.md or a protocol stage then shows its traceback instead of exit code 2 -h, --help the help of fastmace or of one command

--debug may stand before or after the command: fastmace --debug md ... and fastmace md --debug ... are the same.

Exit code Meaning 0 success 1 a FastMACE error (a refused plan, a failed gate, a missing model file, a restart that does not match, ...), a required doctor check failed, a relaxation did not converge, or a protocol stage stopped 2 a usage error: an unknown flag or value (argparse), a flag combination with no fm.md meaning, an unknown or missing TOML key, or no command at all (then the help is printed)

A FastMACE error is printed as its message alone: what happened, why, what to do next, and where the record is. Any other exception is a bug and keeps its traceback.

docs.title: fastmace doctor
docs.text:
fastmace doctor [--no-hash]
Flag Values Default What it does --no-hash off lists the model files without computing their SHA-256 (hashing takes seconds per file)

Prints one line per check, [ ok ], [FAIL] (a required check) or [warn] (an optional one), and for each failed item the command or page that fixes it. Exit code 1 if a required check failed, else 0. The checks are listed item by item on Environment and cache. doctor changes nothing: it creates no directory, imports neither MACE nor OpenEquivariance, and deletes no lock file.

docs.title: fastmace models
docs.text:
fastmace models

No flags. Prints the label table (label, head, licence, released file name, SHA-256), the licence texts, and the aliases that take a head. It reads only the table: it looks at no file and downloads nothing. See Models and licences.

docs.title: fastmace md
docs.text:
fastmace md --model MODEL --structure FILE [options]

Each flag is one fm.md argument. A flag that is not given is left out, so fm.md's default applies; the command has no defaults of its own. It prints the run report and the output directory, and exits 0.

Model flags

Flag Values Default fm.md argument What it does --model label, path or URL required model the model; labels are listed by fastmace models --head head name none head the head of a multi-head model; required for MH-1 --charge int the model's charge total charge, for models that take it --spin-multiplicity int the model's spin_multiplicity spin multiplicity, for models that take it --sha256 64 hex digits none sha256 the expected SHA-256 of a model file outside the label table --trusted off trusted=True trust a model file without a known SHA-256; it is unpickled

Run flags

Flag Values Default fm.md argument What it does --structure file required structure any format ASE reads --repeat NA NB NC three ints 1 1 1 repeat supercell repeats; the cell is never expanded silently --ensemble NVT, NPT, NVE (any case) NVT ensemble NVT is Langevin, NPT LangevinBAOAB, NVE velocity Verlet from the structure's momenta --temperature K float, K none temperature_K the target temperature; required for NVT and NPT, refused for NVE --pressure GPA float, GPa 0 pressure_GPa NPT only --cell-mode hydrostatic, full hydrostatic cell_mode NPT only --timestep FS float, fs 0.5 timestep_fs the MD timestep --steps int required steps the number of MD steps --dispersion none, d3bj none dispersion d3bj adds D3(BJ), with the parameters of the head's training functional from the label table --d3-functional NAME parameter set, e.g. pbe, r2scan none dispersion=fm.D3(functional=NAME) the D3 parameter set; needs --dispersion d3bj --seed int ≥ 0 drawn seed the noise seed; a drawn seed is recorded in metadata.json --check skip, gate, allow_unavailable skip check gate runs the gate before the first step; allow_unavailable runs it but goes on if no reference can run --output DIR directory ./<structure stem>.fastmace/ output the output directory, with fm.Output's default intervals

The Langevin friction is fm.md's, 0.02 per ASE time unit (about 0.00196 per fs). NVE draws no velocities: a structure file without momenta starts at rest.

Schedules, MC moves, explicit integrators, a full D3 record, output intervals and planner options have no flag. Use fastmace init and fastmace run for them.

fm.md does not download models: a label's file must be in $FASTMACE_MODELS or <cache root>/models already. Fetch it once from Python with fm.load(label, download=True) (see Environment and cache).

docs.title: fastmace init
docs.text:
fastmace init [fastmace md's flags] > run.toml

Takes every flag of fastmace md, all optional, and prints a TOML file of fm.md's arguments for fastmace run. Every argument appears under its own name: the ones given as set lines, the rest as commented lines (# key = value) with what they do and an example. The record tables (schedule segments, integrator, D3, MC, output, planner options) follow as commented examples.

  • Without flags, the set lines are an example run: structure = "NaCl.cif", model = "mh1", head = "matpes_r2scan", ensemble = "NVT", temperature_K = 300.0, steps = 1000000, output = "run/".
  • With flags, the set lines are exactly those flags, so fastmace init <flags> > run.toml; fastmace run run.toml is fastmace md <flags>.
  • --dispersion d3bj --d3-functional NAME is written as a [dispersion] table with the record's numbers.

Exit code 2 for --d3-functional without --dispersion d3bj, else 0.

docs.title: fastmace run
docs.text:
fastmace run CONFIG.toml [--steps N] [--output DIR] [--calibrate]
fastmace run --resume RUN_DIR [--steps N]
Argument or flag Values Default What it does CONFIG.toml a file, -, or a shipped protocol name the run file; - reads standard input (as TOML); a .yaml or .yml file is read as YAML --resume RUN_DIR directory continues the protocol run in RUN_DIR; not together with CONFIG.toml --steps N int ≥ 1 the whole run runs at most N MD steps, writes a restart and stops; makes the run a protocol run (below). A steps key in the file is the run's length; --steps shortens this piece of it --output DIR directory the file's output the output directory, in place of the file's (also replaces directory in an [output] table) --calibrate off the file's calibrate = true: times hybrid against plain cuEquivariance on this structure before the run; refused with --resume

Paths in the file (the structure, the output directory) are taken relative to the directory fastmace run starts in, except for a shipped protocol, whose relative structure path is a file shipped with it. A key that is not an fm.md argument is refused, naming it (exit code 2). structure and model are required.

A YAML file needs PyYAML and is read with safe_load only. It takes the same keys as TOML.

docs.title: Plain runs and protocol runs
docs.text:
A file without [relax] or [quench] tables, run without --steps, is a plain run: fm.md(structure, **keys), exactly as fastmace md. It prints the report and exits.

A file with a [relax] or [quench] table, or any run with --steps, is a protocol run, in stages in the output directory:

  1. [relax]: an initial relaxation at fixed cell (relaxation.log, relaxed.extxyz). If it does not converge, the run stops with exit code 1.
  2. fm.md on the relaxed structure, for at most --steps steps of the schedule (all of it without --steps), then a restart at the last step. If the schedule is not finished, the run pauses and prints the fastmace run --resume command.
  3. [quench], once the schedule is done: trajectory frames picked per target-temperature bin, each relaxed to 0 K (quench/).

protocol.json in the output directory records the stages, the pieces and the status (see Output files). A directory that already holds a protocol run is refused; continue it with --resume. fastmace run --resume RUN_DIR [--steps N] continues for at most N more steps, then the quench. A complete run prints that it is complete and exits 0. A run stopped by a failed relaxation or a diverged cell cannot be resumed.

--resume continues protocol runs only. A plain run is continued from Python with fm.Simulation.resume(RUN_DIR) (see Output, restart and resume).

The shipped protocols are named by their file stem: npt_anneal_NbCl5, npt_anneal_NbCl5_short, swap_anneal_NaNbOCl4 and swap_anneal_NaNbOCl4_short. fastmace run swap_anneal_NaNbOCl4_short runs one; a file of the same name in the current directory wins.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
The keys are fm.md's arguments under their own names. See fm.md for the Python side.

Key Values Default What it does structure path required the structure, any format ASE reads model label, path or URL required the model head string none head of a multi-head model; required for MH-1 charge int the model's total charge, for models that take it spin_multiplicity int the model's spin multiplicity, for models that take it sha256 string none expected SHA-256 of a model file outside the label table trusted bool false trust a model file without a known SHA-256 (it is unpickled) ensemble "NVT", "NPT", "NVE" "NVT" Langevin, LangevinBAOAB or velocity Verlet; ignored in favour of [integrator] when one is given (a conflicting non-default value is refused) temperature_K float, K none the target temperature; or a schedule, not both schedule profile name or [[schedule]] segments none a temperature schedule (below) pressure_GPa float, GPa 0.0 NPT only cell_mode "hydrostatic", "full" "hydrostatic" NPT only timestep_fs float, fs 0.5 the timestep steps int the whole schedule required without a schedule; with one, at most this many steps of it mc [mc] or [[mc]] tables none MC moves (below); experimental min_mc_temperature_K float, K the start temperature MC runs only where the target is at or above it; required with a schedule and MC dispersion "none", "d3bj" or a [dispersion] table none D3(BJ): "d3bj" takes the head's training functional repeat array of three ints [1, 1, 1] supercell repeats output directory or an [output] table "./<structure stem>.fastmace/" the output directory and intervals seed int ≥ 0 drawn the noise seed, recorded in metadata.json initial_velocities "keep", "maxwell_boltzmann" or float, K "keep" starting velocities of a structure at rest: kept at rest, seeded Maxwell-Boltzmann at the starting target, or at this temperature (see Starting velocities) check "skip", "gate", "allow_unavailable" "skip" the gate; opt-in integrator an [integrator] table none an explicit integrator (below); it wins over ensemble mode "graph", "compiled", "eager", "reference" unset the execution tier; unset lets the planner choose allow_reference bool false recorded in the plan only: it lifts no refusal, and mode = "reference" works without it calibrate bool false times hybrid against plain cuEquivariance first and takes plain cuEq only if it is more than 5 % faster; MD only, refused with MC fallback a [fallback] table defaults the fallback options gate a [gate] table defaults where the gate's references may run runner a [runner] table defaults the subprocess runner engine an [engine] table defaults backend and engine options neighbours a [neighbours] table defaults the neighbour list

With an explicit [integrator], temperature_K, timestep_fs, pressure_GPa and cell_mode must be left out or equal the record's fields; set them in the table.

docs.title: schedule
docs.text:
Either a profile name or an array of segments, not both.

Profile Schedule "slow" 0 → 400 K in 30 ps, 400 → 0 K in 240 ps "fast" 0 → 400 K in 3 ps, 400 → 0 K in 24 ps "ultrafast" 0 → 400 K in 1 ps, 400 → 0 K in 8 ps "anneal" 0 → 1000 K in 20 ps, 1000 → 250 K in 250 ps

In a run file a profile name sets the schedule only. The profile's output intervals, relaxation and quench settings are not applied; set them in [output], [relax] and [quench].

Each [[schedule]] table is one segment; segments follow each other without a temperature jump.

Key Segment Values What it does kind both "ramp", "hold" the segment type start_K, end_K ramp float, K the ramp's end points ps ramp or hold float > 0, ps the duration; a ramp takes ps or rate_K_per_ps, not both rate_K_per_ps ramp float, K/ps the rate; its sign must follow the ramp's direction temperature_K hold float, K the held temperature

Durations are rounded half up to whole steps. On a ramp the target moves every step.

docs.title: [integrator]
docs.text:
type names an fm.integrators record; the other keys are that record's fields. Time constants have no defaults. For Langevin and LangevinBAOAB, friction_per_fs defaults to fm.md's (0.02 per ASE time unit). See Integrators and optimisers for what each field does.

type Required fields Optional fields (default) "Langevin" temperature_K timestep_fs (0.5), friction_per_fs, fixcm ("auto"), fixcm_projection ("auto") "LangevinBAOAB" temperature_K timestep_fs (0.5), friction_per_fs, pressure_GPa (0.0), external_stress_GPa (none), cell_mode ("hydrostatic"), barostat_tau_fs (ASE's 20 T_tau), barostat_mass_factor (1.0), disable_cell_langevin (false), fixcm (true), max_volume_ratio (20.0), max_cell_length_A (1000.0) "NVE" timestep_fs fixcm ("auto"), dof ("auto") "CSVR" timestep_fs, temperature_K, tau_fs fixcm ("auto"), dof ("auto") "NoseHooverChain" timestep_fs, temperature_K, tdamp_fs tchain (3), tloop (1), fixcm (true), dof ("auto") "MTK" timestep_fs, temperature_K, pressure_GPa, tdamp_fs, pdamp_fs tchain (3), pchain (3), tloop (1), ploop (1), cell_mode ("hydrostatic"), fixcm (true), dof ("auto") "Berendsen" timestep_fs, temperature_K, taut_fs pressure_GPa, then taup_fs and compressibility_per_GPa (required with a pressure), mask (three 0/1 flags), fixcm ("auto"), dof ("auto")

MTK is experimental. Berendsen is not canonical: use it for equilibration only.

docs.title: dispersion
docs.text:
"none" (the default), "d3bj", or a [dispersion] table with the fields of fm.D3:

Key Values Default What it does functional string required the parameter set, e.g. "pbe", "r2scan"; should be the model's training functional damping "bj" "bj" Becke-Johnson damping pair_cutoff_bohr float 40.0 pair cutoff, bohr cn_cutoff_bohr float 40.0 coordination-number cutoff, bohr three_body bool false the ATM term; true is refused smoothing "none" "none" cutoff smoothing precision "float64" "float64" precision of the reductions autoang, autoev float 0.52917726, 27.21138505 the unit constants s6, s8, a1, a2 float the functional's set give all four or none

See Models, D3, PolarMACE and schedules.

docs.title: mc
docs.text:
One [mc] table or several [[mc]] tables, each an fm.mc record. move picks the record. MC is experimental. See Monte Carlo.

move Fields (default) "swap" pairs (array of species pairs, required), every (required), attempts (required), velocities ("exchange"; or "rescale", "redraw", "redraw_all") "transmute" species (at least two, required), every, attempts (required), velocities ("rescale", or "redraw_all" when the integrator fixes the centre of mass; or "redraw"), mu (table species → eV), formal_charges (table species → int) "displace" delta_A (float, Å, required), every, attempts (required), adaptive (false)

Species are symbols or atomic numbers. every is in MD steps.

docs.title: [output]
docs.text:
The fields of fm.Output. A missing directory is fm.md's default, ./<structure stem>.fastmace/.

Key Values Default What it does directory path ./<structure stem>.fastmace/ the output directory trajectory_every int ≥ 1 20 steps between trajectory frames thermo_every int ≥ 1 20 steps between thermo rows restart_every int ≥ 1 10000 steps between restart points

TOML has no null, so trajectory_every and restart_every cannot be switched off from a TOML file; in a YAML file null switches them off. See Output files.

docs.title: [relax] and [quench]
docs.text:
These two tables make a protocol run. They are not fm.md arguments.

Table Key Values Default What it does [relax] fmax float > 0, eV/Å required converged when every force is below it optimizer an optimizer name "gpu-LBFGS" see fastmace relax max_steps int ≥ 1 5000 at most this many steps [quench] min_K float, K required the lowest target temperature whose frames are picked bin_K float > 0, K required the width of a target-temperature bin per_bin int ≥ 1 required frames per bin and ramp fmax float > 0, eV/Å required the quench's convergence optimizer an optimizer name required the quench's optimizer max_steps int ≥ 1 required at most this many steps per frame

[quench] needs all six keys, a schedule and trajectory frames. The relaxation keeps the cell fixed; each quenched frame keeps its own cell.

docs.title: Planner tables
docs.text:
[engine], [neighbours], [fallback], [gate] and [runner] take the fields of fastmace.config.EngineConfig, NeighbourConfig, FallbackConfig, GateConfig and RunnerConfig. An unknown field is refused, naming the known ones. The common ones:

Table Key Values Default What it does [engine] backend "auto", "hybrid", "cueq" "auto" hybrid OEq/cuEq or plain cuEq compile_mode "default", "none" "default" torch.compile of the model device device string "cuda:0" the GPU [neighbours] skin float, Å, or "auto" "auto" the neighbour-list skin d3_skin float, Å, or "auto" "auto" the D3 pair list's skin [fallback] fallback "auto", "refuse" "auto" fall back to a validated slower plan, or raise [gate] cpu_float64_time_limit_s float, s 300.0 CPU float64 references only within this time [runner] stall_timeout_s float, s 1800.0 a child without progress for this long is killed

The full field lists are on Engine and neighbour list and Planner, gate and fallback. An array becomes a tuple; a [runner.environment] table is a mapping of variable names to values.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
# An NPT anneal with D3, swap MC, a relaxation and a quench.
structure = "NaNbOCl4.cif"
model = "mh1"
head = "matpes_r2scan"
repeat = [3, 3, 3]
ensemble = "NPT"
pressure_GPa = 0.0
cell_mode = "hydrostatic"
timestep_fs = 1.0
min_mc_temperature_K = 250.0     # MC only where the target is >= 250 K
dispersion = "d3bj"              # D3(BJ) of the head's functional (r2scan)
seed = 1
check = "skip"

# 0 -> 1000 K in 2 ps, then down to 250 K at -30 K/ps
[[schedule]]
kind = "ramp"
start_K = 0.0
end_K = 1000.0
ps = 2.0

[[schedule]]
kind = "ramp"
start_K = 1000.0
end_K = 250.0
rate_K_per_ps = -30.0

[[mc]]
move = "swap"
pairs = [["O", "Cl"]]
every = 100                      # a block every 100 MD steps
attempts = 50
velocities = "exchange"

[output]
directory = "anneal/"
trajectory_every = 10
thermo_every = 10
restart_every = 10000

[engine]
backend = "hybrid"

[relax]                          # before the MD, at fixed cell
fmax = 0.01
optimizer = "gpu-LBFGS"
max_steps = 5000

[quench]                         # after the MD: 2 frames per 100 K bin from 500 K
min_K = 500.0
bin_K = 100.0
per_bin = 2
fmax = 0.01
optimizer = "gpu-LBFGS"
max_steps = 5000

fastmace run anneal.toml --steps 100000     # first piece
fastmace run --resume anneal/ --steps 100000

docs.title: fastmace relax
docs.text:
fastmace relax STRUCTURE --model MODEL [options]
Flag Values Default What it does STRUCTURE file required any format ASE reads --model label, path or URL required as fastmace md --head, --charge, --spin-multiplicity, --sha256, --trusted as fastmace md --precision float32, float64 float32 the force-field precision --dispersion, --d3-functional none as fastmace md --optimizer gpu-LBFGS, gpu-FIRE, ase-LBFGS, ase-BFGS, LBFGS, BFGS gpu-LBFGS gpu-* run on the graph engine; ase-* are ASE's on fm.calc; bare LBFGS and BFGS mean ASE's --fmax EV_A float > 0, eV/Å 0.01 converged when every force is below it --steps int ≥ 1 5000 at most this many optimizer steps --repeat NA NB NC three ints ≥ 1 1 1 1 supercell repeats --cell-filter frechet none (fixed cell) relaxes the cell too, with ASE's FrechetCellFilter (its device port for gpu-*) --pressure GPA float, GPa 0 the cell filter's scalar pressure; needs --cell-filter --output FILE file <structure stem>.relaxed.extxyz the relaxed structure; the .json summary and .log go next to it

The Python side is fm.Simulation(..., optimizer=fm.optimize.LBFGS()) and sim.relax(fmax=...); see Relaxations and quenches. The files are described on Output files. A relaxation that does not reach --fmax within --steps still writes its files and exits 1.

docs.title: fastmace quench
docs.text:
fastmace quench RUN_DIR [options]
Flag Values Default What it does RUN_DIR directory required a finished run with a schedule, trajectory frames, restart.npz and simulation.json --into NAME letters, digits, ._- none writes RUN_DIR/quench-NAME/ instead of RUN_DIR/quench/ --optimizer as fastmace relax from the settings the optimizer --fmax EV_A float, eV/Å from the settings converged when every force is below it --max-steps int from the settings at most this many steps per frame --min-K float, K from the settings the lowest target temperature whose frames are picked --bin-K float, K from the settings the width of a target-temperature bin --per-bin int from the settings frames per bin and ramp

The settings are the run's [quench] table for a protocol run, else the anneal profile's: min_K 500, bin_K 100, per_bin 2, fmax 0.01, optimizer gpu-LBFGS, max_steps 5000. Each flag replaces one value.

The quench uses the run's model (checked by SHA-256), precision, D3 record and engine options. Frames are picked by the schedule's target temperature, on each ramp separately, evenly spaced within each bin, plus the final frame; each is relaxed at its own cell. A complete quench (its quench.json exists) only prints its summary. An interrupted one continues with the settings it started with.

docs.title: Engine and neighbour list
docs.text:
Two records hold the options of the engine that steps the simulation:

  • EngineConfig: the backend, compilation, CUDA graphs, pipelining, allocator and float64 settings;
  • NeighbourConfig: the skin neighbour list and the padded edge buffers.

Pass them to fm.Simulation or fm.md as engine= and neighbours=. They are not in the fm namespace; import them from fastmace.config.

import fastmace as fm
from fastmace.config import EngineConfig, NeighbourConfig

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, model,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(temperature_K=1200, friction_per_fs=0.02),
    seed=1,
    engine=EngineConfig(backend="cueq", recapture_budget=16),
    neighbours=NeighbourConfig(skin=0.5),
)
print(sim.plan.overrides())   # the options you set, and what the planner did with them

fm.md(..., engine=EngineConfig(...), neighbours=NeighbourConfig(...)) takes the same records.

Both records are frozen. A value outside the allowed set raises ValueError when you build the record, before anything is loaded. An option the plan cannot honour raises PlanRefused with the reason when the Simulation is built, before the first step.

A record you pass replaces the default one as a whole, so set every field you need in one EngineConfig. Without engine=, a Simulation uses EngineConfig(), on cuda:0. Only fm.ForceField.evaluate, which takes no engine=, falls back to EngineConfig(device="cpu", compile_mode="none") on a machine without CUDA.

For "auto", "on" and "off" see the reference overview. Each resolved value and its reason is in sim.plan.describe(full=True), under the key EngineConfig.<field> or NeighbourConfig.<field>. The planner guide explains how a plan is made.

docs.title: Terms used on this page
docs.text:
• CUDA graph capture. The engine records the GPU work of one stage of a step (for example the force call) once as a CUDA graph and then replays it every step. A replay launches all kernels at once, without Python in between. A graph is tied to fixed tensor shapes and addresses.
  • Re-capture. Recording a graph again, or recording a new variant of a stage that was captured before: for example when the number of edges moves into a new bucket, after a buffer had to grow, or after an event dropped the graphs. Each re-capture costs host time, and the step that needs it waits.
  • Skin. The neighbour list stores every pair closer than cutoff + skin. That list stays valid until some atom has moved more than skin / 2 since the last build. A larger skin means fewer rebuilds and more pairs per step.
  • Edge buffer and edge bucket. The model reads the pairs inside the cutoff (the edges), padded to a fixed length so that one captured graph fits many steps. That length is the edge count rounded up to a bucket. The padded edges lie beyond the cutoff and contribute exactly zero. Each bucket that the run visits costs one graph per stage.
  • Tiers. graph (compiled model and CUDA graphs), compiled (compiled model, no graphs), eager (no compilation, no graphs) and reference (MACE's own calculator). See the planner reference.
  • Backends. hybrid: cuEquivariance for most of the model and OpenEquivariance kernels for the convolutions. cueq: plain cuEquivariance throughout. See the planner reference.

docs.title: EngineConfig
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes backend "auto", "hybrid", "cueq" "auto": hybrid when OpenEquivariance can build, the device is CUDA, MACE was not imported before FastMACE, and the process has not compiled a plain cuEq model; else cueq, with the reason Chooses the model backend. reproducible=True in the workload resolves auto to cueq and refuses hybrid. hybrid on a CPU device is refused. The reference tier always uses MACE's stock cuEq model. compile_mode "default", "none" "default" "default" compiles the model with torch.compile. "none" runs it uncompiled. The eager and reference tiers set "none" themselves. If the installed MACE lacks the compile interface, the planner sets "none" and records why. With "none" on the graph tier, the uncompiled model is still captured in CUDA graphs. device a torch device string "cuda:0" The device of the model and the simulation state. fm.ForceField.evaluate uses "cpu" on a machine without CUDA. pipelined "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on for MD, unless speculative_graph is set Launches the force stage of a step before the host has read the step's neighbour flags. The step is checked while the force stage runs. A step that needed a rebuild, or more edges than were padded, is restored and redone. Off for relaxations (an explicit "on" there is refused). "on" together with speculative_graph=True is refused. The reference tier turns it off. async_output "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on for MD and relaxations Copies thermo samples and trajectory frames behind their step and writes them while the next steps run. Off for one-off evaluations (fm.calc, ForceField.evaluate). speculative_graph True, False False One combined graph per step (integrator and force stage), checked one step later and rolled back when a rebuild was needed. NVT with a fixed cell only: refused with NPT and for relaxations. Turns pipelined off. Opt-in. pipeline_edge_margin float, ≥ 0 0.0 Pipelined steps pad the force stage to the last checked edge count × (1 + margin), rounded up to the bucket. A margin makes count redos rarer, at the cost of more padded edges every step. pipeline_rebuild_fraction float, > 0 and ≤ 1 0.8 Pipelined steps rebuild the neighbour list early once an atom has moved this fraction of skin / 2. Keeps redos after a late rebuild rare. 1 rebuilds only when the list is invalid. cueq_conv_fusion "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on with the cueq backend, except in reproducible plans; off with hybrid Uses cuEquivariance's fused convolution kernel in plain cuEq models. "on" with hybrid is refused (the hybrid fuses its convolution anyway). "on" with reproducible=True is refused. If FastMACE cannot verify the installed MACE's conversion code, MACE's own rule decides and a different explicit value is refused. first_derivative_only True, False True Compiled cuEq models trace MACE's force function without the graph for second derivatives. Exact. No effect on hybrid models. unfuse_full_addmm True, False True Keeps Inductor from fusing a matrix product with a full-matrix add. Same formulas, different kernel grouping. Compiled models only. dynamo_cache_size_limit int, > 0 64 Raises torch._dynamo's per-function cache limit to this value (never lowers it). Beyond the limit, dynamo silently runs the model uncompiled. Must be at least graph_variant_cap. expandable_segments "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on with torch 2.14 or later on CUDA, unless PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF is set to something without expandable_segments Sets PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True before the first CUDA allocation. This lets the allocator grow memory segments instead of fragmenting them. Off on the CPU. It acts only if set before the process makes its first CUDA allocation: plan before you allocate anything on the GPU. fp64_emulation "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on for float64 plans on CUDA that are not reproducible, on GPUs whose measured float64 rate is below 1/8 of their float32 rate Runs float64 matrix products through cuBLAS's emulation on INT8 tensor cores. On consumer and workstation GPUs (float64 at about 1/64 rate) this was faster per MD step (MH-1 on an RTX 5060 Ti and an RTX 4000 Ada), with products at least as accurate as native float64. Off in float32 plans, on the CPU and on full-rate GPUs (A100, H100). "on" with reproducible=True is refused. The rate is measured with a short probe on the device. If a cuBLAS handle existed before the plan, the products stay native and the build warns. fp64_emulation_mantissa_bits "auto", "dynamic", int 8–128 "auto": 56 for float64 MH-1 plans that are not reproducible, on the GPUs where it was measured faster (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation); "dynamic" elsewhere The mantissa bit count of the emulation (CUBLAS_FIXEDPOINT_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT). "dynamic" lets cuBLAS choose. No effect while fp64_emulation is off. A value set in the environment wins. On the measured GPUs, 56 bits gave MD steps 0.86–0.88 of the time of "dynamic", with the same product errors. empty_cache_before_capture True, False True Releases cached free GPU memory between a stage's warm-up runs and its capture. Lowers peak memory of the graph pool. warmup_in_graph_pool True, False True After the first capture of a stage kind, runs later warm-ups inside the graph memory pool. Keeps warm-up allocations from fragmenting ordinary memory. dynamic_edges True, False True Marks the edge dimension as dynamic from the first compiled call. A new edge count then does not compile the model again. On the graph tier, the first padded capture reuses the first compiled graph, which saves one compile per start (7–9 s with warm compiler caches, 16–22 s cold, on an RTX 5060 Ti). The compiled tier and one-off evaluations always use it. Plans that compile nothing turn it off. Off for PolarMACE with a variable cell on the graph tier. Trajectories are the same with and without it. model_template_cache True, False True Keeps each converted model as a template and gives later plans in the process a private copy, instead of loading and converting the checkpoint again. CUDA with cueq or hybrid only. Saves setup time when one process builds several simulations. overlap_rebuild True, False True On a pipelined fixed-cell step, runs an early neighbour rebuild on a side CUDA stream next to the force stage in flight. Exact. Acts only on pipelined fixed-cell CUDA steps. step_graph True, False False Pipelined steps replay one CUDA graph per step instead of two. Exact. Opt-in. fused_integrator True, False True Fixed-cell Langevin on CUDA runs the integrator stage (half kick, drift, neighbour checks, compaction, flags) as four Triton kernels instead of about 45 PyTorch kernels. Exact: same float64 operations, same order, same noise. Stays on in reproducible plans. NPT, the CPU and installations without Triton use the PyTorch stage. recapture_budget "auto" or int ≥ 0 "auto": graph_variant_cap (64 by default) The number of re-captures one run may make before it warns (RecaptureBudgetWarning), records the step, and the report recommends the compiled tier. The first capture of each graph does not count. 0 warns at the first re-capture. Past the budget, runtime adaptation may switch the run to the compiled tier (see planner reference). graph_variant_cap int ≥ 1, ≤ 64 and ≤ dynamo_cache_size_limit 64 The most captured graph variants kept at once. When full, the least recently replayed one is dropped; capturing it again counts as a re-capture. A lower cap saves GPU memory and makes re-captures more likely.

docs.title: NeighbourConfig
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes skin "auto" or float > 0, Å "auto": 0.3 Å for MD; for runs with MC moves or declared species changes, the skin sized from the workload; for relaxations, 3 × the optimiser's maxstep_A and at least 0.3 Å The neighbour-list skin. The workload rule takes the fastest atom expected at Workload.max_temperature_K (lightest mass, timestep) and sizes the skin so that a rebuild comes about every 16 steps, at least 0.3 Å. Displacement moves add 2 × max_displacement_A. For plain MD the plan records what that rule would give, but keeps 0.3 Å. An explicit value is kept and shown as an override. sort_receivers "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on with the hybrid backend, off with cueq Orders the candidate pairs by receiver atom at every rebuild. The hybrid's streaming convolution and the segmented first-interaction sum need it: turning it off turns them off, and asking for them with it off is refused. gpu_neighbour_list "auto", "on", "off" "auto": on Builds the neighbour list on the GPU instead of with matscipy on the host. Both find the same pairs; only the order within a receiver differs. On a CPU device the list is always built with matscipy. edge_multiple int > 0 256 Edge buffer capacities and bucket sizes are multiples of this. Mostly for alignment. edge_bucket_fraction float ≥ 0 0.05 The bucket size as a fraction of the first edge count, rounded up to edge_multiple. Larger buckets mean fewer graphs and re-captures, and more padded edges per step (at most one bucket). 0 uses buckets of edge_multiple edges. capacity_headroom float ≥ 1 1.15 The pair buffer holds this many times the pairs of the first build. A list that outgrows it is reallocated, which drops the graphs that read it. With headroom="auto" and an MC or species-change workload, the planner sizes it from the skin and the cutoff (at least 1.15). headroom "auto", "fixed" "auto": resolves to "fixed" with capacity_headroom sized for MC and species-change workloads "fixed" uses capacity_headroom and edge_bucket_fraction as given. For plain MD "auto" keeps the given values. The plan always records "fixed" with the value it used. edge_bucket_fraction is never resized. d3_skin "auto" or float > 0, Å "auto": sized for the D3 pair list from the fastest atom and, under a barostat, the expected cell strain The skin of the D3 dispersion pair list, which is separate from the model's list. Read only when the force field has D3. Without D3 the plan records it as unused.

docs.title: When to change these
docs.text:
• Hot MD runs. For plain MD skin="auto" stays at 0.3 Å whatever the temperature. Above about 1000 K, or with light atoms (H, Li) and a long timestep, rebuilds become frequent. Set NeighbourConfig(skin=0.5) or more, and check the rebuild count in the report.
  • Many re-captures. If the report shows a RecaptureBudgetWarning, the edge count moves through many buckets (melting, large volume changes, MC). Try a larger edge_bucket_fraction (for example 0.1) or capacity_headroom (for example 1.3), or plan the compiled tier with mode="compiled". Runtime adaptation may also make that switch for you.
  • Recapture budget. Lower recapture_budget to be told earlier that graphs do not pay off. Raising it above graph_variant_cap has little use: past the cap, graphs are evicted and captured again.
  • Debugging. Run the same structure with mode="eager" (see planner reference). It keeps the backend, rewrites and precision but has no compilation and no CUDA graphs, so errors point at the line that raised them. pipelined="off" checks every step before the next one starts.
  • Memory. Leave expandable_segments="auto". If you set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF yourself, include expandable_segments:True, or the planner leaves the allocator alone. Plan before anything else allocates on the GPU.
  • Comparing backends. Set backend="cueq" or backend="hybrid" explicitly; "auto" may already pick plain cuEq when OpenEquivariance is missing or MACE was imported first. fastmace doctor names the reason.
  • Float64 on consumer GPUs. fp64_emulation="auto" already turns on where it pays. Set "off" to compare against native float64 products.
  • CPU runs (testing only; FastMACE's engines are for NVIDIA GPUs). Pass EngineConfig(device="cpu", compile_mode="none").

docs.title: Environment and cache
docs.text: Every run option is a field of a config record. The few settings on this page are process-wide, so they are environment variables. This page lists each variable FastMACE reads or sets, the cache layout, the file-lock rules and what fastmace doctor checks. Installation is on Install; common problems are in the FAQ.

docs.title: Variables FastMACE reads
docs.text: Variable Values Default What it does FASTMACE_CACHE directory the user cache directory (below) the cache root; must lie outside the Python environment (sys.prefix), else CacheLocationError FASTMACE_MODELS directory unset searched for a label's checkpoint file before <cache root>/models; an empty file there is skipped FASTMACE_SOFT_FILE_LOCKS unset, 1, 0 unset PyTorch's file locks; see File locks on NFS. Any other value raises ValueError at import fastmace FASTMACE_OEQ_PREBUILT unset, 0, 1 unset the prebuilt OpenEquivariance extension (fastmace-oeq-ext): unset uses it when its manifest matches the installed torch, OpenEquivariance and CPython, else builds with the host toolchain; 0 never uses it; 1 refuses the toolchain build, so a mismatch makes the hybrid backend unavailable OEQ_CUDA_DRIVER_LIBRARY path to libcuda.so.1 the usual system locations the CUDA driver library linked into the OpenEquivariance build MAX_JOBS int 4 parallel compile jobs of the OpenEquivariance host build TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR directory $XDG_CACHE_HOME/torch_extensions or ~/.cache/torch_extensions read by fastmace doctor to look for stale build locks; FastMACE sets its own value per process for the OEq build (below) CUDA_CACHE_PATH directory ~/.nv/ComputeCache where the CUDA driver keeps its JIT cache; checked for NFS CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE 0, 1 unset the CUDA driver's JIT cache; if you set it, FastMACE leaves it alone XDG_CACHE_HOME, HOME directory ~/.cache the base of the default cache root on Linux LOCALAPPDATA directory the base of the default cache root on Windows PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF PyTorch's syntax unset if you set it, FastMACE does not change it; see below TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR, TRITON_CACHE_DIR directory under the cache root if you set them, they win over the cache root

docs.title: Variables FastMACE sets
docs.text:
FastMACE sets these in its own process (and so in its child processes). A variable you set yourself is kept, except where the table says otherwise.

Variable Set to When CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE 1 at import fastmace, when the CUDA driver cache lies on NFS and the variable is unset (not with FASTMACE_SOFT_FILE_LOCKS=0); always in fastmace doctor's own process TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR, TRITON_CACHE_DIR <cache root>/inductor, <cache root>/triton before a plan's first compilation, where unset (a value equal to Inductor's own default $TMPDIR/torchinductor_$USER counts as unset) TORCHINDUCTOR_FX_GRAPH_CACHE, ENABLE_AOT_AUTOGRAD_CACHE, TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOGRAD_CACHE 1 with the two above, where unset: the compiled graphs and the compiled force derivative are cached PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF expandable_segments:True before the first CUDA allocation, when EngineConfig.expandable_segments resolves on (torch 2.14 or newer) and the variable is unset CUBLAS_EMULATE_DOUBLE_PRECISION, CUBLAS_EMULATION_STRATEGY 1, eager float64 plans with EngineConfig.fp64_emulation on, where unset CUBLAS_FIXEDPOINT_EMULATION_MANTISSA_BIT_COUNT the plan's mantissa bits with the two above, when fp64_emulation_mantissa_bits resolves to a number, where unset CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG, TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC, CUEQUIVARIANCE_OPS_U1D_ALGOS :4096:8, 1, 1,1 reproducible plans (fm.Workload(reproducible=True)), before CUDA starts; these overwrite CUDA_HOME, CUDA_PATH, CUDACXX, CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER, PYTORCH_NVCC, PATH, CPATH, CXX, OEQ_JIT_EXTENSION, OEQ_NVCC_ATTEMPTS, MAX_JOBS, TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR a stand-in CUDA home under <cache root>/oeq once per process, before the first hybrid model load: OpenEquivariance builds its host extension without nvcc PYTHONPATH the directory holding this fastmace first child processes (the gate's reference, the subprocess runner), so they import the same FastMACE; the runner's children also get RunnerConfig.environment

metadata.json records the OEq build variables under software.oeq_extension for hybrid plans, and the planner records the allocator, emulation and reproducibility settings as plan decisions.

docs.title: Cache layout
docs.text:
The cache root is:

  1. $FASTMACE_CACHE, if set (~ is expanded);
  2. otherwise the user cache directory: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/fastmace or ~/.cache/fastmace on Linux, ~/Library/Caches/fastmace on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%\fastmace\Cache on Windows.

It must not lie inside sys.prefix: environments may be read-only, shared or rebuilt. import fastmace creates nothing; each directory is created when it is first needed. The caches hold generated code and checked downloads only; their keys cover everything that changes the code, so results are the same with a cold or a warm cache. Deleting the cache root is safe while no run is active: the next run rebuilds it.

<cache root>/
├── triton/                  Triton kernels
├── inductor/                torch.compile (Inductor) graphs and the compiled force derivative
├── oeq/                     OpenEquivariance
│   ├── cuda-runtime/        stand-in CUDA home: links to the CUDA 13 runtime wheel and the driver
│   ├── extensions/<key>/    one finished host-extension build per build identity
│   ├── torch-extensions-*/  the per-process TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR, seeded from extensions/
│   └── nvcc-attempts.log    calls to the nvcc stand-in
├── models/                  downloaded checkpoints, each checked against its SHA-256 before it is kept
├── handoff/<run>/           subprocess hand-offs of runs without an output directory
└── gate-*/                  scratch of the gate's reference child, removed when it ends

A compile/ kind is reserved; nothing writes it yet.

The OpenEquivariance host extension is built once per build identity (Python and environment, torch, OpenEquivariance, the CUDA runtime wheel, the compiler and the build variables; never shapes or models). The first process builds it into a staging directory and renames it into place, so the cache needs no lock and may lie on NFS. With the prebuilt fastmace-oeq-ext wheel nothing is built.

docs.title: Model files
docs.text:
fm.load(label) looks for the label's released file name in this order:

  1. checkpoint=, an explicit path;
  2. $FASTMACE_MODELS/<file>;
  3. <cache root>/models/<file>;
  4. with download=True, the official URL, downloaded into <cache root>/models/ and kept only if its SHA-256 matches the label table.

fm.md, fastmace md and fastmace run never download; fetch a model once with fm.load(label, download=True). A path is used as it is. A URL is downloaded into <cache root>/models/ and needs sha256= or trusted=True.

docs.title: File locks on NFS
docs.text:
PyTorch locks its extension builds and its Inductor cache through filelock.FileLock, which on Linux uses kernel locks (fcntl.flock). On an NFS home directory every such lock is a request to the server, and a server can stop accepting a client's lock requests until the mount is reset. The CUDA driver also locks the index file of its JIT cache, hundreds of times per run.

import fastmace therefore:

  • makes filelock.FileLock the soft lock (SoftFileLock), which creates the lock file atomically (O_CREAT | O_EXCL) and sends no lock request;
  • switches the CUDA driver's JIT cache off (CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=1) when it lies on NFS and you have not set CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE. NFS is read from /proc/self/mounts, never with stat, which can hang on a broken mount.

PyTorch binds the lock class when it is imported. So import fastmace must come before import torch (and before anything that imports torch, such as MACE). Importing fastmace imports neither torch nor MACE.

FASTMACE_SOFT_FILE_LOCKS Effect unset soft locks when torch is not imported yet; if torch came first, kernel locks stay and fastmace.runtime_info() reports that the switch came late 1 soft locks; importing fastmace after torch raises RuntimeError 0 kernel locks, and the CUDA driver cache is left alone

fastmace.runtime_info() returns the lock mode ("soft" or "kernel"), how it came about, whether the switch came late, and what happened to the CUDA driver cache. metadata.json records it under runtime.

Stale build locks: a killed torch-extension build leaves a lock file in its build directory, and OpenEquivariance waits up to 300 s for it. FastMACE gives each process a fresh extension directory, so a leftover lock elsewhere does not stall a run. fastmace doctor lists locks older than one hour that no process holds, with the command that removes them.

docs.title: fastmace doctor
docs.text:
fastmace doctor prints one line per check, in this order. A failed required check prints [FAIL] and makes the exit code 1; a failed optional check prints [warn]. Each failed item names its fix. --no-hash skips the SHA-256 of the model files.

Check Required ok when When it fails GPU and driver no torch.cuda.is_available(); shows the GPUs, the driver (from nvidia-smi) and torch's CUDA version no CUDA GPU: MD needs an NVIDIA GPU torch yes torch is installed install a CUDA build of torch MACE yes mace-torch is installed (looked up, not imported); notes a version other than 0.3.16, the qualified one install mace-torch==0.3.16 cuEquivariance yes cuequivariance, cuequivariance_torch and the ops package cuequivariance_ops_torch are installed, and every shared library the ops wheels list is present without the ops package MACE would use the naive kernels; install the ops wheel matching torch's CUDA OpenEquivariance no installed; the prebuilt extension matches, or g++, ninja, the CUDA 13 runtime wheel and libcuda.so.1 are found; shows whether the extension was built before; no stale build lock the hybrid backend is unavailable (plain cuEq runs), or a stale lock is listed with its rm command Triton no Triton is available pip install triton NVRTC no NVRTC is available (it compiles the streaming kernels) install cuda-bindings matching torch's CUDA graph-longrange no installed needed for MACE-POLAR-1: pip install 'fastmace[polar]' torch-dftd no installed needed for the D3 reference: pip install 'fastmace[d3]' cache root yes outside sys.prefix and writable (or its nearest existing parent is); shows where it comes from and whether it exists set FASTMACE_CACHE to a writable directory outside the environment file locks yes not (kernel locks with the cache root on NFS), and not (the CUDA driver cache on NFS and enabled) import fastmace before torch and leave FASTMACE_SOFT_FILE_LOCKS unset or 1; or set CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=1 or CUDA_CACHE_PATH to a local directory model files no every file in $FASTMACE_MODELS and <cache root>/models that has a label-table name matches its SHA-256; files outside the table are listed delete the file and fetch it again with fm.load(label, download=True)

doctor changes nothing. It looks MACE and OpenEquivariance up without importing them (importing either builds OEq's host extension), reads the cuEquivariance ops wheels' metadata without importing them (the import creates a Triton cache directory), creates no cache directory, and deletes no lock. So an ops library that is present but does not load shows only at the first model load. A check that crashes is reported as failed, with the hint to run fastmace --debug doctor.

Without a GPU, the GPU check is a warning. On a CPU-only machine the exit code is usually 1 all the same, because the cuEquivariance ops wheel is missing.

docs.title: Integrators and optimisers
docs.text:
This page lists every integrator record in fm.integrators, every optimiser record in fm.optimize, and the two config records they map onto, IntegratorConfig and OptimizerConfig. For worked examples see NPT and D3 and Relaxations and quenches. The generated API pages are Integrators and Optimisers.

All records are frozen dataclasses with keyword-only arguments. They are checked when they are built, so a wrong value raises ValueError before any model is loaded. Each record ports one ASE 3.27 class, and every one of them runs inside the CUDA-graph engine: the choice of integrator does not move a run to a slower tier. What the planner refuses is listed under Constraints and refusals.

docs.title: Which integrator?
docs.text:
Record Ensemble ASE 3.27 class Use it for Notes Langevin NVT Langevin Production NVT; fm.md's default Stochastic. Takes FixAtoms. LangevinBAOAB NPT LangevinBAOAB Production NPT; fm.md's ensemble="NPT" Stochastic thermostat and barostat. Experimental. NVE NVE VelocityVerlet Energy conservation checks, microcanonical runs No thermostat. fm.md's ensemble="NVE". CSVR NVT Bussi Canonical NVT with little disturbance of the dynamics Stochastic velocity rescaling. Takes FixAtoms. NoseHooverChain NVT NoseHooverChainNVT Deterministic canonical NVT No FixAtoms. MTK NPT IsotropicMTKNPT, MTKNPT Deterministic NPT Experimental. No FixAtoms. Berendsen NVT or NPT NVTBerendsen, NPTBerendsen, Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen Equilibration only Not canonical; the report says so.

Every NPT run has an "experimental: not yet qualified" line in its report.

docs.title: Common conventions
docs.text:
Units. Time in fs, temperature in K, pressure and stress in GPa, lengths in Å. The friction of the Langevin records is per fs.

Temperature target. temperature_K is the target at the start. A schedule (Simulation.run(schedule=...), fm.md(schedule=...)) moves the target every step; see Schedules.

Time constants have no defaults. CSVR, Nose-Hoover, MTK and Berendsen need their time constants stated, as in ASE. FastMACE never chooses a physical time constant for you. The exception is LangevinBAOAB's barostat time constant, which follows ASE's default.

Seed. The records take no seed. The Simulation's seed= seeds the noise of the stochastic schemes (Langevin, LangevinBAOAB, CSVR).

Friction units. friction_per_fs is the friction coefficient γ in 1/fs. ASE's Langevin(friction=...) takes it in inverse ASE time units; the record converts with friction_per_fs / ase.units.fs. fm.md uses 0.02 per ASE time unit, which is 0.001965 per fs (a velocity relaxation time 1/γ of about 509 fs). To pass ASE's value, convert it: friction_per_fs = friction_ase * ase.units.fs.

docs.title: fixcm: centre-of-mass motion
docs.text:
Value Meaning "auto" Off when the structure has FixAtoms (the fixed atoms pin the frame already), on otherwise. The default of Langevin, NVE, CSVR and Berendsen. True Remove the total momentum at the start and keep it at zero. Refused with FixAtoms. False Leave the centre of mass free.

NoseHooverChain, MTK and LangevinBAOAB take True or False only, default True, because they refuse FixAtoms anyway.

docs.title: dof: degrees of freedom
docs.text:
dof sets the number of kinetic degrees of freedom N_f that the scheme uses for its target kinetic energy (CSVR, Berendsen, Nose-Hoover, MTK) and for the reported temperature (all schemes). N is the number of atoms, n_fixed the number of fixed atoms.

Value N_f "fastmace" 3(N − n_fixed) with FixAtoms; 3N − 3 under fixcm; 3N otherwise. "ase" The count of the ASE class: 3(N − n_fixed) for VelocityVerlet, Bussi and the Berendsen classes; 3N for NoseHooverChainNVT and the MTK classes. "auto" (default) "fastmace".

With dof="ase" and fixcm=False, the arithmetic is ASE's. The Langevin records have no dof argument. Their count is 3(N − n_fixed) with FixAtoms, 3N − 3 for Langevin with fixcm on and the mass-weighted projection (the default), and 3N otherwise (so 3N for LangevinBAOAB).

docs.title: fm.integrators.Langevin
docs.text:
Langevin NVT, ASE's Langevin. Fixed cell.

fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=0.5, temperature_K=300, friction_per_fs=0.002)
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 0.5 MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Thermostat target at the start. A schedule moves it. friction_per_fs 1/fs, > 0 required Friction γ. fm.md uses 0.001965/fs. fixcm "auto", True, False "auto" Remove centre-of-mass motion. See fixcm. fixcm_projection "auto", "ase", "mass_weighted" "auto" How fixcm removes the centre-of-mass part of the noise. See below.

fixcm_projection only matters with fixcm on:

  • "ase": ASE's projection, bit for bit with ASE's noise stream. It subtracts the plain mean of the random displacements and scales by sqrt(N/(N − 1)). It is canonical only when all masses are equal: with unequal masses, heavy and light species settle at slightly different temperatures.
  • "mass_weighted": the Gaussian noise conditioned on a fixed centre of mass, with mass-weighted means. It is canonical with 3N − 3 degrees of freedom for every species and every mass ratio.
  • "auto": "mass_weighted" under NVT with fixcm on, "ase" otherwise. The plan records the choice.

Use "ase" only to compare trajectories with ASE's Langevin.

docs.title: fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB
docs.text:
Langevin-Hoover NPT, ASE 3.27's LangevinBAOAB: BAOAB Langevin dynamics for the atoms (Leimkuhler and Matthews 2013) and a Langevin-Hoover barostat for the cell (Quigley and Probert 2004).

fm.integrators.LangevinBAOAB(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=300, friction_per_fs=0.002,
                             pressure_GPa=0.0, cell_mode="hydrostatic")
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 0.5 MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Thermostat target at the start. A schedule moves it. friction_per_fs 1/fs, > 0 required Thermostat friction γ. ASE's T_tau is 1/γ. With fm.md's 0.001965/fs, T_tau ≈ 509 fs. pressure_GPa GPa 0.0 Hydrostatic target pressure. Exclusive with external_stress_GPa. external_stress_GPa GPa: a scalar or six Voigt components (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy) None Target stress in ASE's externalstress sign (positive is tensile). None means −pressure_GPa on the diagonal. Giving both this and a non-zero pressure_GPa raises ValueError. cell_mode "hydrostatic", "full" "hydrostatic" "hydrostatic": cell shape fixed, volume free (ASE hydrostatic=True). "full": fully flexible cell. barostat_tau_fs fs, > 0, or None None Barostat time constant, ASE's P_tau. None is ASE's default, 20 T_tau (about 10.2 ps with fm.md's friction). barostat_mass_factor > 0 1.0 Factor on ASE's heuristic barostat mass, ASE's P_mass_factor. ASE's mass gives a cell period of about P_tau/4. disable_cell_langevin bool False No friction and noise on the cell degrees of freedom. As ASE. fixcm False False BAOAB does not remove centre-of-mass motion; True is refused. See the note below. max_volume_ratio > 1, or None 20.0 Stop with CellDivergedError once the volume leaves [V0/ratio, V0·ratio]. V0 is the starting volume. None turns the check off. max_cell_length_A Å, > 0, or None 1000.0 Stop with CellDivergedError once a cell vector is longer than this. float32 coordinates still resolve 6e-5 Å at 1000 Å.

The cell-divergence stop writes the restart and metadata first. Without it, a vapour at low pressure expands without bound until the coordinates lose their precision.

fixcm in LangevinBAOAB. ASE's LangevinBAOAB does not remove the centre-of-mass motion, and neither does FastMACE's port, so the record takes fixcm=False only. MC moves under BAOAB therefore treat the run as one without a fixed centre of mass (see MC). A restart written before this rule, which recorded fixcm=True, resumes with False; its dynamics were the same.

The drag term in the full-cell barostat is the corrected one. ASE 3.27's variant, which applies a trace term to all nine drag elements, stays an IntegratorConfig field (ase_trace_drag_all_elements) for comparisons with ASE only.

docs.title: fm.integrators.NVE
docs.text:
Velocity Verlet, ASE's VelocityVerlet. The conserved quantity is E_kin + E_pot. fm.md(ensemble="NVE") builds it and starts from the structure's momenta; it draws no velocities.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 required MD timestep. fixcm "auto", True, False "auto" Remove the total momentum at the start and project it out after each kick. ASE's class has no fixcm; it stops float drift of the force sum from accumulating. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" Count for the reported temperature. See dof.

With FixAtoms, the step is ASE's constrained step: the fixed atoms' forces and velocities are zero, and the free atoms' velocities are recomputed from their displacement, as VelocityVerlet.step does.

docs.title: fm.integrators.CSVR
docs.text:
Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling (Bussi, Donadio and Parrinello, J. Chem. Phys. 126, 014101 (2007)), ASE 3.27's Bussi. At the start of each step the velocities are scaled by a stochastic factor, then one velocity Verlet step follows. The noise is ASE's stream from the Simulation's seed. The conserved quantity is E_kin + E_pot minus the energy the thermostat transferred, as ASE's transferred_energy.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 required MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Target at the start. A schedule moves it. tau_fs fs, > 0 required Thermostat time constant, ASE's taut. Larger values disturb the dynamics less. fixcm "auto", True, False "auto" Centre-of-mass motion. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" N_f of the target kinetic energy kT·N_f/2.

docs.title: fm.integrators.NoseHooverChain
docs.text:
Nose-Hoover chains, ASE 3.27's NoseHooverChainNVT (Martyna, Klein and Tuckerman 1992). Deterministic. The conserved quantity is E_pot + E_kin plus the thermostat energy, as ASE's get_conserved_energy.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 required MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Target at the start. Also sets the thermostat masses; see below. tdamp_fs fs, > 0 required Thermostat damping time, ASE's tdamp. ASE suggests about 100 timesteps. tchain int ≥ 1 3 Thermostats in the chain, ASE's tchain. tloop int ≥ 1 1 Suzuki-Yoshida sub-loops per half step, ASE's tloop. fixcm bool True Remove the total momentum at the start and after every step. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" N_f in the first thermostat mass, its force and its energy. ASE uses 3N.

The thermostat masses come from the construction temperature, as in ASE. A schedule changes the target kT, not the masses.

docs.title: fm.integrators.MTK
docs.text:
Martyna-Tobias-Klein NPT with Nose-Hoover chains on the atoms and on the cell, ASE 3.27's IsotropicMTKNPT (cell_mode="hydrostatic") and MTKNPT (cell_mode="full"). Deterministic. Experimental: not yet qualified. The conserved quantity is E_pot + E_kin plus the thermostat and barostat energies, the cell kinetic energy and P·V, as ASE's get_conserved_energy.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 required MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Target at the start. Sets the thermostat masses. pressure_GPa GPa required Target pressure, ASE's pressure_au in GPa. tdamp_fs fs, > 0 required Thermostat damping time, ASE's tdamp. pdamp_fs fs, > 0 required Barostat damping time, ASE's pdamp. ASE suggests about 1000 timesteps. tchain int ≥ 1 3 Thermostat chain length. pchain int ≥ 1 3 Barostat chain length. tloop int ≥ 1 1 Thermostat sub-loops. ploop int ≥ 1 1 Barostat sub-loops. cell_mode "hydrostatic", "full" "hydrostatic" "hydrostatic": isotropic strain, cell = cell0·exp(ε). "full": 3×3 cell momentum. fixcm bool True Remove the total momentum at the start and after every step. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" N_f in every coupling term (thermostat mass, drag 1 + d/N_f, barostat mass). "ase" with fixcm=False is ASE's arithmetic.

ASE 3.27's own inconsistencies in these classes are ported as they are; the reference is ASE.

docs.title: fm.integrators.Berendsen
docs.text:
Berendsen thermostat and barostat (Berendsen et al., J. Chem. Phys. 81, 3684 (1984)). Not canonical: use it for equilibration only. The plan warns and the report says "non-canonical: equilibration only".

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes timestep_fs fs, > 0 required MD timestep. temperature_K K, ≥ 0 required Target at the start. taut_fs fs, > 0 required Thermostat time constant, ASE's taut. The velocity scale per step is clamped to [0.9, 1.1], as in ASE. pressure_GPa GPa, or None None Target pressure. None is NVT (NVTBerendsen). A pressure needs taup_fs and compressibility_per_GPa. taup_fs fs, > 0, or None None Barostat time constant, ASE's taup. Needs pressure_GPa. compressibility_per_GPa 1/GPa, > 0, or None None Compressibility κ, ASE's compressibility_au in 1/GPa. Needs pressure_GPa. No default, as in ASE. mask three 0/1 flags, or None None None: the whole cell is scaled (NPTBerendsen). Flags: each cell vector is scaled on its own where its flag is 1 (Inhomogeneous_NPTBerendsen); the angles stay. Needs pressure_GPa. fixcm "auto", True, False "auto" Subtract the mean momentum after the first kick, as ASE. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" N_f of the kinetic temperature.

One deviation from ASE: ASE's NPT step evaluates the forces twice per step, because the cell scaling invalidates its cache. FastMACE makes one force call per step, so the first kick uses the previous step's forces at the unscaled cell. The difference is of order dt·κ·|P0 − P|/τ_P in one half kick. NVT Berendsen is ASE's step exactly.

docs.title: Constraints and refusals
docs.text:
Only FixAtoms is supported; any other ASE constraint is refused.

Record FixAtoms fixcm=True with FixAtoms MC moves Langevin yes refused yes, without constraints NVE yes refused yes, without constraints CSVR yes refused yes, without constraints Berendsen NVT only refused yes, without constraints NoseHooverChain refused (ASE's class has no constraints, so there is no reference) — yes LangevinBAOAB, MTK refused (no variable cell with fixed atoms) — swaps and transmutations; no displacements

MC moves with any constraint are refused. A refusal raises PlanRefused with every reason before the first step.

docs.title: IntegratorConfig
docs.text:
fastmace.config.IntegratorConfig is the integrator's internal settings record. You do not build it: every fm.integrators record turns into one (record.to_config(seed=...)) when the Simulation is created, and Simulation(integrator=...) takes records only. The fields show up in the plan, in metadata.json and in restart files. Units: fs, GPa, and the friction in inverse ASE time units (not 1/fs as on the records).

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes ensemble "nve", "nvt", "npt" "nvt" The ensemble. "npt" means a variable cell and a stress calculation. scheme "langevin", "baoab", "nve", "csvr", "nhc", "mtk", "berendsen", or None None The registered scheme the planner builds. None resolves from the ensemble: nvt → langevin, npt → baoab, nve → nve. dof "auto", "fastmace", "ase" "auto" Degrees-of-freedom convention. The Langevin schemes ignore it. parameters (name, value) pairs () Scheme settings (time constants, chain lengths, the Berendsen mask) in the record's units. Sorted by name. timestep_fs fs, > 0 0.5 MD timestep. friction inverse ASE time units, > 0 0.02 Langevin friction. NPT uses T_tau = 1/friction. The records convert friction_per_fs. Unused by other schemes. seed int ≥ 0 20261001 Noise seed. Always the Simulation's seed when built from a record. fixcm bool True Remove centre-of-mass motion. Resolved from the record's "auto". fixcm_projection "auto", "ase", "mass_weighted" "auto" Langevin's projection of the noise under fixcm. The planner resolves "auto". noise_batch int > 0 256 Steps of random numbers drawn and copied to the GPU at once. Same numbers in the same order for any value. Not set by any record. pressure_GPa GPa 0.0 NPT target pressure (ASE externalstress = −pressure). cell_mode "hydrostatic", "full" "hydrostatic" NPT cell mode. barostat_tau_fs fs, > 0, or None None BAOAB's P_tau. None: 20 T_tau. barostat_mass_factor > 0 1.0 Factor on ASE's barostat mass. ase_trace_drag_all_elements bool False Full cell: ASE 3.27's trace term on all nine drag elements. For comparisons with ASE only. Not set by any record. temperature_K K, ≥ 0, or None None Thermostat target at the start. The records always set it, except NVE. external_stress_GPa GPa: scalar or six Voigt components, or None None NPT target stress, ASE sign. Exclusive with a non-zero pressure_GPa. disable_cell_langevin bool False BAOAB: no friction and noise on the cell.

docs.title: Optimisers: fm.optimize
docs.text:
The optimisers are ASE 3.27's LBFGS and FIRE on the graph engine, with ASE's arguments and defaults. Lengths are in Å. A relaxation is a Simulation built with optimizer= instead of integrator=:

opt = fm.optimize.FIRE(cell_filter=fm.optimize.FrechetCell(scalar_pressure_GPa=0.0))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, model, optimizer=opt, seed=0)
relaxed, summary = sim.relax(fmax=0.01, steps=5000)

docs.title: Convergence: fmax and steps
docs.text: Simulation.relax(fmax=0.05, steps=100_000_000) is ASE's Optimizer.run(fmax=, steps=). The run converges when the largest per-atom force norm (after constraints) is below fmax, in eV/Å. With a cell filter the cell rows count too, as in ASE. Convergence is checked before the first step, so a converged start takes no step. At most steps steps follow, one force call each. A second relax call continues with the optimiser's history. The summary records the steps, whether it converged, the per-step energies and maximum forces, and the neighbour-list rebuilds.

docs.title: fm.optimize.LBFGS
docs.text:
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes maxstep_A Å, > 0 0.2 Largest atom displacement per step, ASE's maxstep. memory int ≥ 1 100 Number of steps kept in the history. damping > 0 1.0 Scale on the step. alpha eV/Å², > 0 70.0 Initial guess of the Hessian, α·I. cell_filter None, FrechetCell(...) None None keeps the cell fixed.

ASE's use_line_search is not offered.

docs.title: fm.optimize.FIRE
docs.text:
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes dt ASE time units, > 0 0.1 Initial timestep. 0.1 ASE time units ≈ 1.02 fs. A step-size parameter, as in ASE. maxstep_A Å, > 0 0.2 Largest atom displacement per step, ASE's maxstep. dtmax ASE time units, > 0 1.0 Largest timestep. ≈ 10.2 fs. Nmin int ≥ 0 5 Downhill steps before the timestep may grow. finc > 0 1.1 Timestep growth factor. fdec > 0 0.5 Timestep shrink factor after an uphill step. astart > 0 0.1 Mixing parameter α after a restart. fa > 0 0.99 Factor on α per downhill step. a ≥ 0 0.1 Initial mixing parameter α. downhill_check bool False Reject a step that raises the energy and go back, as ASE. cell_filter None, FrechetCell(...) None None keeps the cell fixed.

ASE's deprecated maxmove and position_reset_callback are not offered.

docs.title: fm.optimize.FrechetCell
docs.text:
ASE 3.27's FrechetCellFilter on the GPU. The degrees of freedom are the positions in the original cell and the matrix logarithm of the deformation gradient; both optimisers run on them unchanged. A step that would strain the cell by more than about 65 % per element is not applied, and the relaxation stops with a failure reason.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes scalar_pressure_GPa GPa 0.0 External hydrostatic pressure, ASE's scalar_pressure in GPa. The energy becomes E + P·V. hydrostatic_strain bool False Only isotropic strain: the cell shape stays. constant_volume bool False Keep the volume fixed. mask six Voigt 0/1 flags or a 3×3 of 0/1 flags, or None None Which strain components may change, as ASE. exp_cell_factor > 0, or None None Scale between the cell and position degrees of freedom. None is N, the number of atoms (ASE's default).

FixAtoms with a cell filter is refused. PolarMACE with a cell filter is refused: relax PolarMACE structures at fixed cell.

docs.title: OptimizerConfig
docs.text:
fastmace.config.OptimizerConfig is the optimiser's internal settings record. You do not build it: LBFGS(...).to_config() and FIRE(...).to_config() produce it when the Simulation is created. The fmax and steps of Simulation.relax replace the config's values at run time.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes scheme "lbfgs", "fire" required The optimiser. parameters (name, value) pairs () The record's settings, in its units. Sorted by name. cell_filter None, "frechet" None None keeps the cell fixed. cell_filter_parameters (name, value) pairs () FrechetCell's settings. Needs a cell_filter. fmax eV/Å, > 0 0.05 Convergence threshold on the largest force. relax(fmax=) overrides it. steps int ≥ 0 100,000,000 Most optimiser steps (ASE's run default). relax(steps=) overrides it.

docs.title: Command line and protocol files
docs.text: fastmace relax and the [relax] and [quench] tables of protocol files take optimiser names: gpu-LBFGS (default) and gpu-FIRE run these records on the graph engine; ase-LBFGS and ase-BFGS run ASE's own optimisers on FastMACE's calculator; bare LBFGS and BFGS mean the ASE ones. See Relaxations and quenches.

docs.title: Monte Carlo moves
docs.text:
This page lists every move record in fm.mc, how moves attach to an MD run, and the MCConfig limits. For worked examples see Monte Carlo and swaps. The generated API page is Monte Carlo.

Experimental

MC moves are not yet qualified. Every run with MC has an "MC: experimental: not yet qualified" line in its report.

docs.title: How hybrid MD/MC works
docs.text:
A run with MC alternates MD steps and blocks of MC attempts. A move with every=100 and attempts=50 runs a block of 50 attempts after every simulation step that is a multiple of 100. When several moves are due at the same step, they run in the order they were attached.

Each attempt is: propose, apply the trial, evaluate the energy, accept or reject, and restore the old state where rejected. All of it runs as device operations inside a captured CUDA graph, so an attempt costs one energy evaluation and no re-capture. The forces are recomputed once at the end of a block that accepted anything.

Acceptance. The Metropolis rule at the thermostat's current target temperature T: accept if ln u < −ΔE / (k_B T), with u uniform in [0, 1). For a transmutation the exponent uses ΔE − Σ Δμ_s ΔN_s, the semi-grand canonical excess. A NaN energy rejects. T is the target at the start of the block, so it follows a schedule.

Energy precision. The MC energy is evaluated in the force precision when the plan's move-energy gate passes, else in float64. The gate threshold is 0.01 k_B T_min, with T_min the workload's min_mc_temperature_K. Set fm.Workload(mc_energy_precision="float32" | "float64") to choose it yourself.

Counters. Each move counts attempted, impossible (a swap whose species are not both present, for example) and accepted. The thermo output has mc_<move>_attempted and mc_<move>_accepted columns, and the counters survive restarts.

docs.title: fm.mc.Swap
docs.text:
Swap the species of two atoms. A pair type is chosen uniformly from pairs, then one atom of each of its two species uniformly.

fm.mc.Swap(pairs=[("O", "Cl")], every=100, attempts=50)
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes pairs sequence of pairs of species (symbols or atomic numbers) required The species pairs that may swap. At least one pair; each pair names two different species. every MD steps, int ≥ 1 required Block interval. attempts int ≥ 1 required Attempts per block. At most 10,000. velocities "exchange", "rescale", "redraw", "redraw_all" "exchange" Momentum treatment of the two atoms after an accepted swap. See Velocity treatments.

With a model that reads per-atom charges, the charges move with the species.

docs.title: fm.mc.Transmute
docs.text:
Change one atom's species within a transmutable set: semi-grand canonical MC. One atom whose species is in the set is chosen uniformly, and a new species is drawn uniformly from the rest of the set.
