fm.mc.Transmute(species=("Na", "K"), every=100, attempts=20, mu={"K": -0.15})
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes species sequence of species (symbols or atomic numbers) required The transmutable set. At least two different species. every MD steps, int ≥ 1 required Block interval. attempts int ≥ 1 required Attempts per block. At most 10,000. velocities None, "rescale", "redraw", "redraw_all" None Momentum treatment of the changed atom. None: "redraw_all" when the integrator fixes the centre of mass, "rescale" otherwise. "exchange" is for swaps only. mu mapping species → eV None Configurational chemical-potential differences Δμ_s, against a reference species. Species left out have 0. Keys must be in species. formal_charges mapping species → int None Formal charge q_s of each species, for the charge and spin parity rule. Species left out have 0.

Chemical potentials. mu takes configurational differences. To convert full chemical-potential differences (which include the kinetic part), use

mu = fm.mc.configurational_mu({"K": -0.20}, temperature_K=600, reference="Na")

which returns Δμ_s^conf = Δμ_s^full + (3/2) k_B T ln(m_s / m_ref) for each key. masses= (amu, by species) replaces ASE's standard atomic masses. The reference's own entry, if given, must be 0.

Charge and spin. For a model that reads charges or a total charge or spin (PolarMACE, MACE-OMOL-0), every pair of species in the set must have ΔZ − Δq even, so that the spin multiplicity stays valid. Give formal_charges to make it so; otherwise the move is refused with ChargeParityRefused. For other models the rule does not apply.

docs.title: fm.mc.Displace
docs.text:
Move one atom, chosen uniformly, to a uniform point in a sphere of radius δ around it. The proposal is symmetric, so the acceptance is plain Metropolis on ΔE. Momenta are not changed.

fm.mc.Displace(delta_A=0.1, every=10, attempts=100)
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes delta_A Å, > 0 required Sphere radius δ, and the largest δ an adaptive move may reach. At most the workload's max_displacement_A. every MD steps, int ≥ 1 required Block interval. attempts int ≥ 1 required Attempts per block. At most 10,000. adaptive bool False Tune δ at the end of every block toward 30 % acceptance. See below.

With adaptive=True, after each block δ ← δ · clamp(acceptance / 0.3, 0.5, 2), capped at delta_A and at max_displacement_A. Every value is recorded, and the restart keeps the current one. A changing δ breaks detailed balance, so use an adaptive move for equilibration and a fixed one for sampling.

Displacements need fm.Workload(max_displacement_A=...), because the neighbour-list skin is sized for them (2δ is added to the skin). They are refused with a variable cell (NPT). fm.md sets max_displacement_A to the largest delta_A of its Displace moves; with fm.Simulation, pass it in the Workload.

An attempt that would need a neighbour-list rebuild, or more edges than the captured graph holds, is redone on the host with the same random numbers. The outcome is the same; only that attempt is slower.

docs.title: Velocity treatments
docs.text:
A swap or transmutation changes atomic masses. The momentum treatment says what the velocities of the changed atoms become after an accepted move. v is the velocity, m the mass, z a standard normal vector.

Value Moves What it does Conserves "exchange" swaps The two atoms exchange velocities with their species: v_i' = v_j, v_j' = v_i. Kinetic energy and total momentum. "rescale" swaps, transmutations Keep each atom's kinetic energy: v' = v · sqrt(m_old / m_new). Kinetic energy, not total momentum. "redraw" swaps, transmutations Draw the changed atoms' velocities from Maxwell-Boltzmann at T with the new masses: v' = sqrt(k_B T / m_new) · z. Neither. "redraw_all" swaps, transmutations Once per block with an acceptance, draw every velocity from Maxwell-Boltzmann at T and project to zero total momentum. Total momentum (zero).

The integrator's centre-of-mass setting limits the choice:

  • With fixcm on, "rescale" and "redraw" are refused, because they change the total momentum behind the integrator's back. Use "exchange" (swaps) or "redraw_all".
  • "redraw_all" under fixcm draws (3N − 3)·k_B T of kinetic energy. It needs the Langevin noise projection fixcm_projection="mass_weighted", which is what "auto" gives under NVT Langevin with fixcm on. LangevinBAOAB never fixes the centre of mass (fixcm=False), so its moves follow the rules without fixcm.

docs.title: Random numbers and seeds
docs.text: MC uses three counter-based random streams (Philox4x32-10): proposal, acceptance and velocity. Their seeds are fixed 63-bit values derived by SHA-256 from the Simulation's seed, distinct from the integrator's noise seed. Every attempt consumes a fixed count of numbers from each stream, whatever its outcome, so a number is a function of the seed and its position only. The numbers are the same on the CPU and the GPU. A stream's state is its seed and offset, which the restart stores; a resumed run continues the same streams.

docs.title: fm.md
docs.text:
fm.md(..., mc=...) takes one move record or a sequence of them. It infers the species superset (the structure's species plus every species the moves name) and the workload from mc=.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes mc an fm.mc record or a sequence of them None The move set. Refused with ensemble="NVE". min_mc_temperature_K K, > 0 None The lowest target at which MC blocks run, and T_min of the energy gate. Without a schedule: defaults to temperature_K, which must be positive. With a schedule: required.

With a schedule, the move set is attached only over the step ranges whose target is at or above min_mc_temperature_K, and detached elsewhere. The report and metadata.json record the ranges.

docs.title: fm.Simulation
docs.text:
sim.run(steps=..., mc=...) attaches a move set. It stays attached until a later run passes another mc= or mc=None. The workload must declare the moves up front, because the plan and its gate are built for them:

workload = fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=1000, species_changes=True,
                       mc_moves=("swap",), min_mc_temperature_K=250)
Workload field Needed for mc_moves Every move type you will attach ("swap", "transmute", "displace"). An undeclared move is refused. species_changes=True Swaps and transmutations. min_mc_temperature_K Any MC. A block whose target falls below it is refused. max_displacement_A Displacements. mc_energy_precision Optional: "auto" (default), "float32" or "float64".

The ForceField's species= must contain every species a move can create; a species outside it raises SpeciesNotInSuperset. MC with any constraint, FixAtoms included, is refused.

docs.title: TOML
docs.text:
One [[mc]] table per move, with move = "swap", "transmute" or "displace" and the record's fields:

[[mc]]
move = "swap"
pairs = [["O", "Cl"]]
every = 100
attempts = 50
velocities = "exchange"

docs.title: MCConfig
docs.text:
fastmace.config.MCConfig holds the limits of the MC driver. A Simulation always uses the defaults; fm.md, Simulation and the TOML files take no MCConfig. A move set over a limit raises ValueError when it is attached.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes max_attempts_per_block int ≥ 1 10,000 The largest attempts of one move. The captured attempt is replayed at most this often per block. max_move_sets int ≥ 1 8 The most move records attached at once.

docs.title: Models, force fields, dispersion and schedules
docs.text: This page lists the model label table, the arguments of fm.load and fm.ForceField, the fm.D3 dispersion record, the PolarMACE options in PolarConfig, and the temperature schedules of fm.protocols. For advice on which model to use see Models and licences; for D3 in practice see NPT and D3. The generated API pages are Models and force fields, Dispersion (D3) and Protocols and schedules.

docs.title: The label table
docs.text:
A label names one released checkpoint and, for a multi-head checkpoint, one head. Each label's file has a fixed SHA-256; a file that does not match is not loaded. fastmace models prints the table with file names and hashes, the licence texts and the aliases; it reads no file and downloads nothing.

Label Head Model Training functional Licence File mp0-medium — MACE-MP-0 medium PBE (PBE+U) MIT 2023-12-03-mace-128-L1_epoch-199.model mp0-large — MACE-MP-0 large PBE (PBE+U) MIT MACE_MPtrj_2022.9.model mp0b3-medium default MACE-MP-0b3 medium PBE (PBE+U) MIT mace-mp-0b3-medium.model mpa0-medium default MACE-MPA-0 medium PBE (PBE+U) MIT mace-mpa-0-medium.model omat0-medium default MACE-OMAT-0 medium PBE (PBE+U) ASL mace-omat-0-medium.model matpes-pbe default MACE-MatPES-PBE-0 PBE (no U) ASL MACE-matpes-pbe-omat-ft.model matpes-r2scan default MACE-MatPES-r2SCAN-0 r2SCAN ASL MACE-matpes-r2scan-omat-ft.model mh1-omat omat_pbe MACE-MH-1 PBE (PBE+U), OMat24 ASL mace-mh-1.model mh1-mp mp_pbe_refit_add MACE-MH-1 PBE (PBE+U), MPTraj ASL mace-mh-1.model mh1-r2scan matpes_r2scan MACE-MH-1 r2SCAN ASL mace-mh-1.model polar1-s Default MACE-POLAR-1 S (PolarMACE) unknown ASL MACE-POLAR-1-S.model polar1-m Default MACE-POLAR-1 M (PolarMACE) unknown ASL MACE-POLAR-1-M.model polar1-l Default MACE-POLAR-1 L (PolarMACE) unknown ASL MACE-POLAR-1-L.model omol0-xl omol MACE-OMOL-0 extra large ωB97M-V (includes VV10 dispersion) ASL MACE-omol-0-extra-large-1024.model off23-small — MACE-OFF23 small ωB97M-D3(BJ) ASL MACE-OFF23_small.model off23-medium — MACE-OFF23 medium ωB97M-D3(BJ) ASL MACE-OFF23_medium.model off23-large — MACE-OFF23 large ωB97M-D3(BJ) ASL MACE-OFF23_large.model off23b-medium — MACE-OFF23b medium ωB97M-D3(BJ) ASL MACE-OFF23b_medium.model off24-medium — MACE-OFF24 medium ωB97M-D3(BJ) ASL MACE-OFF24_medium.model

"—" means a single-head checkpoint whose head has no name. ASL is the Academic Software License (non-commercial use only); MIT is the MIT License. The weights' licence binds you independently of FastMACE's own. FastMACE shows each checkpoint's licence once per process as a ModelLicenceWarning.

Aliases. mh1 (the MACE-MH-1 checkpoint) and omol0 (MACE-OMOL-0) take head=. The checkpoint names (mh-1, omol-0-xl, and so on) work the same way. A multi-head checkpoint without head= raises ValueError listing its heads; there is no default head.

MACE-MH-1 heads.

Head Training data and functional Own label matpes_r2scan MatPES, r2SCAN mh1-r2scan mp_pbe_refit_add MPTraj, PBE/PBE+U mh1-mp omat_pbe OMat24, PBE/PBE+U mh1-omat oc20_usemppbe OC20 subset, PBE — spice_wB97M SPICE, ωB97M-D3(BJ) — omol OMol25 subset, ωB97M-V —

The training functional decides what dispersion="d3bj" expands to (see D3).

Known issues. The plan and the report warn, without refusing, when a model meets a structure it is known to handle badly:

Model Condition Warning polar1-s structure contains Na, Nb and O Fukui charge runaway on NaNbO3 polar1-s, polar1-m, polar1-l Na, Ta and O huge forces and pressures on NaTaO3 omol0-xl Na and Cl outside its training domain; collapses in NaCl MD omol0-xl O in an inorganic structure outside its training domain on dense oxides off23-small, off23-medium, off23-large, off23b-medium variable cell relaxes molecular crystals to 5.5-9.2 % below the experimental volume; OFF24-medium is closest off23-large 2,000 atoms or more may need more than 16 GB in some engines

docs.title: fm.load
docs.text:
model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
model = fm.load("/data/my.model", sha256="9f65...")

fm.load returns the checkpoint as a pristine model: MACE's e3nn modules in float64 on the CPU. Each plan converts its own copy to the chosen backend, precision and device; the pristine model is never changed.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes source label, alias, checkpoint name, path or URL required The checkpoint to load. First positional argument. head head name None The head of a multi-head checkpoint. A label fixes its head; a different head= raises ValueError. sha256 hex string None The expected SHA-256 of the file. Must match the file. Lets a path or URL load. trusted bool False Load a file without a stated hash. Also loads a label's file whose hash differs from the table. download bool False Fetch a missing file into the models cache. The hash is checked before the file is kept. charge int None Total charge for a model with a total-charge embedding (MACE-OMOL-0). OMOL-0's range is −100 to 100. Raises ValueError for a model without that embedding. spin_multiplicity int None Spin multiplicity for a model with a total-spin embedding (MACE-OMOL-0). Raises ValueError for a model without that embedding. checkpoint path None An explicit file for a label. The label's hash still applies.

Where a label's file is found, in order:

  1. checkpoint=, if given;
  2. $FASTMACE_MODELS/<file>;
  3. <cache root>/models/<file>, where the cache root is $FASTMACE_CACHE, else the user cache directory (~/.cache/fastmace on Linux);
  4. with download=True, the label's official release URL, downloaded into <cache root>/models/.

Otherwise FileNotFoundError names the places searched.

Trust. MACE checkpoints are Python pickles, which run code when they are loaded. The SHA-256 is computed before anything is unpickled:

Source Loads when A label the file's hash matches the table, or trusted=True A path sha256= matches, or trusted=True A URL sha256= is given (checked on download) or trusted=True; refused before any download otherwise. The URL needs download=True unless the file is already in the cache.

provenance() of the result records the trust decision, the hash, the source and the licence. FastMACE never ships or redistributes weights.

docs.title: fm.ForceField
docs.text:
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, precision="float32", species=["Na", "Nb", "Cl", "O"],
                   dispersion="d3bj")

The force field the user holds. It keeps the pristine model, the force precision, the species superset and the dispersion record. It builds nothing itself; each plan builds its own execution copy. fm.md and Simulation build one for you when you pass a model.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes model an fm.load result, or a label required The model. A path or URL needs fm.load first, for the trust decision. atoms ASE Atoms, or None None Its species are the default superset. Without it, the first structure used fixes the superset. precision "float32", "float64" "float32" Precision of the force evaluation. Integration is always float64, and the energy is summed in float64. rewrites "auto" or a RewriteConfig "auto" Which exact rewrites the planner may apply. Resolved per plan; see The planner. species symbols or atomic numbers None The species superset: every species the run may contain. May be larger than the structure's (needed for MC). A species the model has no embedding for raises ModelElementError. dispersion None, "d3bj", or an fm.D3 None Add a D3 term to the model. See D3. Refused for PolarMACE.

ff.evaluate(atoms, stress=False) returns (energy, forces, stress) as host copies (eV, eV/Å, eV/Å³), through a one-off plan; the structure must be periodic in all three directions. ff.dispersion_warnings lists warnings of the dispersion record, for example a functional that differs from the training one.

docs.title: fm.D3
docs.text:
A complete D3 dispersion correction with Becke-Johnson damping, computed on the GPU inside the captured step. "D3(BJ)" alone does not identify a correction, so every choice is a field, and the whole record is part of the force field's identity (and of the restart check).

fm.D3(functional="pbe")
fm.D3(functional="custom", s6=1.0, s8=0.8, a1=0.45, a2=5.0)
Option Values / units Default What it does Notes functional "pbe", "r2scan", or any name with explicit s6, s8, a1, a2 required The Becke-Johnson parameter set. Must match the model's training functional; a mismatch is a warning. damping "bj" "bj" Becke-Johnson damping. The only damping. pair_cutoff_bohr bohr, > 0 40.0 Cutoff of the pair terms. 40 bohr = 21.167 Å. As mace_mp and torch-dftd. cn_cutoff_bohr bohr, > 0 40.0 Cutoff of the coordination numbers. three_body bool False The Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term. True is refused: it is not implemented. smoothing "none" "none" Cutoff smoothing. None is applied. precision "float64" "float64" Precision of the coordination-number, energy and virial reductions. The pair terms run in the force precision. autoang Å per bohr 0.52917726 Length unit constant. torch-dftd's value; differs from ASE's Bohr by about 1e-7 relative. autoev eV per hartree 27.21138505 Energy unit constant. torch-dftd's value. s6 > 0 from functional Scale of the C6 term. Give all four of s6, s8, a1, a2 or none. s8 ≥ 0 from functional Scale of the C8 term. a1 ≥ 0 from functional BJ damping parameter. a2 bohr, > 0 from functional BJ damping parameter.

Built-in parameter sets (torch-dftd 0.5.1):

functional s6 s8 a1 a2 pbe 1.0 0.7875 0.4289 4.4407 r2scan 1.0 0.7898 0.4948 5.7308

dispersion="d3bj" expands to fm.D3(functional=...) with the head's training functional from the label table: pbe for the PBE-trained models and heads, r2scan for matpes-r2scan and mh1-r2scan. It raises ValueError when:

  • the training functional already contains dispersion: ωB97M-D3(BJ) (MACE-OFF, MH-1's spice_wB97M) or ωB97M-V (MACE-OMOL-0, MH-1's omol), since D3 would count it twice;
  • the functional is unknown: MACE-POLAR-1, or any model loaded from a path or URL. Pass an explicit fm.D3 then.

The expanded record is printed in the report and recorded in metadata.json. D3 is experimental: the report carries a "D3: experimental: not yet qualified" line.

docs.title: PolarMACE
docs.text:
MACE-POLAR-1 (polar1-s, polar1-m, polar1-l) adds long-range electrostatics with charges from Fukui equilibration. It needs the [polar] extra (graph-longrange 0.4.0). FastMACE replaces the parts of its long-range code that synchronise with the host, so the force call can be captured in a CUDA graph. The k-vectors are a superset fixed when the force field is built; the k-vectors outside the reciprocal-space cutoff of the current cell contribute exactly zero.

  • The stress includes the long-range energy's dependence on the cell. MACE 0.3.16 omits it; FastMACE has no switch back to the uncorrected stress.
  • The structure's total charge is 0 and its spin multiplicity 1.
  • Refused: D3 with PolarMACE; a cell filter in a relaxation (relax at fixed cell); the compiled plain cuEquivariance backend, which returns zero forces for PolarMACE. The hybrid backend is exact.
  • PolarMACE NPT stress has an extra "experimental" report line: it was validated against finite differences on NaCl and NbCl5 3×3×3 only.

docs.title: PolarConfig
docs.text:
fastmace.config.PolarConfig holds PolarMACE's options; it has no effect on other models. The defaults reproduce the released model. The two stabilising options are MACE pull request 1762, open upstream; they change the model, so they are opt-in only. Pass the record to the force field:

from fastmace.config import PolarConfig

model = fm.load("polar1-s")
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, polar=PolarConfig(fukui_regularisation=0.1, dipole_cap=(0.5, 2.0)))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, ff, integrator=..., seed=1)

Not tested

The PR 1762 options are wired through the planner, the gate's float64 reference, simulation.json and resume, and they are part of the force-field identity. No PolarMACE run with them has been validated. The run report carries a "not tested" warning whenever they are set.

A non-default PolarConfig on a model that is not PolarMACE raises ValueError. fm.md and the TOML files take no PolarConfig and run the defaults.

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes fukui_regularisation 0 ≤ R < 1 0.0 Regularised Fukui normalisation: the weights are normalised by s / (s² + (R·Σ|f|)²). 0 is the released model. dipole_cap (onset, ceiling) in e·Å, 0 < onset < ceiling, or None None Smooth cap on each atom's charge dipole. None is the released model. kspace_headroom relative, ≥ 0, or "auto" "auto" How far the cell may deform before the fixed k-vector superset no longer covers the cutoff. "auto": 0.1 with a variable cell, 0 otherwise. A cell beyond it sets an overflow flag.

docs.title: Schedules and profiles
docs.text:
fm.protocols builds temperature schedules. A schedule is independent of the timestep: its segments are in ps. At a given timestep each segment is rounded to whole steps (half up), and the run report records the rounded durations and rates.

anneal = fm.protocols.ramp(0, 1000, ps=20) + fm.protocols.ramp(1000, 250, rate_K_per_ps=-3)
run = fm.md("NaCl.cif", model="mh1", head="matpes_r2scan", schedule=anneal, output="anneal/")
sim.run(schedule=fm.protocols.hold(300, ps=10))

docs.title: Segments
docs.text:
Builder Arguments What it does Notes ramp(start_K, end_K, *, ps=None, rate_K_per_ps=None) K, K; ps or K/ps Linear ramp from start_K to end_K. Exactly one of ps and rate_K_per_ps. The rate is signed and must point from start to end. hold(temperature_K, *, ps) K; ps Constant target for ps. a + b two schedules Concatenate. The second must start where the first ends: a temperature jump raises ValueError.

Temperatures must be finite and at least 0 K; durations positive. A segment that rounds to 0 steps raises ValueError.

Target per step. Step n of a segment uses the target at the step's end point. On a ramp the target changes every step; on a hold it never changes. The target reaches the thermostat before the step; it is not an event.

Steps. fm.md(schedule=...) without steps= runs the whole schedule. steps= beyond what remains raises before any step. The plan's skin is sized for the schedule's highest target, so Simulation.run refuses a schedule above Workload.max_temperature_K.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
fm.protocols.PROFILES holds four named profiles: a schedule with output intervals and, for anneal, an initial relaxation and a quench.

Profile Schedule Output interval (steps) Initial relaxation Quench slow 0 → 400 K in 30 ps, 400 → 0 K in 240 ps 100 none none fast 0 → 400 K in 3 ps, 400 → 0 K in 24 ps 100 none none ultrafast 0 → 400 K in 1 ps, 400 → 0 K in 8 ps 100 none none anneal 0 → 1000 K in 20 ps, 1000 → 250 K in 250 ps (3 K/ps) 20 fixed cell, fmax 0.01 eV/Å, gpu-LBFGS 2 frames per 100 K bin from 500 K, fmax 0.01 eV/Å, gpu-LBFGS, at most 5000 steps

In Python, pass the schedule: fm.md(..., schedule=fm.protocols.PROFILES["anneal"].schedule). In a TOML file for fastmace run, schedule = "anneal" names the profile, or [[schedule]] tables give segments:

[[schedule]]
kind = "ramp"
start_K = 0.0
end_K = 1000.0
ps = 2.0

[[schedule]]
kind = "hold"
temperature_K = 1000.0
ps = 5.0

A ramp table has start_K, end_K and one of ps and rate_K_per_ps; a hold table has temperature_K and ps. Unknown keys raise ValueError.

docs.title: Profile fields
docs.text:
fm.protocols.load_profile(path) reads a profile from a .toml, .yaml or .yml file (YAML through safe_load only). A profile has name, segments and these optional fields:

Option Values / units Default What it does Notes sample_interval steps, int ≥ 1 100 Thermo sample interval. trajectory_interval steps, int ≥ 1 100 Trajectory frame interval. relax_fmax eV/Å, ≥ 0 0.0 Initial fixed-cell relaxation to this fmax. 0 means none. relax_optimizer gpu-LBFGS, gpu-FIRE, ase-LBFGS, ase-BFGS, LBFGS, BFGS gpu-LBFGS Optimiser of the initial relaxation. Bare LBFGS and BFGS mean ASE's. quench table with min_K, bin_K, per_bin, fmax, optimizer, max_steps none Quench frames: per_bin frames per bin_K bin of the target from min_K, relaxed to fmax eV/Å with optimizer, at most max_steps steps. All six keys are required. Each frame is relaxed at its own cell, with the cell fixed. ensemble "NVT", "NPT" "NVT" As fm.md. pressure_GPa GPa none (NVT); 0.0 (NPT) NPT's constant hydrostatic target. Pressure schedules are refused. dispersion "none", "d3bj" "none" As fm.md.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: This page lists what a run writes, file by file and column by column. The how-to is Output, restart and resume.

docs.title: fm.Output
docs.text:
fm.Output(directory, trajectory_every=20, thermo_every=20, restart_every=10_000)
Parameter Values Default What it does directory path (str or os.PathLike) required where the run writes; kept as given, as a string trajectory_every int ≥ 1 or None 20 steps between trajectory frames; None writes no trajectory thermo_every int ≥ 1 20 steps between thermo rows; thermo rows are always written restart_every int ≥ 1 or None 10000 steps between restart points; None writes no restart files on its own

fm.md(output=...) takes a directory or an fm.Output. A directory gets these default intervals. Without output, fm.md writes to ./<structure stem>.fastmace/, or ./fastmace-run/ for an in-memory Atoms. fm.Simulation(output=None) writes nothing.

Intervals count the simulation's steps from 0, across run() calls and resumes. A thermo row and, with trajectory_every, a frame are written at step 0 when the run starts, then at every step that is a multiple of the interval. A restart point is written at every multiple of restart_every.

docs.title: The output directory
docs.text:
File Written by Content thermo.<n>.csv every MD run thermo rows, one chunk per file trajectory.<n>.traj every MD run ASE trajectory frames, one chunk per file restart.npz restart points the complete state at the last restart point simulation.json restart points the inputs a resume needs metadata.json setup, each run(), restart points, stops plan, gate, report, counters, provenance .fastmace-handoff/ a plan that runs in a child process the hand-off between parent and child; deleted on a clean close protocol.json protocol runs stages, pieces, status relaxation.log, relaxed.extxyz protocol runs with [relax] the initial relaxation quench/, quench-NAME/ protocol runs with [quench], fastmace quench the quenched frames

A new run refuses a directory that already holds output chunks (FileExistsError): resume the run or use a new directory.

docs.title: Chunks
docs.text:
The thermo table and the trajectory are written in chunks, n = 0, 1, .... Every restart point closes the current pair of chunk files and opens the next, so a chunk boundary lies exactly at each restart point. Each chunk is complete on its own: every thermo chunk starts with the header, and a chunk without rows or frames still has both files.

from fastmace.io.output import read_frames, read_thermo

header, rows = read_thermo("run/")      # every chunk, in order; rows as strings
frames = read_frames("run/")            # a list of ase.Atoms
ase.io.read("run/trajectory.0.traj", index=":")   # one chunk

docs.title: Thermo table
docs.text:
thermo.<n>.csv is a CSV file with a header line. Energies are per atom.

Column Unit Content step the MD step time_ps ps step × timestep_fs / 1000 phase heating, cooling or hold (the schedule segment), or constant without a schedule target_K K the thermostat target at this step; nan for NVE temperature_K K the kinetic temperature, 2 E_kin / (f k_B) potential_eV_atom eV/atom potential energy kinetic_eV_atom eV/atom kinetic energy total_eV_atom eV/atom potential plus kinetic volume_A3_atom Å³/atom NPT runs only: the cell volume pressure_GPa GPa NPT runs only: the instantaneous pressure, kinetic part included mc_<move>_attempted, mc_<move>_accepted runs with MC only: cumulative counts per move type, as of the last MC block

The degrees of freedom f are 3N − 3 for Langevin NVT with the centre of mass fixed under the "mass_weighted" projection, 3(N − n_fixed) with FixAtoms, and otherwise the integrator's count (3N for ASE's projection, NPT and fixcm off). Simulation.degrees_of_freedom gives the value of a run. A non-finite value stops the run before the row is written.

The NPT columns appear for every integrator with ensemble NPT: LangevinBAOAB, MTK, and Berendsen with a pressure.

docs.title: Trajectory frames
docs.text: trajectory.<n>.traj is an ASE trajectory. Each frame holds the step's cell, positions and momenta, and a single-point calculator with the energy and forces; variable-cell runs add the stress (Voigt, eV/Å³). After an MC swap or transmutation, a frame carries the step's species and masses.

docs.title: Durable writes
docs.text:
restart.npz, simulation.json and metadata.json are written durably and atomically: a temporary file next to the target is written, flushed and fsynced, renamed over the target, and then the directory is fsynced. A crash leaves the old file or the new one, never a short one. The directory fsync is skipped on Windows and on file systems that refuse it.

Thermo rows are flushed after each row; frames are on disk once written. At a restart point, the output queue is drained, the closing chunks and the directory are fsynced, and only then is the restart file written. So a restart never counts rows or frames that are not on disk. Rows and frames after the last restart point are flushed but not fsynced.

Output is asynchronous: a step's values are copied to the host behind the step and written while the next step runs. The files are the same as with synchronous writing.

docs.title: restart.npz
docs.text:
One .npz file (plain arrays and JSON text, no pickles), format version 4. The writer makes the same bytes from the same state.

Entry Content step, engine the step and the writing engine ("fastmace") positions, momenta, velocities, cell, forces, energy the state at the step masses, species, charges the current composition, after any MC change cell_state, stress, p_eps, force_eps variable-cell runs: the barostat state rng_state, noise, noise_next the random generator's state and the batch drawn ahead with its cursor integrator_keys the integrator scheme's own state (NHC, MTK, CSVR) physical total charge, spin, PBC, constraints, fixed atoms integrator class, configuration and thermostat target protocol the schedule and its position plan, plan_revision the plan record, with the edge bucket and neighbour capacity identity, identity_digest the force-field identity output_chunk, output_rows, output_frames the last closed chunk, and the rows and frames in chunks 0 to it mc the attached move set: moves, cycle position, counters, stream seeds, displacement step sizes fastmace_restart the format version

Every restart write is a canonical point: the pipeline is quiesced and the neighbour lists are rebuilt first, so a resumed engine is in the state of the uninterrupted one. Restart writes happen only at committed steps, never inside an MC block.

restart.npz is written:

  • every restart_every steps;
  • by sim.save_restart(directory) (the file name must be restart.npz);
  • at the end of each piece of a protocol run;
  • when an NPT run stops because the cell diverged.

A run that ends between restart points, for example fm.md with steps not a multiple of restart_every, has no restart at its last step. Call sim.save_restart(...) on RunResult.simulation if you need one.

docs.title: simulation.json
docs.text:
Written next to every restart: what the restart format does not hold.

Key Content simulation_record_version 2 model label, path, head, sha256, trust, charge, spin_multiplicity force_field precision, species, rewrites, and dispersion (the D3 record) when there is one integrator class and fields of the fm.integrators record workload the fm.Workload fields output the fm.Output fields; directory is "." when the restart lies in the output directory, so the directory can be moved seed the seed allow_naive_cueq as given planner_options mode, allow_reference, the fallback, gate, runner, engine, neighbour, adaptation and calibration records structure initial numbers, masses, pbc plan_revision the active plan revision restart_points [{step, output_chunk, output_rows, output_frames}] mc the MC record reference_volume_A3 NPT only: the starting volume of the cell-divergence check

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
sim = fm.Simulation.resume("run/", allow_plan_change=False, check="skip")
sim.run()                     # the rest of the schedule, or sim.run(steps=...)

Simulation.resume(directory) needs restart.npz and simulation.json in directory. It:

  1. loads the model again from simulation.json's file, checked against its SHA-256;
  2. compares the force-field identity with the restart's. A different identity raises RestartMismatch; a different MACE or FastMACE version alone warns, and is recorded as a new plan revision and in the report;
  3. plans again. A plan different from the recorded one needs allow_plan_change=True, and makes a new revision. A resume never calibrates;
  4. builds the engine at the restart's positions, cell and composition, then loads the state, edge bucket and neighbour capacity;
  5. checks the output: every chunk up to output_chunk must be present with the recorded numbers of rows and frames, and every later chunk must be deletable. Otherwise it raises RestartMismatch before it touches anything;
  6. deletes the later chunks (rows and frames written after the restart point) and continues with chunk output_chunk + 1. Nothing is rewritten.

check is as in fm.Simulation. The command-line resume, fastmace run --resume RUN_DIR, is for protocol runs only (below).

docs.title: metadata.json
docs.text:
Schema fastmace.metadata/1, minor version 1. A JSON object with these top-level keys, in this order. It holds no NaN, no infinity and no raw random states (generator states appear as SHA-256 hashes).

Key Content schema, schema_minor "fastmace.metadata/1", 1; a record without schema_minor is minor 0 created_utc ISO time of the write code version, git_commit, git_dirty checkpoint path, sha256, head, licence, label, trust model the model block force_field_identity the force-field identity and its digest reference_record the reference record, with at least id plan the active plan: revision, tier, reason, step, description (str(plan)), description_full (plan.describe(full=True)), backend, conv_fusion, rewrites, engine, neighbours, polar, integrator, decisions (key, choice, reason, code, rule), requested, auto_options_off, superset, workload, software, allowances, fallbacks_tried, predicted_memory_bytes, runner ("in-process" or "subprocess"), calibration, adaptation plan_revisions every revision, oldest first, the active one last: revision, tier, step, reason, description, description_full, runner, fallback precision force, integration (always "float64"), tf32 (PyTorch's process-wide matmul TF32 flag when the record was written: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32, also set by torch.set_float32_matmul_precision), tf32_requested (the plan's PrecisionConfig.tf32), float64_energy runtime file_locks ("soft" or "kernel"), file_lock_source, file_lock_switch_late, cuda_driver_cache (see Environment and cache) software versions (Python and packages), kernels, patches, triton, oeq_extension (the OEq build variables for a hybrid plan, else null), treatments hardware gpu, driver, compute_capability; null off CUDA random seed, generators (SHA-256 of each generator state), cursors integrator the integrator parameters schedule the schedule and its position gate status, reason, selfchecks, device, reduced_cell, steps, and the rest of the gate record; status "skipped" without check="gate" counters recaptures, neighbour_lists ({name: {rebuilds, build_time_s, skin_A}}), overflows_redone, mc ({move: {attempted, impossible, accepted}}), tier_switches, segments (the runtime monitor's last 1,000 segments), fallbacks (mid-run fallbacks), engine (the engine's info()) restart_points [{step, output_chunk, output_rows, output_frames}] timing setup_s ({stage: seconds}), setup_total_s, status, steps, loop_s report the run report: text, speed, measured_window, speed_window, setup_s, setup_total_s, licence, gate_status, move_energy_status, mc_energy_precision, reasons, warnings, mc force_field the engine's force field record: backend, dtype, rewrites applied with their decisions and self-check errors, energy_treatment, strain_path, and d3 with D3 subprocess null in-process; for a plan in a child: python, reason, directory, children, calls, persistent, seconds, failed, last

timing.status is running, paused (after a run() call; also after fm.md returns), complete (after sim.close()), non-finite, cell-diverged or fallback-failed. The fastmace.ase integrators add an ase block.

docs.title: RunResult
docs.text:
fm.md returns a frozen RunResult:

Field Type Content summary str the one-screen run report plan Plan the plan the run used gate gate record the gate status and results simulation fm.Simulation the simulation, with its output flushed; it can run on (run) or write a restart (save_restart) metadata dict metadata.json as written at the end of the run output str the output directory

docs.title: Protocol runs
docs.text:
fastmace run with [relax], [quench] or --steps writes, besides the files above:

File Content protocol.json the protocol record (below) relaxation.log the initial relaxation's optimizer log relaxed.extxyz the relaxed starting structure quench/ the quench (below)

protocol.json keys: protocol_record_version (1), source, structure, repeat, atoms, timestep_fs, relax and relaxation (settings and summary), quench and quench_result, mc, min_mc_temperature_K, md_steps (the run's MD steps for a run without a schedule, so that --resume continues to it; null with a schedule), dispersion, pieces (each first_step, last_step, wall_s, counters), counters (the sums of neighbour_rebuilds, d3_builds, d3_rebuilds, d3_build_s), and status:

status Meaning --resume relax the relaxation is running no md the MD is running or paused continues quench the quench is running continues complete done reports it is complete relaxation not converged the relaxation stopped no cell diverged an NPT piece stopped; stop holds the reason no

docs.title: Quench directory
docs.text:
quench/ (or quench-NAME/ from fastmace quench --into NAME):

File Content settings.json the resolved settings, written first; an interrupted quench continues only with them captured.traj the picked MD frames quenched.traj their minima quench.csv one row per frame, written after each frame quench.json settings and summary, written last; a quench with it is complete

quench.csv columns: phase, bin, frame, step, time_ps, target_K, md_temperature_K, md_potential_eV_atom, singlepoint_eV_atom, quenched_eV_atom, converged, optimizer_steps, seconds, fmax_eV_A, volume_A3_atom.

docs.title: fastmace relax
docs.text:
fastmace relax writes three files, by default <stem>.relaxed.extxyz, <stem>.relaxed.json and <stem>.relaxed.log (the --output name with .json and .log).

.json key Content structure, repeat, atoms the input model, head, precision, output the model and the output file optimizer the optimizer that ran fixed_cell false with --cell-filter fmax_target_eV_A, max_steps the limits converged, steps, seconds the result initial_eV_atom, energy_eV_atom energy per atom before and after fmax_eV_A the largest force at the end energies_eV, fmax_history_eV_A, neighbour_rebuilds, recaptures gpu-* optimizers only cell_A, volume_A3, stress_GPa, scalar_pressure_GPa with --cell-filter only

A relaxation Simulation in Python writes no output files and no restart.

docs.title: Planner, gate and fallback
docs.text:
These are the planner's inputs: the keyword arguments of fm.Simulation that choose the tier and the checks, the fm.Workload record, and five configuration records:

  • FallbackConfig: what happens when a build, compile, capture, self-check or gate fails;
  • GateConfig: where the gate's float64 references may run;
  • RunnerConfig: the child process that runs a plan this process cannot;
  • AdaptationConfig: runtime tier switches;
  • CalibrationConfig: the optional backend measurement before a run.

The planner guide explains how to read a plan. This page lists every option. Engine and neighbour-list options are on Engine and neighbour list.

import fastmace as fm
from fastmace.config import AdaptationConfig, FallbackConfig, GateConfig, RunnerConfig

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
sim = fm.Simulation(
    atoms, model,
    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(temperature_K=600, friction_per_fs=0.02),
    seed=1,
    workload=fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=900),
    check="gate",
    fallback=FallbackConfig(fallback="refuse"),
    gate=GateConfig(cpu_float64_time_limit_s=600),
    runner=RunnerConfig(stall_timeout_s=3600),
    adaptation=AdaptationConfig(adapt="off"),
)
print(sim.plan)        # tier, backend, precision and the decisions that matter
print(sim.gate)        # the gate record

fm.Workload is in the fm namespace. The other records are imported from fastmace.config. Every record is frozen and checks its values when you build it (ValueError). Options the planner cannot honour raise PlanRefused with every reason when the Simulation is built, before anything runs.

fm.md takes mode=, allow_reference=, check=, seed=, fallback=, gate=, runner=, engine= and neighbours= and passes them on unchanged. It builds the Workload from its own arguments (the highest target temperature of the schedule, and the declared MC moves), and takes calibrate=True instead of a CalibrationConfig. It has no adaptation= or allow_naive_cueq=; use fm.Simulation for those.

The options are recorded in simulation.json next to the restart. Simulation.resume plans with the same options.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
A tier is the way the engine executes each step. Every tier runs FastMACE's own integrators, noise, output and restart, so a trajectory has the same physics on every tier.

Tier What runs When the planner picks it graph The compiled model, with each stage of a step recorded once as a CUDA graph and replayed. Edges are padded to buckets so that one graph fits many steps. Fastest. The default for MD and relaxations. On a CPU device the same engine runs its stages without graphs. compiled The compiled model without CUDA graphs. Exact edge counts; a new edge count does not compile again. Each step is launched from the host. Without mode=, when padded edges would change this model's energies (padding is not exact). With mode="compiled". As the target of a runtime switch. eager The graph tier's backend, rewrites and precision, with no compilation and no CUDA graphs. Exact edge counts. With mode="eager". When the installed MACE cannot capture this model's readout (some multi-head models), even for mode="graph". As a fallback candidate. reference MACE's own calculator through the versioned reference record: stock uncompiled cuEquivariance model, no rewrites, no padding, MACE's own neighbour list. Slowest. With mode="reference". As the last fallback candidate, if it fits on the device and reference_last=True.

Host callbacks (Workload.host_callbacks_every) keep the graph tier, with a host synchronisation at each callback: the compiled tier measured 1.3–4.7× slower with a callback every 1–10 steps (MH-1, hybrid float32, NaCl and NbCl5 on an RTX 5060 Ti).

docs.title: Backends
docs.text:
Backend What it is When EngineConfig.backend="auto" picks it hybrid cuEquivariance for the symmetric contraction and linear layers, OpenEquivariance kernels for the convolutions (message passing). Most rewrites need it. Float32 by default. OpenEquivariance can build, the device is CUDA, MACE was not imported before FastMACE prepared the OpenEquivariance runtime, and the process has not compiled a plain cuEq model. cueq Plain cuEquivariance throughout, with its fused convolution unless the plan is reproducible. Every other case, with the reason in the plan. reproducible=True always uses it.

One process can hold compiled models of only one of the two backends, because MACE's compile setting is process-wide. A plan of the other backend runs in a child process through the subprocess runner (RunnerConfig). Calibration measures the two backends against each other on your structure.

docs.title: Simulation keyword arguments
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes mode None, "graph", "compiled", "eager", "reference" None: the graph tier, or the compiled tier when padding is not exact for the model Asks for a tier. An explicit "graph" with inexact padding is refused. An explicit mode also stops runtime tier switches. check "skip", "gate", "allow_unavailable" "skip" Whether the gate runs before the first step. "gate": a failed gate goes to the fallback, or raises GateFailed; a gate whose reference cannot run raises GateUnavailable. "allow_unavailable": as "gate", but an unavailable reference is recorded and the run goes on. MC runs always run the move-energy part of the gate, whatever check is. The record is sim.gate. allow_reference True, False False Recorded in the plan. It does not lift any refusal and is not needed for mode="reference". allow_naive_cueq True, False False Accepts cuEquivariance's slow fallback kernels when its fused kernels (cuequivariance_ops_torch) do not load. Without it, such a plan is refused with the import error. Recorded. seed int required The seed of the integrator's noise. MC streams derive their own seeds from it. fm.md(seed=None) draws a seed and records it in metadata.json. workload fm.Workload or None None: fm.Workload(max_temperature_K=<integrator's temperature_K>); for a relaxation max_temperature_K=0 What the run will do; see fm.Workload. An integrator without a temperature (NVE) needs an explicit workload. A starting target above max_temperature_K is refused. engine EngineConfig or None None: the default planner's Engine options; see Engine and neighbour list. A record you pass replaces the default as a whole. neighbours NeighbourConfig or None None: the default planner's Neighbour-list options; see Engine and neighbour list. fallback FallbackConfig or None None: FallbackConfig() See FallbackConfig. gate GateConfig or None None: GateConfig() See GateConfig. The record is sim.gate_config; the result is sim.gate. runner RunnerConfig or None None: RunnerConfig() See RunnerConfig. adaptation AdaptationConfig or None None: AdaptationConfig() See AdaptationConfig. calibration CalibrationConfig or None None: CalibrationConfig() See CalibrationConfig.

docs.title: fm.Workload
docs.text:
The workload holds the facts about the run that no other object knows. Periodicity and constraints come from the Atoms, the ensemble from the integrator, and the precision and species superset from the ForceField.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes max_temperature_K float ≥ 0, K required (Simulation fills it from the integrator) The highest thermostat target of the run. Simulation.run refuses a schedule that goes above it. For MC and species-change runs it sizes the skin and the pair buffers; for plain MD it is recorded. species_changes True, False False Declares that species will change (swaps, transmutations, species events). Required for "swap" and "transmute" moves. Keeps the graph tier and builds species-dependent tables for the whole superset. Makes the planner size the skin and buffers from the workload. atom_count_changes True, False False Declares that atoms will be added or removed. Accepted by the record and refused by the planner: not supported in 1.0. min_mc_temperature_K float > 0, K, or None None The lowest MC target temperature. Sets the move-energy gate's limit, 0.01 k_B T_min. Required when mc_moves is not empty. Attaching MC moves while the target temperature is below it is refused. host_callbacks_every int > 0 or None None Declares that user Python runs every n steps. Keeps the graph tier, with a host synchronisation at each callback. The ASE front end sets it from its attached observers. needs_per_atom set of names, for example {"energies", "charges"} empty Per-atom outputs the run needs. Recorded in the plan. mc_moves tuple of "swap", "transmute", "displace" () The MC move types the run will attach through Simulation.run(mc=...). Attaching a move type not declared here is refused. Declaring moves turns on the move-energy gate. reproducible True, False False Asks for bitwise reproducible trajectories on the same hardware, driver, software, model, plan, seeds and restart cadence. Qualified only for plain cuEq with the unfused convolution, the MH-1 architecture, the graph or eager tier and the checked cuequivariance_ops version; everything else is refused with the reason. The process is set to deterministic mode before CUDA starts; if CUDA already started, the plan runs in a child process. mc_energy_precision "auto", "float32", "float64" "auto": the force precision if the move-energy gate passes, else float64 The precision of MC trial energies. MD forces keep their own precision. "float32" with float64 forces is refused. max_displacement_A float > 0, Å, or None None The largest displacement any Displace move of the run may use, adaptive steps included. Required when "displace" is in mc_moves. Adds 2 × this value to the skin. A Displace with a larger delta_A is refused.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
The gate checks the planned engine on your structure before the first step. It is opt-in: check="gate".

  1. Copies. The gate makes 2 copies of the structure, each rattled by 0.05 Å. For a variable-cell integrator it adds 2 copies strained by up to ±2 % and then rattled.
  2. References. On each copy it evaluates MACE's own model in float64 (the reference) and in float32 with the energy summed in float64 (the yardstick). These run before the production engine is built, or in a child process.
  3. Production. It evaluates each copy through the planned engine, in the mode it will run (captured graphs on the graph tier), and restores the engine's state bit for bit afterwards.
  4. Rule. For energy per atom, forces and stress, the production error against the float64 reference, maximised over all copies, must be at most 2 × the yardstick's error, or at most the floor: 0.01 meV/atom, 1×10⁻⁵ eV/Å (largest force component), 1×10⁻⁷ eV/Å³ (largest stress component; 5×10⁻⁷ eV/Å³ for PolarMACE). Any NaN or infinity fails. NVT plans have no stress path and record "stress: not in plan".

Move energies. A run with MC moves always runs the move-energy part, whatever check is. It samples trial moves (2 swaps, 1 transmutation, 4 displacements per declared type) and requires every |ΔE_production − ΔE_reference| ≤ 0.01 k_B T_min, which keeps acceptance probabilities within about 1 %. With mc_energy_precision="auto", a failure switches the MC energies to float64.

Resources. If the float64 reference runs out of GPU memory, the gate tries, in order: the CPU in float64 on the full cell (if its estimated time is within cpu_float64_time_limit_s and its memory fits); a reduced cell on the GPU; the reduced cell on the CPU. A pass on a reduced cell is recorded as passed-reduced. A reference that fails for any reason other than memory makes the gate unavailable at once.

docs.title: GateConfig
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes cpu_float64_time_limit_s float ≥ 0, s 300.0 After a GPU out-of-memory, the CPU float64 reference is tried only if its estimated time is within this limit. 0 never tries the CPU. The estimate comes from timing two small boxes cut from your structure, in the same run. reduced_cell "auto", "off" "auto": the largest supercell of the same primitive cell, smaller than the production cell, whose every height is at least reduced_cell_min_height_cutoffs × the cutoff Allows the reference on a reduced cell when the full cell does not fit. "off": never; the gate is unavailable instead. On a reduced cell the production path is evaluated by a separate uncaptured force field with the same rewrites and precision, and the captured replay is checked against it on the full cell. reduced_cell_min_height_cutoffs float ≥ 1 2.0 The reduced cell's smallest height, in cutoffs. Below 1 a periodic image would sit inside the cutoff.

docs.title: FallbackConfig
docs.text:
The fallback acts when something fails before the first step: the build, compilation, the first CUDA graph capture, a rewrite self-check, or the gate. With fallback="auto" it searches for the closest plan that passes:

  1. Diagnose. It runs the failing check again on the eager tier with the same rewrites. If eager passes, the CUDA graphs or compilation were the problem and the tier changes. If not, it narrows down the rewrite set (turning rewrites off in groups, respecting their dependencies), each try checked with a reduced gate: one rattled copy, the failing quantity only.
  2. Budget. At most diagnosis_budget reduced-gate runs. Each candidate that would become active also gets a full gate run, counted apart.
  3. Terminal sequence. When the budget is spent: the same tier with every rewrite off; eager with every rewrite off; the reference tier if it fits and reference_last=True.
  4. Nothing passes. FallbackExhausted with every candidate tried.

Candidates are built from the pristine model, never by undoing rewrites in place. A candidate becomes active only after it passed. The physics (integrator, force precision, structure) never changes. Every candidate is listed in sim.plan.fallbacks and in metadata.json. With check="skip" the fallback still validates its candidate against float64 references; the gate record stays skipped.

During run(), a capture error at a re-capture or a compile error on the compiled tier starts the same search from the last committed restart point. A second such failure before the next restart point stops the run with FallbackExhausted. Out-of-memory errors, non-finite values, refusals and process constraints never start the fallback.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes fallback "auto", "refuse" "auto": search for a validated slower plan and record it What a failure does. "refuse" raises the original error, with the record. No effect on a run where nothing fails. diagnosis_budget int > 0 64 The most reduced-gate runs of one fallback. Full gate runs (one per candidate that would become active) are not counted. reference_last True, False True Allows the reference tier as the last candidate, if it fits on the plan's device: the gate's reference ran there on the full cell, or a trial evaluation runs. False ends the search with FallbackExhausted instead.

docs.title: RunnerConfig
docs.text:
Some plans cannot run in the current process:

  • a compiled model of the other backend after this process compiled one;
  • reproducible=True after CUDA was started in this process, or a plan that is not reproducible in a process that was made reproducible.

The planner then marks the plan runner="subprocess". The Simulation builds nothing in this process; a child process plans, gates and builds, and the two hand the state over through restart files in <output>/.fastmace-handoff/ (or the cache's handoff/ without output). sim.plan, sim.gate, sim.report and metadata.json reflect the child. The runner is also used for calibration.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes python path or None None: this process's sys.executable The child's Python interpreter. The child imports the same FastMACE as the parent. environment mapping or (name, value) pairs of strings () Environment variables set in the child, over the inherited ones. A mapping is stored as sorted pairs. inherit_environment True, False True The child starts from the parent's environment. False: from environment alone. timeout_s float > 0, s, or None None: no limit The total time limit of one child run. A child past it is killed; SubprocessRunnerError is raised. stall_timeout_s float > 0, s 1800.0 A child with no progress (no committed step, read from its heartbeat file) for this long is killed. The heartbeat changes when the child's phase or committed step changes. One long setup phase (compilation, the gate's reference) counts as no progress, so keep this above your longest setup phase. persistent True, False True One child serves every run() of the Simulation and keeps its compiled engine. False: a fresh child for each run(), resuming from the last hand-off. Windows always uses fresh children. Both write the same restart points.

docs.title: AdaptationConfig
docs.text:
During a run the monitor reads the engine's counters at each restart point and at the end of each run(): re-captures and their time, overflows redone, neighbour-list rebuilds. These are in metadata.json and the report's runtime line.

The implemented adaptation is one switch from the graph tier to the compiled tier. It happens when both:

  • the run has made more re-captures than EngineConfig.recapture_budget;
  • re-capturing took more than recapture_time_fraction of the wall time since the start (or the last switch).

The switch is made at the next committed step outside an MC block, which becomes a restart point. The new plan has the same backend, rewrites, precision and physics; it is a new plan revision, validated before it becomes active. A resume rebuilds the same revision. A run that never reaches the trigger is unchanged.

There is no switch with reproducible=True, with an explicit mode=, for a relaxation, or on any tier other than graph.

Refused values. The record can hold more options than are implemented. Simulation refuses, with PlanRefused (code adaptation-unsupported), any record where:

  • trigger is "recapture-budget";
  • skin_replan is True;
  • max_switches is None or above 1;
  • switch_back_after is not None;
  • min_points_between is not None;
  • reproducible is True.

This holds even with adapt="off". To turn adaptation off, change only adapt (or trigger="none", or max_switches=0).

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes adapt "auto", "off" "auto": switch as described above Whether the monitor may switch tiers. "off": the monitor still records. trigger "recapture-time", "none"; "recapture-budget" is refused "recapture-time" What fires a switch. "recapture-time": budget exceeded and re-capture time above recapture_time_fraction. "none": no switch. recapture_time_fraction float, > 0 and < 1 0.2 The share of wall time spent re-capturing above which an exceeded budget switches tiers. Measured in the run, so it holds on any GPU. skin_replan False only False Reserved: re-plan the skin from the measured rebuild rate. True is refused. max_switches 0, 1 1 The most tier switches one run may make. A resume counts the switches already in its plan history. 0 disables switches. None (no limit) and values above 1 are refused. switch_back_after None only None: switches are one way Reserved: go back to the graph tier after this many quiet segments. Any other value is refused. min_points_between None only None Reserved: a minimum number of restart points between two switches. Any other value is refused. reproducible False only False Reserved: allow switches under reproducible=True. True is refused.

docs.title: CalibrationConfig
docs.text:
Calibration is off by default. With calibrate=True the run first measures the two backends on your structure, when the rules rank them equal: the planner chose hybrid because OpenEquivariance builds, and plain cuEq is also allowed. It does nothing when you set EngineConfig.backend, for reproducible runs, for the reference tier, or when the plan runs in a child process.

Each measurement is a fresh child process that builds the plan, runs 50 warm-up steps, then times steps steps. The blocks alternate hybrid, cuEq, hybrid, cuEq (2 pairs). Plain cuEq replaces hybrid only when it is faster by more than margin in every pair. The four child builds are the cost; the report shows it as setup: calibration. Nothing is stored or reused by another run. The chosen backend is recorded, so a resume plans the same one; a resume never calibrates.

calibrate=True is refused (code calibration-workload) for relaxations and for runs with MC moves: their step time is not a steady MD step. fm.md(calibrate=True) sets it.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Notes calibrate True, False False Measures the backends before the run. MD runs only. steps int ≥ 1 50 Timed steps per block, after the warm-up. margin float, > 0 and < 1 0.05 How much faster plain cuEq must be, in every pair, to replace hybrid. The default is above the cross-process timing noise of about 3 %. choose True only True The measurement may change the backend. False (measure and record only) is not implemented: Simulation refuses it with code calibration-unsupported, even with calibrate=False.

docs.title: When to change these
docs.text:
• Debugging a failure. Pass mode="eager": same backend, rewrites and precision, no compilation and no graphs, so a traceback points at the failing operation. fallback=FallbackConfig(fallback="refuse") raises the original error instead of searching for another plan.
  • New model or new structure. Run once with check="gate". If the gate is unavailable on a large cell and you accept running without it, use check="allow_unavailable". Raise cpu_float64_time_limit_s if the CPU reference is declined for time and you can wait.
  • Gate is slow. The gate's float64 reference dominates setup on large cells. It is a one-off cost per run; leave check="skip" for production runs of a validated model and structure.
  • MC runs. Declare every move type in Workload.mc_moves, with min_mc_temperature_K and, for displacements, max_displacement_A. Set max_temperature_K to the highest target of the whole run, not of the first segment.
  • Hot or changing structures. If re-captures are frequent, the graph tier loses its advantage. Leave adaptation at its default, so the run can move to the compiled tier, or plan mode="compiled" yourself.
  • Long setups in a child process. A child that compiles and runs the gate on a large cell can take a long time before its first step. Raise stall_timeout_s if it is killed during setup, and set timeout_s on shared machines so that a stuck child cannot hold the GPU.
  • Persistent runner. Keep persistent=True: one child keeps its compiled engine across run() calls. Use False only to get a fresh process per run(), for example to release GPU memory between calls.
  • Comparing backends on one structure. Use calibrate=True (or fm.md(calibrate=True)) for an MD run. It costs four extra builds, so use it for long runs only.

docs.title: Rewrites and precision options
docs.text: This page lists every field of RewriteConfig and PrecisionConfig, what "auto" resolves to, and the limits of each option. For the history of the screens behind these defaults (measurements, rejected ideas) see Rewrite screens. For how the planner works in general see The planner.

docs.title: What a rewrite is
docs.text:
A rewrite replaces part of the MACE model with code that computes the same function faster: weights folded together, sums reordered, several kernels fused into one, or a stock module replaced by a custom kernel. The model's weights and its physics do not change. Each rewrite is a record in the rewrite registry (fastmace/rewrites/). The record names the models it fits, the MACE source it was written against (checked by hash), the records it needs and its exactness class.

Every rewrite runs a self-check when it is applied: the rewritten module is compared with the original module on random inputs. The relative error must be at most 1e-4 in float32 and 1e-10 in float64. A failed self-check turns the rewrite off, together with every rewrite that needs it, and the plan is built again from the unrewritten model.

docs.title: Toggle values
docs.text:
Most fields take one of three values:

  • "auto" (the default): the planner decides, by a fixed rule per field, from the backend, the force precision, the model and whether the plan is reproducible. The rule and the outcome are recorded in the plan.
  • "on": you ask for the rewrite. If the model, the backend or the plan cannot take it, planning stops with PlanRefused, which lists every reason. An "on" is never silently turned off.
  • "off": the rewrite is not applied. Rewrites that need it are off too.

A few fields are plain booleans or have their own values; their rows say so.

docs.title: Exactness classes
docs.text:
Each registry record has one of these classes. The tables below give the class of each option.

Class Meaning exact The same arithmetic in the same order as the original. Results are bit-for-bit identical, except where a kernel sums with atomic additions, whose order can change from run to run. rounding The same mathematical function, computed in a different order or grouping (reassociated sums, folded or factored weights, different matrix-product grouping). Results differ from the original only by floating-point rounding. Most rewrites are of this class. certified An approximation (for example a fitted table) whose error is measured when the plan is built, on the plan's own model, species and range, against a float64 evaluation of the same weights. The error must be at most the rounding error of the computation it replaces, for the values and their first derivatives. The self-check holds this certificate; a ratio above 1 fails it and turns the rewrite off. approximate Not exact to rounding. Never on under "auto". No current option is of this class.

"Deterministic" in the tables means bitwise repeatable from run to run on the same GPU. A reproducible plan (fm.Workload(reproducible=True)) refuses any rewrite that is not deterministic.

docs.title: Short names
docs.text:
• cuEq: NVIDIA cuEquivariance, the tensor-product library MACE uses.
  • OEq: OpenEquivariance, the second tensor-product library of the hybrid backend. "Hybrid" means cuEq for most of the model and OEq for the convolution.
  • Plain cuEq: the cuEq backend without OEq.
  • Inductor: PyTorch's compiler (torch.compile).
  • MH-1 class: models whose interaction blocks are MACE's non-linear residual blocks and that apply the radial cutoff inside the interaction. MACE-MH-1 is the main one; OMOL-0 and POLAR-1 also have these blocks.
  • Generic MACE family: MACE-MP-0, MPA-0, OMAT-0 and MatPES, whose interactions are MP-0's residual block or the density-normalised block. MACE-OFF has a plain first interaction and is not in this family, but takes the generic variants of some rewrites.

docs.title: See which rewrites are on
docs.text:
print(sim.plan)                        # rewrites on, and the ones off with a short reason
print(sim.plan.describe(full=True))    # every decision with its rule and reason
sim.plan.decision("RewriteConfig.fold_cutoff")   # (item, choice, reason)
sim.plan.overrides()                   # the options you set explicitly

The resolved values are also in sim.plan.rewrites and sim.plan.precision, in the run report and in metadata.json.

docs.title: Set an option
docs.text:
RewriteConfig is not in the top-level fastmace namespace. Import it from fastmace.config and pass it to the force field:

import fastmace as fm
from fastmace.config import RewriteConfig

model = fm.load("mh1", head="matpes_r2scan")
ff = fm.ForceField(model, atoms, precision="float32",
                   rewrites=RewriteConfig(radial_tables="off", direct_node_feats="on"))
sim = fm.Simulation(atoms, ff, seed=1,
                    integrator=fm.integrators.Langevin(timestep_fs=1.0, temperature_K=600,
                                                       friction_per_fs=0.002))
print(sim.plan.decision("RewriteConfig.radial_tables"))

Fields you leave out stay at "auto". rewrites="auto" is the same as RewriteConfig(). fm.md always uses rewrites="auto".

docs.title: How "auto" chains
docs.text:
Many rewrites build on another one. Under "auto" a rewrite is on only when the rewrites it needs are on, so turning one off also turns off what is built on it. The main chains are:

  • factor_species → fold_cutoff → density_first, joint_radial_input, reassociate_first, fused_folded_backward, streaming_conv, radial_tables;
  • streaming_conv + fused_folded_backward → chunked_conv_backward → fused_folded_forward; radial_tables + chunked_conv_backward → w_tables, wprime_backward;
  • block_linear → grouped_linear, merged_residual → gated_rows → segment_gemm; block_linear → grouped_launch, fold_readout_tail; block_linear + species_tables → fold_product_linear.

factor_species and block_linear are on under "auto" only with the hybrid backend, so on plain cuEq most rewrites are off. Setting fold_cutoff="off" also turns off the generic variants of reassociate_first, streaming_conv and fused_folded_backward, because the planner checks fold_cutoff before it checks which variant fits the model.

The reference tier (Simulation(mode="reference")) runs MACE's own calculator with every rewrite off. The eager and compiled tiers keep the graph plan's rewrites.

docs.title: Radial network
docs.text:
The radial network turns each edge length into the weights of that edge's tensor product. In the MH-1 class it also reads the species of both atoms.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Exactness / limits factor_species auto, on, off On with the hybrid backend where the model takes it (MH-1 class). Splits the radial network's first layer into a species part and a distance part, so the species part is computed once per species instead of once per edge. rounding, deterministic. Needs a factored (MH-1-class) interaction. fold_cutoff auto, on, off On with factor_species where the model takes it. Folds the cutoff function into the last radial layer instead of multiplying the edge weights by it afterwards. rounding, deterministic. Needs factor_species and a model that applies its cutoff in the interaction (apply_cutoff=False). joint_radial_input auto, on, off On with fold_cutoff. Runs one first layer for both radial networks of an interaction (the tensor-product weights and the edge density) instead of two. rounding, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff. fused_folded_backward auto, on, off On with fold_cutoff (MH-1 class); for the generic MACE family its generic variant is on with the hybrid backend. Computes the input gradient of the folded last radial layer in one Triton kernel. rounding, deterministic. folded_backward_tiles auto, on, off On with fused_folded_backward (MH-1 class). Picks 128-row tiles for that gradient kernel where 64-row tiles would give 2 to 8 waves over the GPU's multiprocessors. A rule from the GPU's size, not a per-GPU table. exact (bitwise the same), deterministic. Needs fused_folded_backward. fused_radial_hidden auto, on, off Off. Only "on" enables it. Runs the radial network's hidden block as one pair of Triton kernels. rounding, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff. No measured gain. radial_tables auto, on, off On with fold_cutoff (MH-1 class) in float32 and float64 plans that are not reproducible. Replaces the radial chain (distance → edge weights and edge density) with per-species-pair piecewise Chebyshev tables, fitted when the plan is built. One Triton kernel evaluates them; the backward recomputes. certified, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff. A failed certificate turns it off. Float64 tables are held to float64 rounding. "on" is refused in reproducible float64 plans. w_tables auto, on, off On only in float64 MH-1 plans that are not reproducible, on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti or an NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation, with at most 3 species. Off elsewhere. Builds the second interaction's per-edge weights straight from the radial tables (one table per piece already multiplied by the last layer), and their distance gradient without a separate product. rounding, not deterministic. Needs radial_tables and chunked_conv_backward. "on" needs float64 outside reproducible plans. The tables grow with the square of the species count; above 2 GiB per interaction the rewrite does not apply. wprime_backward auto, on, off On for MH-1 checkpoints in float32 plans that are not reproducible, on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti or an NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation (matched by exact name). Off on every other GPU, for other models, in float64 and in reproducible plans. Computes the second interaction's distance gradient inside the streaming convolution's backward: each edge's weight gradient is multiplied with the derivative of its per-edge weights, read from per-piece tables. The weight gradient is never stored, and the folded layer's input gradient and the radial table's backward are not needed. rounding, not deterministic. Needs radial_tables and chunked_conv_backward. "on" needs float32 outside reproducible plans; with it, any GPU takes it. MD step 6–19 % faster on the listed GPUs (docs/validation/opt9-T03.md).

docs.title: Density and first interaction
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Exactness / limits density_first auto, on, off On with fold_cutoff (MH-1 class). Divides by the edge density before the bias-free linear_1 instead of after it. rounding, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff. reassociate_first auto, on, off On with the hybrid backend where the first interaction's inputs depend only on species: the MH-1 variant needs fold_cutoff; the generic variant serves the generic MACE family and MACE-OFF. Off on plain cuEq. Sums the first interaction per receiver and per sender species before its last radial layer, so the layer runs on far fewer rows. rounding, deterministic. "on" on plain cuEq is refused. Built for the species superset. segmented_first_sum auto, on, off On with reassociate_first and receiver-sorted edges. Computes that per-species sum with a run-segmented Triton kernel over receiver-sorted edges. exact, not deterministic (atomic additions). Needs reassociate_first and NeighbourConfig.sort_receivers="on". species_skip auto, on, off On with the graph engine on either backend where the model takes it (generic MACE family, MACE-OFF). Restricts the element-dependent skip connection to the species of the structure (or the declared superset). exact, deterministic.

docs.title: Convolution (OEq streaming)
docs.text:
The convolution combines each edge's weights with its sender's features and sums the messages per receiver.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Exactness / limits streaming_conv auto, on, off On with the hybrid backend and receiver-sorted edges, where the model takes it: the MH-1 variant needs fold_cutoff; the generic variant serves the generic MACE family and MACE-OFF. Runs the convolution with OEq's receiver-streaming kernels: messages are summed per receiver as they are produced, without a per-edge message tensor. exact, not deterministic. Needs the hybrid backend and NeighbourConfig.sort_receivers="on": on unsorted edges these kernels give wrong results while every self-check passes, so the planner refuses that combination. chunked_conv_backward auto, on, off On with streaming_conv and fused_folded_backward (MH-1 class). Runs the streaming backward in edge chunks sized to the GPU's L2 cache. Each chunk's weight gradient goes straight into the folded layer's input gradient, so the full per-edge weight gradient is never written to device memory. Cells whose weights fit in four L2 caches run unchunked inside the same kernel. exact, not deterministic. Needs streaming_conv and fused_folded_backward. fused_folded_forward auto, on, off On for MH-1 checkpoints (by label, or by SHA-256 and head) in float32 plans that are not reproducible. Off for other models, in float64 and in reproducible plans. Fuses the folded last radial layer into the streaming forward: one kernel builds the per-edge weights and the message, and stores the weights for the chunked backward. exact (the same float32 sums in the same order), not deterministic. Needs chunked_conv_backward. "on" needs float32; with it, any float32 model with chunked_conv_backward takes it. direct_node_feats auto, on, off Off. Only "on" enables it. In the folded MH-1 forward, skips the join of node features and attributes that MACE builds for LAMMPS, whose strided slices the streaming convolution had to copy. exact, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff. folded_constants auto, on, off Off. Only "on" enables it. Builds the folded last radial layer's weight-and-bias matrix and its halves once, not on every force call. exact, deterministic. Needs fold_cutoff.

docs.title: Linear layers
docs.text:
MACE's equivariant linear layers act per angular momentum l. cuEq runs each as one generic kernel; these rewrites run them as ordinary matrix products.

Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Exactness / limits block_linear auto, on, off On with the hybrid backend. Runs each cuEq Linear as one matrix product per l, with the weights extracted once. rounding, deterministic. grouped_linear auto, on, off On with block_linear. Puts input segments of the same irrep that feed one output segment into a single product. rounding, deterministic. Needs block_linear. merged_residual auto, on, off On with block_linear. Runs linear_1 and the residual linear as one product per output segment. rounding, deterministic. Needs block_linear and density_first; does nothing on models without density_first. gated_rows auto, on, off On with merged_residual (MH-1 class). Runs the residual products, the gate and linear_2 of MH-1-class interactions on per-segment rows, without the joins and copies between them. exact, deterministic. Needs block_linear and merged_residual. segment_gemm auto, on, off On with gated_rows in float32 plans that are not reproducible. Writes linear_2's products straight into its joined output with a gathered-row Triton matrix product, where a shared shape rule picks it. rounding, deterministic. Needs gated_rows. The kernel is float32. gate_epilogue auto, on, off Off. Only "on" enables it. Runs the gate's backward inside linear_2's input-gradient matrix product in MH-1-class chains: one atom-tiled Triton kernel per gated segment stores the gated rows' gradient and sums the gates' gradient in registers, where the shape rule picks Triton. rounding, deterministic. Needs segment_gemm and float32. Conflicts with tf32x3_gemms. grouped_launch auto, on, off On with block_linear for the generic MACE family in float32 plans that are not reproducible. Off for other families. Runs a block linear's small per-l products (too few row tiles to fill the GPU, by the shared shape rule) in one Triton launch. rounding, deterministic. Needs block_linear. Conflicts with tf32x3_gemms. inplace_block_linear False, True (bool) False. Runs the per-l products as in-place strided-batched products. True is refused: it was slower and is not carried over.

docs.title: Species tables and folding
docs.text: Option Values Default (auto means) What it does Exactness / limits species_tables auto, on, off On where the model takes it, in float32 and float64 plans that are not reproducible, on either backend. Replaces atom-level products that depend only on the species (embeddings, the first interaction's skip_tp and linear_up) with per-species tables, gathered each step. rounding, deterministic (but not bitwise equal to the per-atom products on the GPU). Needs ScaleShiftMACE, a factored first interaction with species-only inputs, and no charge/spin embedding (so not OMOL-0). Tables are built for the species superset. species_residual auto, on, off Off unless set to "on" (opt-in; not a default yet). With species_tables, the first interaction's residual product linear_res(linear_up(embedding)) depends only on the species, so it becomes per-species rows added to linear_1's products; the merged product loses that half of its inputs and of its backward. Measured 0.4–0.8 % faster on the RTX 4000 Ada and 0.2–1 % on the RTX 5060 Ti's large cells (fp32 profile, 29 October 2026). rounding. Needs species_tables and the fold_cutoff interaction forward. fold_readout_tail auto, on, off On with block_linear where the model takes it, in plans that are not reproducible. Folds the last readout's first linear into the last product's linear and skip_tp. rounding, deterministic.
